problem_statement:
## Description
The OpenTitan SPI_HOST IP does not reliably stay electrically idle after reset. With default reset values and before any software configuration, the block may assert external output-enable signals and begin affecting the SPI bus immediately after reset release. In systems where the SPI bus is shared with another controller or external programmer, this can create contention at power-up.

## Expected Behavior
Immediately after reset, and before software explicitly enables SPI_HOST output driving, the external output-enable signals for the SPI clock (SCK), chip-select (CSB), and serial-data (SD) pins must all remain deasserted. The IP should therefore leave its SPI pins in a high-impedance (tri-stated) state by default and have no electrical effect on the bus.

## Actual Behavior
After reset release with default settings, SPI_HOST is not guaranteed to keep all of its external drivers disabled. Its output-enable path can become active before software has enabled bus driving, so the IP may drive the bus at power-up instead of remaining tri-stated.

## Affected Function
The bug affects the SPI_HOST IP's reset-time external output-enable control for the SCK, CSB, and SD pins.

## Trigger Condition
The problem is triggered when SPI_HOST exits reset with default register values and no software writes have yet been made to enable or configure external bus driving.

resolved_issues.body:
Test for direct host reads has two parts, both initiating back to back reads. First part is with scramble disabled while second part is with scramble enabled. Second part of test is sometimes failing in small regression (i.e. for fixed seed 1 for VCS test is failing while for fixed seed 3552393510 for VCS test is passing). First read data by Host is matched with SW read data. Second data read by Host is not matched with SW read data and test is failing on that point. 
Local changes are done on RTL rtl/flash_ctrl_lcmgr.sv as presented on https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/pull/9771/files so this is mandatory before test execution.
Branch for test is https://github.com/nikola-miladinovic/opentitan/tree/flash_ctrl_host_direct_rd.

fix_patch:
diff --git a/hw/ip/flash_ctrl/rtl/flash_phy_rd.sv b/hw/ip/flash_ctrl/rtl/flash_phy_rd.sv
index ed9e7e0ad102f..4d9d342a2baa6 100644
--- a/hw/ip/flash_ctrl/rtl/flash_phy_rd.sv
+++ b/hw/ip/flash_ctrl/rtl/flash_phy_rd.sv
@@ -495,6 +495,11 @@ module flash_phy_rd
 
   // generate the mask calculation request
   // mask calculation is done in parallel to the read stage
+  // calc_req_o is done a cycle after req_o so that most of the
+  // cycle can be allocated to mask calculation logic. req_o,
+  // unlike calc_req_o, asserts the same cycle the transaction is
+  // received, so much of the timing may have already been lost to
+  // transaction routing.
   always_ff @(posedge clk_i or negedge rst_ni) begin
     if (!rst_ni) begin
       calc_req_o <= '0;
diff --git a/hw/ip/flash_ctrl/rtl/flash_phy_scramble.sv b/hw/ip/flash_ctrl/rtl/flash_phy_scramble.sv
index 041f102c5cf03..4c6590d763428 100644
--- a/hw/ip/flash_ctrl/rtl/flash_phy_scramble.sv
+++ b/hw/ip/flash_ctrl/rtl/flash_phy_scramble.sv
@@ -81,6 +81,25 @@ module flash_phy_scramble import flash_phy_pkg::*; (
     end
   end
 
+  // the prim_prince valid_o is a flopped version of valid_i
+  // As a result, when op_req_i stays high due to multiple transactions
+  // in-flight, the receiving logic can misinterpret the 'ack' if we just
+  // tie it to valid_o.
+  // Add a little bit of shimming logic here to properly create the ack
+  logic cipher_valid_in_d, cipher_valid_in_q;
+  logic cipher_valid_out;
+
+  always_ff @(posedge clk_i or negedge rst_ni) begin
+    if (!rst_ni) begin
+      cipher_valid_in_q <= '0;
+    end else begin
+      cipher_valid_in_q <= cipher_valid_in_d;
+    end
+  end
+
+  assign cipher_valid_in_d = op_ack_o ? '0 : op_req_i & !cipher_valid_out;
+  assign op_ack_o = cipher_valid_in_q & cipher_valid_out;
+
   prim_prince # (
     .DataWidth(DataWidth),
     .KeyWidth(KeySize),
@@ -93,12 +112,12 @@ module flash_phy_scramble import flash_phy_pkg::*; (
   ) u_cipher (
     .clk_i,
     .rst_ni,
-    .valid_i(op_req_i),
+    .valid_i(cipher_valid_in_d),
     .data_i(dec ? scrambled_data_i : plain_data_i),
     .key_i(data_key_sel ? rand_data_key_i : data_key_i),
     .dec_i(dec),
     .data_o(data),
-    .valid_o(op_ack_o)
+    .valid_o(cipher_valid_out)
   );
 
   // if decrypt, output the unscrambled data, feed input through otherwise

problem_statement:
## Description
Within the OpenTitan flash controller (`flash_ctrl`), direct reads issued on the host interface can return different data than reads of the same programmed flash words performed through the flash software-controller operation path. Here, a host direct read is a host-side memory-mapped read of flash contents, while a software-controller read is a read started through the flash controller's programmed read operation.

## Expected Behavior
For programmed flash words, each host direct read must return the same word that is stored in flash, and it must match the value returned by the flash software-controller read path for the same address. This must remain true when host direct reads are issued back to back without waiting for each read to complete, both when region scrambling is disabled and when region scrambling is enabled.

## Actual Behavior
The back-to-back host direct read sequence is unreliable when scrambling is enabled for the accessed region. A typical failure is that the first host direct read matches the software-controller readback, but a later host direct read in the same sequence returns different data even though the flash contents were not changed.

## Affected Function
The affected functionality is the flash controller host direct-read path for programmed flash data, especially when its results are compared against the flash software-controller read path under back-to-back read traffic.

## Trigger Condition
The issue is triggered by issuing consecutive host direct reads to programmed flash words without inserting idle time or waiting for earlier reads to finish, in a configuration where scrambling is enabled for the accessed flash region.

resolved_issues.body:
I created a test that turns off measured clocks to verify the timeout functionality. I found the clock can be off for a couple of AON cycles and no timeout will be generated, even though `ref_en` is active. In contrast, a regular measurement asserts `valid` almost concurrently with the assertion of `ref_en`.

I think this weakens the timeout mechanism, allowing the clock to be shut down for enough time with nothing detecting it. See the waves below. The specific test is still under development, but it will eventually become part of the clkmgr_frequency test.

problem_statement:
## Description
OpenTitan clock manager (`clkmgr`) uses the `prim_clock_meas` primitive to monitor root clocks against an always-on (AON) reference clock. In the timeout path that detects a stopped measured clock from the reference-clock domain, the timeout margin is too large.

## Affected Function
The affected functionality is the `prim_clock_meas` timeout check that `clkmgr` uses to detect when a measured root clock stops while the AON reference clock continues running.

## Expected Behavior
After monitoring has fully enabled and the reference-side enable is active, halting the measured clock should cause the reference-domain timeout indication to assert after the normal synchronization delay of the timeout mechanism. A stopped clock should not remain undetected for a couple of extra AON cycles once checking is active.

## Actual Behavior
A measured clock can be absent for a couple of AON cycles without a timeout being reported, even though timeout checking is already enabled. This weakens the timeout mechanism and can allow a short clock stoppage to go undetected.

## Trigger Condition
The issue appears when `prim_clock_meas` is already in steady-state monitoring, the AON reference clock keeps toggling, and the measured clock is then turned off.

problem_statement:
## Description
In the SPI Device upload path, command and address entries are stored in a shared dual-port SRAM and later exposed to software through the command FIFO (CmdFifo) and address FIFO (AddrFifo) in the system clock domain. The affected logic is the `spid_upload` path that issues the system-side SRAM accesses for those two FIFOs after an upload-enabled SPI flash transaction captures an opcode and address.

## Expected Behavior
If the shared SRAM arbiter delays the system-side CmdFifo or AddrFifo request, the pending entry must be held until the grant arrives. After the grant and SRAM response complete, software must still be able to read the uploaded command byte and captured address from the corresponding FIFO outputs in the same order they were recorded.

## Actual Behavior
The upload path can treat a system-side CmdFifo or AddrFifo SRAM request as accepted before the arbiter actually grants it. When the grant is delayed, the read side can advance too early, causing the uploaded command or address entry to disappear or never become visible to software. Software can then miss the upload record or wait indefinitely for FIFO data that should be present.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered during an upload-enabled SPI flash transaction that records both a command byte and an address, when the system-clock-domain SRAM request for CmdFifo or AddrFifo is not granted immediately and remains stalled for one or more system clock cycles.

problem_statement:
## Description
In the Earl Grey top-level `xbar_main` TileLink Uncached Lightweight (TL-UL) interconnect, the RISC-V Debug Module (RV_DM) System Bus Access (SBA) path exposed over JTAG is expected to reach the control and status registers (CSRs) of both SPI Host controller instances, `spi_host0` and `spi_host1`. The affected functionality is the debug-access routing from `rv_dm.sba` to those two SPI Host IP blocks.

## Expected Behavior
A debugger-issued RV_DM SBA read to the `spi_host0` or `spi_host1` CSR address window should be accepted by the main crossbar, routed to the selected SPI Host instance, and return a normal TL-UL read response from that instance without an access error.

## Actual Behavior
`spi_host0` and `spi_host1` are not reachable through the RV_DM SBA path. A JTAG-initiated SBA read to either SPI Host CSR window is not forwarded to the selected SPI Host instance, so the read does not complete as a normal SPI Host CSR access.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered when the debugger uses RV_DM SBA over JTAG to access either SPI Host CSR address window, for example by performing a basic CSR read of `spi_host0` or `spi_host1`. Other RV_DM SBA targets are not the failing case described here.

title: [flash_ctrl] Allow rma entry even if flash has not been initialized.
body:
As part of #10188, it was realized that rma entry is currently gated
by flash initilization.

This may not be a good idea because if flash initlization were to ever
stall (ROM could not program it for whatever reason), then rma entry
could never be done.

This PR allows RMA entry to happen even if initilization has not been
called.  If initilization has not been called, it is possible that
entropy is not properly behaving as part of the ROM routine, so the
reseeding is also skipped so that the flash can be directly wiped.

Signed-off-by: Timothy Chen <timothytim@google.com>

resolved_issues.title: [flash_ctrl] Questions On Secret Seeds (Creator and Owner) and OTP Seed Functionality
resolved_issues.body:
The Spec says: -

Secret Information Partitions

Two information partition pages (one for creator and one for owner) in the design hold secret seeds for the key manager. These pages, when enabled by life cycle and otp, are read upon flash controller initialization (no software configuration is required). The read values are then fed to the key manager for later processing. There is a page for creator and a page for the owner.

This may be true for the secret seeds via Life Cycle Controller, but is does not seem to be the case for the OTP Interface …

**SECRET SEEDS**

During Power Up Initialisation, the secret seeds are output from the Flash Ctrl into the Key Manager, these keys reflect what is programmed into 

    // Secret partition 0 (used for creator): Bank 0, information partition 0, page 1 (Addr 0x0800, 8 Words)
    // Secret partition 1 (used for owner):   Bank 0, information partition 0, page 2 (Addr 0x1000, 8 Words)

Question 1: Using Default CSR values, these secret seeds are NOT read out during INIT.  They are only output during INIT if FLASH_CTRL.INIT (0x18) is set to 1.  However, its default reset value is 0.  

The description for this bit says: -

“Initializes the flash controller. During the initialization process, the flash controller reads out the root seeds before allowing other usage of the flash controller”

Just checking the wording, as this implies the bit controls the Initialization period, which it seems it does not?  This bit controls whether the seeds are read out or not during the initialization period?

Is this the intended functionality? Or is the Reset Value incorrect?

Question 2: It has been observed that FLASH_CTRL.INIT does not exclusively enable the Secret Seeds for output, it also enables the OTP Seed Interface and the RMA Seed interface.

Question 3: To get the Seeds to work, we have to set FLASH_CTRL.INIT to 1 as soon as we start a test (via SW), to get the Seed features to work.

Question 4: It is also noticed that the parameter KEYMGR_FLASH_DEFAULT as defined in both RTL and DV, is unused (maybe left over from a previous version of the TB)

parameter keymgr_flash_t KEYMGR_FLASH_DEFAULT = '{
    seeds: '{
     256'h9152e32c9380a4bcc3e0ab263581e6b0e8825186e1e445631646e8bef8c45d47,
     256'hfa365df52da48cd752fb3a026a8e608f0098cfe5fa9810494829d0cd9479eb78
    }
  };
      Observation 5:  When an RMA Ack has been sent, the RMA State Machine remains in its ‘final’state, until the                device is reset.  I suspect this because after an RMA the DUT is effectively inoperable.

**OTP Seeds**

During Flash Initialisation, the Flash Controller REQUESTS two seeds from the OTP (which makes it different to the Secret Seeds which are output, not input)

These two seeds, Address and Data are sent onto the Scramble Feature in the Flash PHY.

There is little or no information on this in the spec.  I have arrived at this functionality being ‘true’ by investigating the design and waveforms.

Question 6: Is this the functionality as you see it?  The OTP Seeds seem to have no dependence on any Info Partitions.

Question 7: As previously discussed in a meeting, the SCRAMBLE feature will be thoroughly tested at V3, so for V2, we just need to confirm that a seed read from OTP makes it to the SCRAMBLE block.  I am considering probing into the DUT for this test.  Although not ideal, it is quicker, and the full feature will be tested at V3.  What is your opinion?

#!/bin/bash
set -e

# Stage 1: checkout base_sha in a clean workspace (+submodules)
cd /home/opentitan
git reset --hard
git clean -fdx
git checkout 677811a92ecc34d214da44236928b6c680985cca
git submodule update --init --recursive

# Stage 2: install repository apt dependencies (if present)
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
if [[ -f apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing apt dependencies from apt-requirements.txt"
  cp apt-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  sed -i -e '/^$/d' -e '/^#/d' -e 's/#.*//' /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  if [[ -s /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
    apt-get update
    xargs -r apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends < /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
  else
    echo "[INFO] apt-requirements.txt is empty after filtering comments"
  fi
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
else
  echo "[WARN] apt-requirements.txt not found at base_sha; skipping repo-specific apt install"
fi

# Stage 3: install project-specific Python dependencies from the checked-out repo
if [[ -f python-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Python deps from python-requirements.txt"
  python -m pip install -U pip "setuptools<66.0.0"
  cp python-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
  python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re

path = Path("/tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt")
lines = []
for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
    stripped = line.strip()
    if stripped in {
        "types-dataclasses",
        "types-pkg_resources",
    }:
        continue
    line = re.sub(r'(#egg=[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)\s+[<>=!~].*', r'\1', line)
    lines.append(line)
path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
PY
  python -m pip install -r /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt --no-warn-script-location
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
else
  echo "[ERROR] python-requirements.txt not found at base_sha"
  exit 1
fi

# Stage 4: install RISC-V toolchain + Verible, then persist their PATH
if [[ -f util/get-toolchain.py ]]; then
  toolchain_version=""
  if [[ -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
    toolchain_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
  fi

  echo "[INFO] Installing RISC-V toolchain via util/get-toolchain.py"
  if [[ -n "$toolchain_version" ]]; then
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update -r "$toolchain_version"
  else
    echo "[WARN] RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION not found; falling back to util/get-toolchain.py defaults"
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update
  fi
else
  echo "[WARN] util/get-toolchain.py not found at base_sha; skipping RISC-V toolchain install"
fi

verible_version=""
if [[ -f hw/tool_requirements.py ]]; then
  verible_version="$(python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path

ns = {}
exec(Path("hw/tool_requirements.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8"), ns)
reqs = ns.get("__TOOL_REQUIREMENTS__", {})
entry = reqs.get("verible", "")
if isinstance(entry, dict):
    print(entry.get("min_version", ""))
elif isinstance(entry, str):
    print(entry)
PY
)"
fi
if [[ -z "$verible_version" && -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
  verible_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG VERIBLE_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
fi

if [[ -n "$verible_version" ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Verible ${verible_version}"
  rm -rf /tools/verible
  mkdir -p /tools/verible

  verible_url=""
  if [[ -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
    verible_url="https://github.com/chipsalliance/verible/releases/download/${verible_version}/verible-${verible_version}-Ubuntu-18.04-bionic-x86_64.tar.gz"

problem_statement:
## Description
The bug is in the Flash Controller life-cycle manager (`flash_ctrl_lcmgr`) RMA (Return Material Authorization) entry path. The controller currently treats RMA requests as serviceable only after flash initialization has been started through `FLASH_CTRL.INIT`.

## Expected Behavior
An RMA request must be accepted and completed even when `FLASH_CTRL.INIT` has never been asserted. If the life cycle controller requests RMA while the Flash Controller is still in its pre-initialization state, the controller should start the RMA wipe flow and eventually assert the RMA acknowledge signal instead of waiting for flash initialization first.

## Actual Behavior
If the life cycle controller requests RMA before software starts flash initialization, the request is not serviced. The life-cycle manager stays in the pre-initialization path and does not produce an RMA acknowledge, so the device cannot complete RMA entry through the Flash Controller.

## Affected Function
The affected logic is the Flash Controller life-cycle manager's handling of RMA entry before normal flash initialization.

## Trigger Condition
Leave `FLASH_CTRL.INIT` deasserted after reset, then assert an RMA request from the life cycle controller.

resolved_issues.title: [ entropy_src rtl, dv ] Do not clear entropy_src statistics on disable
resolved_issues.body:
The health check statistics registers (watermarks, test failure counts, alert counts etc.) have all proven to be essential tools for verification.    In DV these registers are read and scoreboarded
- At the end of every simulation, and
- Every time an alert occurs.
However these checks are made more complicated by the fact that these registers are cleared every time the IP is disabled.  Ideally DV would be able to disable the DUT, check the statistics.  This would allow the testbench to take a clean snapshot of the health check data.

However since these registers are cleared once the enable register is set to `MuBi4False` this forced the test bench to read these stats while the DUT is still collecting data.
  
If the RNG test runs long enough (about 2ms) eventually the testbench will encounter a scenario where the test tries to read a register as it is being updated this leads to scenarios such as in the following UVM error example:

```
UVM_WARNING @ 2534116459 ps: (uvm_reg_field.svh:1186) [RegModel] Trying to predict value of field 'markov_hi_total_fails' while register 'entropy_src_reg_block.markov_hi_total_fails' is being accessed
UVM_FATAL @ 2534116459 ps: (entropy_src_scoreboard.sv:324) [uvm_test_top.env.scoreboard] Check failed (total_fail_field.predict(.value(fail_total), .kind(UVM_PREDICT_DIRECT)))
```

This issue requests that the following registers not be cleared on disable, rather the clear event should be delayed to just before the following enable event: 
- repcnt_hi_watermarks
- repcnts_hi_watermarks
- adaptp_hi_watermarks
- adaptp_lo_watermarks
- extht_hi_watermarks
- extht_lo_watermarks
- bucket_hi_watermarks
- markov_hi_watermarks
- markov_lo_watermarks
- repcnt_total_fails
- repcnts_total_fails
- adaptp_hi_total_fails
- adaptp_lo_total_fails
- bucket_total_fails
- markov_hi_total_fails
- markov_lo_total_fails
- extht_hi_total_fails
- extht_lo_total_fails
- alert_summary_fail_counts
- alert_fail_counts
- extht_fail_counts

#!/bin/bash
cd /home/opentitan || exit 1

source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

set +e
timeout 1800 ./util/dvsim/dvsim.py hw/ip/entropy_src/dv/entropy_src_sim_cfg.hjson \
  -i entropy_src_rng \
  -t vcs \
  --fixed-seed 1 \
  --scratch-root /home/opentitan/.tb_entropy_src_rng_repro \
  --local \
  --purge \
  --no-rerun \
  -v l
rc=$?
set -e

echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_START"
if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "TEST: entropy_src_rng_disable_stats ... PASS"
else
  echo "TEST: entropy_src_rng_disable_stats ... FAIL"
fi
echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"

exit "$rc"
problem_statement:
## Description
OpenTitan's Entropy Source IP records health-test results in read-only control/status registers (CSRs) so firmware and design verification (DV) can inspect the outcome of a run after collection stops. These statistics include watermark registers, total failure counters, and alert-related failure counters. The bug is that disabling the Entropy Source immediately destroys the accumulated statistics.

## Affected Function
The affected functionality is retention of Entropy Source health-test statistics in CSRs, including `repcnt_hi_watermarks`, `repcnts_hi_watermarks`, `adaptp_hi_watermarks`, `adaptp_lo_watermarks`, `extht_hi_watermarks`, `extht_lo_watermarks`, `bucket_hi_watermarks`, `markov_hi_watermarks`, `markov_lo_watermarks`, the corresponding `*_total_fails` counters, `alert_summary_fail_counts`, `alert_fail_counts`, and `extht_fail_counts`.

## Expected Behavior
After the Entropy Source is disabled, these statistics CSRs should stop changing but must continue to hold the values accumulated during the completed run so software or DV can read a clean, stable snapshot. The listed registers should be cleared only when a new Entropy Source run starts because the IP is enabled again, not when the current run is disabled.

## Actual Behavior
When the main enable is turned off, the Entropy Source clears the accumulated health-test statistics immediately. This removes the post-run snapshot needed for verification and firmware analysis, so the only remaining option is to read the statistics while the block is still active and the counters or watermarks may still be updating. In long-running random-number-generator health-test simulations, that can produce scoreboard mismatches when a statistics CSR is read around the same time it changes.

## Trigger Condition
The bug appears when the Entropy Source has been enabled long enough to accumulate health-test statistics and is then disabled before those statistics are read. It is especially exposed in random-number-generator mode tests that disable the block before checking the statistics CSRs at the end of collection.

It appears that np_sample_cnt_q[15:0] is not being reset when the set of matching filters changes as required by the design spec.

> All pairs of filters that are enabled in adc_chn0_filter_ctl[7:0] and adc_chn1_filter_ctl[7:0] are evaluated after each pair of samples has been taken. The filter result is passed to the periodic scan counter if enabled and not at its limit otherwise the result is passed to the debounce counter. The list below describes how the counters interpret the filter results:
If no filters are hit then the counter will reset to zero.
**If one or more filters are hit but the set hit differs from the previous evaluation the counter resets to zero.**
If one or more filters are hit and either none was hit in the previous evaluation or the same set was hit in the previous evaluation and the counter is not at its limit then the counter will increment.

To reproduce:
gh pr checkout 10147
./util/dvsim/dvsim.py hw/ip/adc_ctrl/dv/adc_ctrl_sim_cfg.hjson -i adc_ctrl_filters_polled --fixed-seed 1 --tool xcelium --waves

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/78102677/150572591-449750f7-7bfd-4f4b-b42a-f88327406cfd.png)

problem_statement:
## Description
The OpenTitan ADC (Analog-to-Digital Converter) controller IP (`adc_ctrl`) does not follow the design-spec semantics of the normal-power (NP) debounce counter (`np_sample_cnt`) when the set of matching enabled filter pairs changes. After each pair of channel samples is evaluated, if the current non-zero filter-match bitmap differs from the previous non-zero filter-match bitmap, the NP debounce sequence must restart for the new bitmap instead of reusing debounce history from the old one.

## Expected Behavior
A debounce-complete result must be reported only after `np_sample_cnt` consecutive evaluations of the same non-zero filter-match bitmap. If the match bitmap changes to a different non-zero value, the accumulated NP debounce count must be cleared and the new bitmap must start a fresh debounce run. This rule also applies when the controller has just moved from low-power (LP) periodic scanning into continuous NP scanning.

## Actual Behavior
When the controller is already accumulating NP debounce history, a later evaluation with a different non-zero filter-match bitmap can inherit the previous count. In that case the ADC controller can report debounce completion too early for the new filter match.

## Trigger Condition
The failure occurs when one filter-match bitmap has already contributed to NP debouncing and a later evaluation produces a different non-zero bitmap before the new bitmap has been debounced for the full configured NP sample count. One concrete failing case is the LP-to-NP path: an LP periodic scan sees one matching filter set, NP scanning begins, and then the match bitmap changes to a different non-zero filter set.

resolved_issues.title: [ entropy_src ] Bucket Health Test not including last sample
resolved_issues.body:
The Bucket health test looks for excessive correlations between RNG channels by maintaining a histogram of the RNG symbols coming and reporting an error if any symbols exceed a given threshold.

If the last RNG symbol pushes the test over the threshold, the histogram peak is recorded but not in time to register a test failure.

---

For example, in the following waveform (taken from signals within `u_entropy_src_bucket_ht`), the relevant signals are near the bottom of the screenshot.  The end of the window is shown by the last signal `window_wrap_pulse_o`.   The last input to `entropy_bit_i[3:0]` is `4'hf`, and it is the 11th instance of that value in the window.  At the very end of the test, this count (`16'000B`) is accurately reflected in the signal `test_cnt_o`, highlighted as dark blue.  Though this exceeds the threshold of 16'h000A (highlighed as light blue).  The `test_fail_pulse_o` signal remains low (highlighted as orange).

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47870387/150387854-1d62d606-bfb3-42b1-9273-766bc6292510.png)

To reproduce this result, pull the branch `issue_10226`  from my fork (`git@github.com:martin-lueker/opentitan.git`) and run the following  command (from `$OT_ROOT` on WD servers):
```
./util/dvsim/dvsim.py hw/ip/entropy_src/dv/entropy_src_sim_cfg.hjson -i entropy_src_rng -r 1 -t xcelium --job-prefix="nc run -C ncsim_interactive -Il" -w=shm -s=1 --run-modes set_verbosity_comp_a_uvm_debug set_verbosity_comp_b_uvm_debug
```

---

Suggested Fix: 
The `test_fail_pulse_o` signal is drawn from the output of a secondary "Test event counter" which counts the _number_ of bins that exceed threshold, and fires an error if `test_cnt > '0`.  This however incurs a one cycle delay, and is not strictly necessary.  Instead one could look at the array `bin_cnt_exceeds_thresh`.

Written as a patch this change would look like this:

```
diff --git a/hw/ip/entropy_src/rtl/entropy_src_bucket_ht.sv b/hw/ip/entropy_src/rtl/entropy_src_bucket_ht.sv
index d6210ebb0..4b71cc9b2 100644
--- a/hw/ip/entropy_src/rtl/entropy_src_bucket_ht.sv
+++ b/hw/ip/entropy_src/rtl/entropy_src_bucket_ht.sv
@@ -94,7 +94,7 @@ module entropy_src_bucket_ht #(
     );
 
   // the pulses will be only one clock in length
-  assign test_fail_pulse_o = active_i && window_wrap_pulse_i && (|bin_cnt_exceeds_thresh);
+  assign test_fail_pulse_o = active_i && window_wrap_pulse_i && (test_cnt > '0);
   assign test_cnt_o = bin_max;
   assign count_err_o = test_cnt_err || (|bin_cntr_err);
```

Note: Once this change is applied, lint checks confirm that the signal test_cnt is no longer needed and the whole unit `u_prim_count_test_cnt` can be removed from the bucket test as well.

-  assign test_fail_pulse_o = active_i && window_wrap_pulse_i && (test_cnt > '0);
+  assign test_fail_pulse_o = active_i && window_wrap_pulse_i && (|bin_cnt_exceeds_thresh);

-  assign count_err_o = test_cnt_err || (|bin_cntr_err);
+  assign count_err_o = |bin_cntr_err;

problem_statement:
## Description
The Entropy Source (`entropy_src`) IP contains a bucket health test in the `entropy_src_bucket_ht` submodule. For each observation window, this test builds a histogram of random number generator (RNG) symbols and reports a failure when any histogram bin exceeds the programmed threshold.

## Trigger Condition
The bug occurs when the symbol that first pushes a histogram bin above the threshold is also the final valid symbol of the observation window. One concrete case is a 4-bit symbol stream in which the value `0xf` appears 11 times in a single window while the threshold is 10.

## Expected Behavior
When an observation window closes, the bucket health test must evaluate the completed histogram for that window, including the last valid symbol. If any bin count is greater than the threshold, `test_fail_pulse_o` must assert for that window, and `test_cnt_o` must report the completed window's peak bin count.

## Actual Behavior
In the failing case above, the completed histogram and `test_cnt_o` reflect the final count of 11, but `test_fail_pulse_o` does not assert when the window ends. As a result, a bucket-test failure that occurs on the last sample of the window is missed.

resolved_issues.title: prim_count may never trigger an error
resolved_issues.body:
In otp, this prim_count is parameterized to a up increasing CrossCnt, but `set_i` is tie to 0 as it uses the default max value (all 1s).
https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/68e86515989c047e28915f6d5d534c578c9bdb3d/hw/ip/otp_ctrl/rtl/otp_ctrl_part_buf.sv#L585-L599

However, since `set_i` is always 0. `cmp_valid` is always invalid, which causes the error is always 0 regardless the counter value.

https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/68e86515989c047e28915f6d5d534c578c9bdb3d/hw/ip/prim/rtl/prim_count.sv#L114-L122

Some observations:
We can always set `en_i` to let counters count, but there are some cases that `cmp_valid` stays invalid which prevents the error from being triggered, such as
1. `set_i` is tie to 0 
2. set `clr_i` and then increase the counter by setting `en_i` without sending a new `set_i`.

Can we try to get rid of `cmp_valid` which can prevent the error? 

cc: @cindychip

resolved_issues.title: [flash_ctrl] Possible bug with Vivado 2020.2
resolved_issues.body:
The Vivado PnR tool seems to create an unintended combo loop under specific conditions:

1. The fsm is sparsely encoded (not consecutive in value)
2. Not all the defined states are explicitly listed out (ie, absorbed into default state)

This problem manifested in both `flash_ctrl_lcmgr` and `flash_ctrl_arb`, where both cw305 and cw310 fpga builds claimed there was a combo loop when there was not. 

@a-will helped have a look, and it the following are the pictures are before and after optimizations.

![image (1)](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1026250/150246347-7cbaee99-60ac-40f0-8b31-ae93f3bb83dc.png)
![image (2)](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1026250/150246353-30616d28-f98c-4a9c-9cd3-ac4328237060.png)

After optimizations, the `done_i` signal is used directly in creating `ctrl_op`, however, this is not the case in the actual design.

#!/bin/bash

cd /home/opentitan
git reset --hard
git clean -fdx
git checkout 95ba869ee4359cdc5627a88046abcc1a11da80e2
git submodule update --init --recursive

# Stage 2: install repository apt dependencies (if present)
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
if [[ -f apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing apt dependencies from apt-requirements.txt"
  cp apt-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  sed -i -e '/^$/d' -e '/^#/d' -e 's/#.*//' /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  if [[ -s /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
    apt-get update
    xargs -r apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends < /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
  else
    echo "[INFO] apt-requirements.txt is empty after filtering comments"
  fi
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
else
  echo "[WARN] apt-requirements.txt not found at base SHA; skipping repo-specific apt install"
fi

# Stage 3: install project-specific Python dependencies from the checked-out repo
if [[ -f python-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Python deps from python-requirements.txt"
  python -m pip install -U pip "setuptools<66.0.0"
  cp python-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
  python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re

path = Path("/tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt")
lines = []
for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
    stripped = line.strip()
    if stripped in {
        "types-dataclasses",
        "types-pkg_resources",
    }:
        continue
    line = re.sub(r'(#egg=[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)\s+[<>=!~].*', r'\1', line)
    lines.append(line)
path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
PY
  python -m pip install -r /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt --no-warn-script-location
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
else
  echo "[ERROR] python-requirements.txt not found at base SHA"
  exit 1
fi

# Stage 4: install RISC-V toolchain + Verible, then persist their PATH
if [[ -f util/get-toolchain.py ]]; then
  toolchain_version=""
  if [[ -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
    toolchain_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
  fi

  echo "[INFO] Installing RISC-V toolchain via util/get-toolchain.py"
  if [[ -n "$toolchain_version" ]]; then
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update -r "$toolchain_version"
  else
    echo "[WARN] RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION not found; falling back to util/get-toolchain.py defaults"
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update
  fi
else
  echo "[WARN] util/get-toolchain.py not found at base SHA; skipping RISC-V toolchain install"
fi

verible_version=""
if [[ -f hw/tool_requirements.py ]]; then
  verible_version="$(python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path

ns = {}
exec(Path("hw/tool_requirements.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8"), ns)
reqs = ns.get("__TOOL_REQUIREMENTS__", {})
entry = reqs.get("verible", "")
if isinstance(entry, dict):
    print(entry.get("min_version", ""))
elif isinstance(entry, str):
    print(entry)
PY
)"
fi
if [[ -z "$verible_version" && -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
  verible_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG VERIBLE_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
fi

if [[ -n "$verible_version" ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Verible ${verible_version}"
  rm -rf /tools/verible
  mkdir -p /tools/verible

  verible_url=""
  for asset in \
    "verible-${verible_version}-linux-static-x86_64.tar.gz" \
    "verible-${verible_version}-Ubuntu-20.04-focal-x86_64.tar.gz" \
    "verible-${verible_version}-Ubuntu-18.04-bionic-x86_64.tar.gz" \
    "verible-${verible_version}-Ubuntu-16.04-xenial-x86_64.tar.gz"
  do
    candidate_url="https://github.com/chipsalliance/verible/releases/download/${verible_version}/${asset}"
    if curl -fILs -o /dev/null "$candidate_url"; then
      verible_url="$candidate_url"
      break
    fi
  done

  if [[ -n "$verible_url" ]]; then
    curl -fLs -o /tmp/verible.tar.gz "$verible_url"
    tar -C /tools/verible -xf /tmp/verible.tar.gz --strip-components=1
    rm -f /tmp/verible.tar.gz
  else
    echo "[WARN] Unable to locate a downloadable Verible archive for ${verible_version}; continuing without Verible"
  fi
else
  echo "[WARN] Unable to determine Verible version from hw/tool_requirements.py or util/container/Dockerfile"
fi

cat > /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh <<'EOF'
for d in /tools/riscv/bin /tools/verible/bin; do
  [ -d "$d" ] && export PATH="$d:$PATH"
done
EOF

if ! grep -q "/etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh" /etc/opentitan_bash_env; then
  echo "source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh" >> /etc/opentitan_bash_env
fi

else
  echo "[WARN] verible-verilog-lint not found after Stage 4"

problem_statement:
## Description
`prim_count` is an OpenTitan hardened counter primitive. In `CrossCnt` mode, it keeps an up counter and a complementary down counter whose sum must equal the active maximum count value. Some users, including the OTP (One-Time Programmable) controller partition-buffer address counter, do not load a custom maximum with `set_i` and instead rely on the built-in default maximum of `2**Width - 1`.

## Affected Function
The bug affects `prim_count` in `CrossCnt` mode when an instance relies on the implicit default maximum instead of loading a custom one with `set_i`.

## Expected Behavior
If no custom maximum has been loaded, `prim_count` must use `2**Width - 1` as the active maximum. After reset, and after any later `clr_i`, the cross-counter state must return to the default consistent state: the up counter at `0` and the down counter at `2**Width - 1`. When the instance is configured so `cnt_o` exposes the down-counter value (`OutSelDnCnt == 1`), `cnt_o` must therefore read `2**Width - 1` immediately after reset or clear, and `err_o` must remain low in that valid default state.

## Actual Behavior
In the current implementation, reset and `clr_i` do not restore a valid default-maximum state for `CrossCnt` instances that rely on the implicit maximum. As a result, when the down counter is selected as the observable output, `cnt_o` becomes `0` after reset or clear instead of `2**Width - 1`, even though the instance is supposed to restart from the default maximum state.

## Trigger Conditions
This bug appears when `prim_count` runs in `CrossCnt` mode and the design relies on the implicit default maximum rather than loading a new one through `set_i`, either because `set_i` is tied low from power-up or because `clr_i` was asserted after a previous run and no new maximum was loaded afterward.

title: [aes] Rework hardened round counter, forward fatal alert to cipher core
body:
Based on the D2S review (See #10422) this PR implements the following two changes:
1. The hardened round counter is reworked to move the counter flops back into the multi-rail FSMs.
2. The fatal alert is forwarded from the main FSM to the cipher core.

I will update the documentation accordingly in a separate PR (together with other doc-related AIs of the D2S review).

repo.name: opentitan
repo.description: OpenTitan: Open source silicon root of trust

commits.message:
[aes] Rework hardened round counter using multi-rail FSM

Moving the counter flops into the multi-rail FSMs of the AES cipher core
has two advantages:
- The design becomes simpler and the RTL more readable.
- The security of the counter scales with the number of FSM rails.

This is related to lowRISC/OpenTitan#10422.

Signed-off-by: Pirmin Vogel <vogelpi@lowrisc.org>

[aes] Forward fatal alert to cipher core

Previously, in case of a fatal alert detected outside of the cipher
core, the cipher core would still continue to process the current block
but eventually get blocked by the main FSM not performing the
handshake. Whit this commit, the cipher core will lock up immediately.

This is related to lowRISC/OpenTitan#10422.

Signed-off-by: Pirmin Vogel <vogelpi@lowrisc.org>

problem_statement:
## Description
The OpenTitan AES IP mishandles fatal alerts that originate in AES control logic outside the cipher core. If such an unrecoverable fault is detected while a block encryption or decryption operation is already running, the top-level AES controller raises a fatal alert, but the cipher-core control finite state machine (FSM) does not immediately treat that alert as a terminal condition.

## Affected Function
The affected logic is the AES cipher-core control FSM and the interface that propagates fatal alerts from the top-level AES controller into an active cipher-core operation.

## Expected Behavior
A fatal alert in the AES IP is unrecoverable for the current operation. If any AES logic raises a fatal alert while the cipher core is processing a block, the cipher-core control FSM must immediately enter its terminal error or lockup state and remain locked until reset, even when the fault originated outside the cipher core.

## Actual Behavior
When a fatal alert is raised by non-cipher-core AES logic during an active block operation, the AES IP reports the fatal condition, but the cipher-core FSM can continue its current round activity instead of locking immediately. Because the top-level controller stops the normal handshakes, the cipher core then stalls in an in-progress state instead of transitioning directly to its terminal error or lockup state.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered when the cipher core has already started round processing for a block and a fatal alert is raised by AES control logic outside the cipher core, for example because an AES control-register value becomes invalid or corrupted during the operation.

resolved_issues.title: [sw, dif, aes] The AES DIF is mixing up MODE and OPERATION

problem_statement:
OpenTitan's AES Device Interface Function (DIF) incorrectly translates a `dif_aes_transaction_t` into the shadowed AES control register (`AES_CTRL_SHADOWED`). The affected functionality is the AES DIF transaction setup path that programs the AES control fields before a transaction starts.

The expected behavior is that the control register fields are derived directly and independently from the transaction description. In particular, the MODE field must come from `transaction.mode`, and the OPERATION field must come from `transaction.operation`. A request for Cipher Block Chaining (CBC) decryption must therefore program CBC in the MODE field and decryption in the OPERATION field. Software must be able to request non-Electronic Codebook (non-ECB) modes through the transaction itself rather than through a separate mode-selection path.

The observed behavior is that these control fields are mixed up when the AES DIF prepares the register value. The transaction's `mode` is not used correctly to drive the MODE field, and the OPERATION field can be chosen using the wrong transaction field. As a result, the value written to `AES_CTRL_SHADOWED` can differ from the requested transaction, so non-ECB requests and decrypt requests can be configured incorrectly.

This bug is triggered when software starts an AES transaction through the AES DIF and relies on the transaction structure as the source of truth for configuration. A concrete failing case is a CBC decryption request: after the DIF programs `AES_CTRL_SHADOWED`, the MODE and OPERATION fields may not match the CBC-decrypt transaction that software requested.

resolved_issues.title: [entropy_src, security] Need to prevent generation of FIPS entropy before FIPS thresholds are set.
resolved_issues.body:
The `entropy_src` FSM has two modes of entropy "BOOT" and "FIPS".  The health checks for the two modes have different stringency requirements and are configured at different times in the boot process.
1. As indicated in #9492, the boot thresholds are meant to be very light, meant to catch very gross defects in the `entropy_src`.  These must be programmed in _OTP_ memory to allow for the creation of entropy pre-boot.
2. FIPS (or CC) grade entropy requires the addition of more stringent health-check thresholds to make sure that the `entropy_src` outputs achieve maximal entropy at the output of the conditioning block.  The final decision for these thresholds must be reserved for _firmware_, as they may require some knowledge of post silicon tolerances in the RNG.

Furthermore, since the `entropy_src` prohibits the relaxation of thresholds after reset (they can only be strengthened), the default values are always set to their most relaxed values by default.

The current plan (#9492) then requires the entropy source to be enabled by the ROM (using OTP values), while leaving the FIPS thresholds wide open.   Furthermore the transition from BOOT mode to "FIPS" mode is automatic.   This means that any few "FIPS mode" seeds that come out before the ROM_EXT comes on line will be labelled as full-entropy ("FIPS"==1), but without any real health checking.

We need a mechanism to prevent the generation of fully-qualified entropy until all of the "FIPS" health check thresholds have been fully populated.  (If such a mechanism already exists it needs to be called out in the register spec).

#!/bin/bash
cd /home/opentitan || exit 1
set +e
set -o pipefail

if [ -f /home/opentitan_tools/path.sh ]; then
  source /home/opentitan_tools/path.sh
fi

TEST_NAME="entropy_src_smoke"
TB_DIR="/home/opentitan/.tb_${TEST_NAME}"
BUILD_LOG="${TB_DIR}/dvsim.log"

rm -rf "$TB_DIR"
mkdir -p "$TB_DIR"

cat > "$TB_DIR/entropy_src_boot_phase_done_vseq.sv" <<'EOF'
class entropy_src_boot_phase_done_vseq extends entropy_src_smoke_vseq;
  `uvm_object_utils(entropy_src_boot_phase_done_vseq)

    bit [31:0] debug_status;
    int unsigned wait_cnt;

    super.body();

    // Wait for boot-done to assert, then make sure it stays asserted.
    for (wait_cnt = 0; wait_cnt < 200; wait_cnt++) begin
      cfg.clk_rst_vif.wait_clks(5);
      csr_rd(.ptr(ral.debug_status), .value(debug_status), .backdoor(1));
      if (debug_status[17] === 1'b1) begin
        repeat (5) begin
          cfg.clk_rst_vif.wait_clks(5);
          csr_rd(.ptr(ral.debug_status), .value(debug_status), .backdoor(1));
          if (debug_status[17] !== 1'b1) begin
            `uvm_fatal(`gfn, "boot phase done deasserted before thresholds were updated")
          end
        end
        return;
      end
    end

    `uvm_fatal(`gfn, "boot phase done never asserted")
  endtask
endclass
EOF

problem_statement:
## Description
The `entropy_src` IP has a BOOT mode that uses light health-test thresholds stored in OTP (One-Time Programmable) memory so ROM can obtain entropy before later firmware initialization. It also has a post-boot path that is intended to produce Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS)-qualified entropy only after firmware has programmed stricter health-test thresholds. The bug is in the `entropy_src` main finite state machine (FSM): when the block is left enabled after BOOT mode, it automatically leaves the BOOT path and enters the post-boot startup/FIPS path while those stricter thresholds are still at their default relaxed values.

## Expected Behavior
If `entropy_src` is enabled during ROM boot with only the BOOT thresholds configured, it may produce BOOT-mode entropy only. After the BOOT phase finishes, the main FSM must not automatically enter the post-boot startup/FIPS path. No seed generated before firmware has populated the stricter post-boot health-test thresholds may be exposed or labeled as full-entropy / FIPS-qualified output.

## Actual Behavior
The main FSM automatically transitions from BOOT mode into the post-boot startup/FIPS path without waiting for the stricter post-boot thresholds to be programmed. As a result, seeds generated after the BOOT phase can be treated as full-entropy / FIPS-qualified output even though the intended stronger health checks are not yet in place.

## Affected Function
The affected logic is the `entropy_src` IP's main FSM, specifically the BOOT-mode to post-boot startup/FIPS handoff.

## Trigger Condition
This occurs when ROM enables `entropy_src` using BOOT thresholds from OTP, leaves the stricter post-boot thresholds at their default relaxed values for later firmware configuration, and the block remains enabled when the BOOT phase completes.

title: [rstmgr] Correctly handle non-always-on por_ni
body:
- fixes https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/issues/10682
- The fix in https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/pull/8010 was incomplete. The non-always-on por_ni was fed in
  to rstmgr, however the non-always-on lc_src_rst did not take effect
  based on por_ni asserting.
- This fix uses the internal por reset directly as the parent reset for lc/sys
  reset nodes.  This ensures that if the external por_n_i drops for any reason,
  even if clocks are killed, the internal nodes are all reset as well.

resolved_issues.title: [rstmgr] Issue with non-always-on POR handling
resolved_issues.body:
When the non-always-on POR drops in unexpected scenarios (ie, instability of power instead of low power entry), the fast clocks in the system may also be simultaneously turned off.   This situation is not handled by the rstmgr right now as the non-always-on domain resets are typically treated as a synchronous event instead of asynchronous event.

This means when the clocks disappear, the synchronous event cannot propagate, and in effect the unexpected POR drop does not reset anything that is connected to that power rail.

This has to be fixed or else the behavior of such situations can be non-deterministic.

problem_statement:
## Description
OpenTitan's Reset Manager (rstmgr) generates power-on reset (POR) signals and downstream reset sources for the always-on domain and for non-always-on power domains. There is a bug in the non-always-on reset path: when a non-always-on `por_ni` input drops unexpectedly, the downstream resets for that domain are still effectively dependent on synchronous propagation through the domain's fast clocks.

## Affected Function
The affected logic is rstmgr's reset propagation for a non-always-on power domain, specifically the path from a non-always-on POR event to that domain's POR-generated reset, life cycle reset source, and system reset source.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered when a non-always-on POR asserts unexpectedly, such as during a power instability rather than an intentional low-power transition, while the fast clocks for that domain are stopped or disappear at the same time.

## Expected Behavior
For a non-always-on power domain, asserting `por_ni` must deterministically place that domain in reset even when its fast clocks are unavailable. While `por_ni` remains asserted, rstmgr must keep that domain's POR-generated reset, life cycle reset source, and system reset source asserted. After `por_ni` is released and normal clocking resumes, those reset sources may return inactive.

## Actual Behavior
In the failing case, the non-always-on POR event occurs, but the downstream life cycle reset source and system reset source for that domain do not assert if the fast clocks are absent. As a result, an unexpected POR drop does not fully reset logic on that non-always-on power rail.

cd /home/opentitan

CFG_FILE="${TB_DIR}/kmac_state_valid_cfg.hjson"

emit_result() {
  local status="$1"
  echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_START"
  echo "TEST: ${TEST_NAME} ... ${status}"
  echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"
}

rm -rf "${TB_DIR}"
mkdir -p "${TB_DIR}"

python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path

root = Path("/home/opentitan")
tb_dir = Path("/home/opentitan/.tb_kmac_state_valid_gate")

(root / "hw/ip/kmac/dv/env/seq_lib/kmac_state_valid_gate_vseq.sv").write_text(
    r'''class kmac_state_valid_gate_vseq extends kmac_base_vseq;
  `uvm_object_utils(kmac_state_valid_gate_vseq)
  `uvm_object_new

  virtual task body();
    bit [TL_DW-1:0] word;
    uvm_hdl_data_t force_word;

    do_kmac_init = 0;
    dut_init();
    cfg.clk_rst_vif.wait_clks(5);

    if (!cfg.kmac_vif.idle_o) begin
      `uvm_fatal(`gfn, "kmac not idle")
    end

    force_word = 32'h1badb002;
    if (!uvm_hdl_force("tb.dut.reg_state[0][31:0]", force_word)) begin
      `uvm_fatal(`gfn, "failed to force reg_state word")
    end

    cfg.clk_rst_vif.wait_clks(2);
    tl_access(.addr(ral.get_addr_from_offset(KMAC_STATE_SHARE0_BASE)),
              .write(1'b0),
              .data(word));
    if (word !== 32'h0) begin
      `uvm_fatal(`gfn, $sformatf("STATE window leaked internal state: 0x%08h", word))
    end

    if (!uvm_hdl_release("tb.dut.reg_state[0][31:0]")) begin
      `uvm_fatal(`gfn, "failed to release reg_state")
    end
  endtask
endclass
''',
    encoding="utf-8",
)


def patch_once(path_str: str, old: str, new: str) -> None:
    path = root / path_str
    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    if new in text:
        return
    if old not in text:
        raise SystemExit(f"missing anchor in {path}")
    path.write_text(text.replace(old, new, 1), encoding="utf-8")


patch_once(
    "hw/ip/kmac/dv/env/seq_lib/kmac_vseq_list.sv",
    '`include "kmac_stress_all_vseq.sv"\n',

)

    "hw/ip/kmac/dv/env/kmac_env.core",
    "      - seq_lib/kmac_stress_all_vseq.sv: {is_include_file: true}\n",
    "      - seq_lib/kmac_stress_all_vseq.sv: {is_include_file: true}\n"
    "      - seq_lib/kmac_state_valid_gate_vseq.sv: {is_include_file: true}\n",
)

(tb_dir / "kmac_state_valid_cfg.hjson").write_text(
    """{
  import_cfgs: ["{proj_root}/hw/ip/kmac/dv/kmac_unmasked_sim_cfg.hjson"]
  tests: [
    {
      name: kmac_state_valid_gate
      uvm_test_seq: kmac_state_valid_gate_vseq
      reseed: 1
    }
  ]
}
""",
    encoding="utf-8",
)
PY
patch_rc=$?

if [[ ${patch_rc} -ne 0 ]]; then
  emit_result "FAIL"
  exit "${patch_rc}"
fi

timeout 1800 python3 util/dvsim/dvsim.py \
  "${CFG_FILE}" \
  -i "${TEST_NAME}" \
  -t vcs \
  --fixed-seed 1 \
  --reseed 1 \
  --local \
  --max-parallel 1 \
  --no-rerun \
  --scratch-root "${TB_DIR}" \
  2>&1 | tee "${LOG_FILE}"
rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}

if [[ ${rc} -eq 0 ]]; then
  emit_result "PASS"
else
  emit_result "FAIL"
fi

exit "${rc}"

problem_statement:
## Description
The KMAC (Keccak Message Authentication Code) hardware IP does not sufficiently harden the software-visible output path for its `STATE` window. Because the same KMAC block is also used by the OpenTitan key manager, the `STATE` window must fail closed whenever no software-readable state is valid.

## Expected Behavior
The `STATE` window must expose the Keccak state only when a software-visible digest/state is valid. In particular, while KMAC is idle and no digest/state is available for software, reads from `STATE` must return all zeros.

## Actual Behavior
When the software-visible state is invalid, the `STATE` output path can still reflect a non-zero internal Keccak state instead of zero. This weakens the hardening of the KMAC output path and can make it a single point of failure for observing activity that should not be exposed through the software interface.

## Affected Function
The bug affects the KMAC IP's software-visible `STATE` window output gating.

## Trigger Condition
The issue is triggered when software accesses the `STATE` window while KMAC is in a non-readable condition, especially the idle state before any digest/state has become valid for software, and the internal state path still contains non-zero data.

problem_statement:
## Description
The USB device controller (USBDEV) full-speed packet engine does not correctly resolve transfer type when the same USB endpoint number is used in both directions. If the OUT direction for endpoint N is configured to use control-transfer handling while the IN direction for endpoint N is marked as isochronous, the IN side can still be treated as isochronous.

## Affected Function
The affected logic is the USBDEV full-speed packet engine's endpoint-type handling for a shared endpoint number, specifically the interaction between control handling on the OUT side and isochronous handling on the IN side.

## Expected Behavior
Control-transfer handling on endpoint N OUT must override isochronous classification on endpoint N IN for the same endpoint number. In that mixed configuration, an IN token for endpoint N with no queued IN payload must produce a short USB handshake response rather than starting a longer data-style isochronous transmit response.

## Actual Behavior
The current implementation can leave endpoint N IN classified as isochronous even when the matching endpoint N OUT is configured for control handling. Under that configuration, an IN token can trigger a longer data-style transmit response instead of the short control/handshake response that software expects.

## Trigger Conditions
The bug appears when the same endpoint number is used for both directions, the OUT direction is configured for control handling, the IN direction is marked as isochronous, no IN payload is ready, and the device receives an IN token for that endpoint number.

resolved_issues.title: [entropy_src] Implementation & Documentation of Markov Test
resolved_issues.body:
In the entropy_src the "Markov test" aims to detect either 
1. Oversampling of AST/RNG outputs leading to "clustered" input values that eventually change, but often are just repeats of the previous sample.  For example the string: "00111111000011000111000111000001111" has roughly equal numbers of 1's and 0's, but no good entropy source should generate such strings, because each bit is likely just a repeat of the previous one.
2. Wild oscillation of the RNG, in a distinctly non-random way.  For instance the string: "010101010101010101" has almost zero entropy, even though the number of 1's and 0's appears unbiased.

Detection accomplished by counting the number of changes in the a fixed number of RNG samples, and comparing number of "01"/"10" pairs to the number of "00"/"11" pairs.  Ideally the switched "01"vs. non-switched pairs should be roughly equal.

The [specification]() illustrates this test with a figure: 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47870387/146693810-1b46c562-1b78-4c24-a85c-3ece616393a5.png)

However the specification is very light on details and there are (at least) two ways of interpreting the spec:
1.  The total number of "10"/"01" pairs is counted and summed for all four RNG inputs.  In the figure above the test would output 5+2+5+2=14, and this value would be recorded for diagnostics and compared to thresholds.
2. The number of "10"/"01" pairs is counted for all for each RNG channel, and among each of the four channels the minimum and maximum value is taken, and compared to HI and LO threshold's.   The minimum and maximum would both be output separately for diagnostic purposes.

In verifying the design, I've noticed that the second approach has been adopted, even though the specification does not clearly state one way or the other.  This choice is suboptimal though, as the statistical power of this test is greatly reduced by only looking at the worst lines.   Individual lines can have more frequent outliers and the test thresholds need to be broadened to keep the number of false alarms within acceptable levels.

One could claim that this choice gives better insight into the behavior of a particular line, however such reasoning is not consistent with the construction of the other tests.  For instance, the adaptive proportion test sums statistics over all four lines.  This adaptive proportion test in principle could be implemented to detect defects in single RNG lines, taking min and max statistics across all four lines, but this is not what has been done in the implementation of the adaptive proportion test.

I recommend we:
1. Switch the implementation of the Markov Test to take the _sum_ over all four channels, to 
    a. get the most resolution from the statistics and 
    b. make the test more in line with the Adaptive Proportion test, and
2. Expand the specification to make our choices and motivations more clear (perhaps including some of the text above).

#!/bin/bash
cd /home/opentitan || exit 1

TEST_NAME="entropy_src_threshold_scope_smoke"
SCRATCH_ROOT="/home/opentitan/.tb_entropy_src_threshold_scope"

# Inject the THRESHOLD_SCOPE stimulus into the existing smoke test so both
# baseline and fixed runs exercise the same real DV flow.
python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path

path = Path("/home/opentitan/hw/ip/entropy_src/dv/tests/entropy_src_smoke_test.sv")
text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
if "ht_threshold_scope_pct" not in text:
    lines = text.splitlines()
    for idx, line in enumerate(lines):
        if "entropy_data_reg_enable_pct" not in line or "=" not in line:
            continue
        indent = line[: len(line) - len(line.lstrip())]
        prefix = "cfg.dut_cfg." if "cfg.dut_cfg." in line else "cfg."
        lines.insert(idx + 1, f"{indent}{prefix}ht_threshold_scope_pct      = 100;")
        path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        break
    else:
        raise SystemExit("Failed to locate entropy_data_reg_enable_pct assignment in entropy_src_smoke_test.sv")
PY

set +e
timeout 1700 ./util/dvsim/dvsim.py hw/ip/entropy_src/dv/entropy_src_sim_cfg.hjson \
  -i entropy_src_smoke \
  -t vcs \
  --local \
  --max-parallel 1 \
  --scratch-root "${SCRATCH_ROOT}" \
  --fixed-seed 1 \
  --no-rerun \
  --purge
rc=$?

echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_START"
if [ "${rc}" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "TEST: ${TEST_NAME} ... PASS"
else
  echo "TEST: ${TEST_NAME} ... FAIL"
fi
echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"

exit "${rc}"

    echo "[INFO] apt-requirements.txt is empty after filtering comments"

  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
else
  echo "[WARN] apt-requirements.txt not found at base_sha; skipping repo-specific apt install"
fi

# Stage 3: install project-specific Python dependencies from the checked-out repo
if [[ -f python-requirements.txt ]]; then

  python -m pip install -U pip "setuptools<66.0.0"
  cp python-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
  python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re

path = Path("/tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt")

for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
    stripped = line.strip()
    if stripped in {
        "types-dataclasses",

path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

  echo "[WARN] util/get-toolchain.py not found at base_sha; skipping RISC-V toolchain install"

problem_statement:
## Description
OpenTitan's ENTROPY_SRC IP runs Adaptive Proportion and Markov health tests over multi-line random number generator (RNG) input windows. The `CONF.THRESHOLD_SCOPE` field is intended to make both tests use the same interpretation of a window. When this field is enabled, both tests should treat the four RNG lines as one combined stream for thresholding and for the reported test counts.

## Expected Behavior
With multi-line RNG input active and `CONF.THRESHOLD_SCOPE` enabled, both the Adaptive Proportion test and the Markov test must compare a single aggregate count, summed across all RNG lines in the window, against their configured high and low thresholds. The reported high and low counts for each test must reflect that same aggregate-by-sum interpretation.

## Actual Behavior
The two health tests do not honor `CONF.THRESHOLD_SCOPE` consistently. The Adaptive Proportion test already behaves as an aggregate-by-sum check, but the Markov test still evaluates each RNG line separately and derives its high and low results from per-line extrema. As a result, enabling `CONF.THRESHOLD_SCOPE` does not actually make both tests operate on the same scope, and the Markov test's threshold comparisons and reported counts do not match the configured mode.

## Affected Function
The bug affects the ENTROPY_SRC health-test logic for the Adaptive Proportion and Markov tests, specifically the logic that applies `CONF.THRESHOLD_SCOPE` to multi-line RNG windows.

## Trigger Condition
The mismatch appears when software enables `CONF.THRESHOLD_SCOPE` while ENTROPY_SRC is processing normal multi-line RNG input rather than single-lane mode.

## Implementation Constraint
The implementation should provide the software-visible control `CONF.THRESHOLD_SCOPE`, and the DV/config layer should expose a corresponding threshold-scope enable token named `ht_threshold_scope_pct` so tests can force this mode on.

resolved_issues.title: [ibex, epmp] Set reset values for ePMP CSRs
resolved_issues.body:
Currently all ePMP CSRs are set to 0 when the device is reset. Ideally I think we should have a more locked down configuration encoded in the reset logic. I see a couple of options for the reset logic (we could also combine them):

1. Specify a single PMP entry which makes eFlash read-only or totally inaccessible at reset (i.e. hard code entry 5 in [memory protection](https://docs.opentitan.org/sw/device/silicon_creator/mask_rom/docs/memory_protection/) into the reset logic).

    | Entry | Address Space | Encoding | Permissions |
    |-|-|-|-|
    | 5 | eFlash | NAPOT | L or LR |

2. Specify PMP entries for the ROM (RX) and MMIO (RW) address spaces and lock down all other accesses using either a final locked NAPOT region disabling all other access to the entire address space or by enabling MMWP.

    | Entry | Address Space | Encoding | Permissions |
    |-|-|-|-|
    | 2 | ROM | NAPOT | LRX |
    | 11 | MMIO | TOR (or NAPOT) | LRW |
    | 15? | All | NAPOT | L (no access) |

I prefer option 1 since it is simpler while still preventing premature execution of eFlash. It also means that the test ROM can easily disable memory protection and therefore existing test behavior can be retained for the time being.

TB_DIR=/home/opentitan/.tb_ibex_epmp_reset_values
COMPILE_LOG="$TB_DIR/compile.log"
RUN_LOG="$TB_DIR/run.log"

report_result() {
  local status="$1"
  echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_START"
  echo "TEST: $TEST_NAME ... $status"
  echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"
}

rm -rf "$TB_DIR"
mkdir -p "$TB_DIR"

cat > "$TB_DIR/epmp_reset_tb.sv" <<'SV'
module epmp_reset_tb;
  import ibex_pkg::*;

  logic clk_i = 1'b0;
  logic rst_ni = 1'b0;

  pmp_cfg_t     csr_pmp_cfg   [16];
  logic [33:0]  csr_pmp_addr  [16];
  pmp_mseccfg_t csr_pmp_mseccfg;

  always #5 clk_i = ~clk_i;

  task automatic fail(input string msg);
    begin
      $display("CHECK_FAIL: %s", msg);
      $fatal(1);
    end
  endtask

  ibex_cs_registers #(
    .PMPEnable      (1'b1),
    .PMPGranularity (0),
    .PMPNumRegions  (16)
  ) dut (
    .clk_i                       (clk_i),

    .priv_mode_id_o              (),
    .priv_mode_lsu_o             (),
    .csr_mstatus_tw_o            (),
    .csr_mtvec_o                 (),
    .csr_mtvec_init_i            (1'b0),
    .boot_addr_i                 (32'h0),
    .csr_access_i                (1'b0),
    .csr_addr_i                  (ibex_pkg::csr_num_e'(12'h000)),
    .csr_wdata_i                 (32'h0),
    .csr_op_i                    (ibex_pkg::csr_op_e'(0)),
    .csr_op_en_i                 (1'b0),
    .csr_rdata_o                 (),
    .irq_software_i              (1'b0),
    .irq_timer_i                 (1'b0),
    .irq_external_i              (1'b0),
    .irq_fast_i                  (15'h0),
    .nmi_mode_i                  (1'b0),
    .irq_pending_o               (),
    .irqs_o                      (),
    .csr_mstatus_mie_o           (),
    .csr_mepc_o                  (),
    .csr_pmp_cfg_o               (csr_pmp_cfg),
    .csr_pmp_addr_o              (csr_pmp_addr),
    .csr_pmp_mseccfg_o           (csr_pmp_mseccfg),
    .debug_mode_i                (1'b0),
    .debug_cause_i               (ibex_pkg::dbg_cause_e'(0)),
    .debug_csr_save_i            (1'b0),
    .csr_depc_o                  (),
    .debug_single_step_o         (),
    .debug_ebreakm_o             (),
    .debug_ebreaku_o             (),
    .trigger_match_o             (),
    .pc_if_i                     (32'h0),
    .pc_id_i                     (32'h0),

    .dummy_instr_seed_en_o       (),
    .dummy_instr_seed_o          (),
    .icache_enable_o             (),
    .csr_shadow_err_o            (),
    .csr_save_if_i               (1'b0),
    .csr_save_id_i               (1'b0),
    .csr_save_wb_i               (1'b0),
    .csr_restore_mret_i          (1'b0),
    .csr_restore_dret_i          (1'b0),
    .csr_save_cause_i            (1'b0),
    .csr_mcause_i                (ibex_pkg::exc_cause_e'(0)),
    .csr_mtval_i                 (32'h0),
    .illegal_csr_insn_o          (),
    .double_fault_seen_o         (),
    .instr_ret_i                 (1'b0),
    .instr_ret_compressed_i      (1'b0),
    .instr_ret_spec_i            (1'b0),

         csr_pmp_cfg[11].write, csr_pmp_cfg[11].read} !==

                     csr_pmp_cfg[11].lock, csr_pmp_cfg[11].mode,
                     csr_pmp_cfg[11].exec, csr_pmp_cfg[11].write, csr_pmp_cfg[11].read));
    end

    if (csr_pmp_addr[11] !== 34'h42010000) begin
      fail($sformatf("region11 addr mismatch: got %h", csr_pmp_addr[11]));
    end

    if ({csr_pmp_mseccfg.rlb, csr_pmp_mseccfg.mmwp, csr_pmp_mseccfg.mml} !== 3'b110) begin
      fail($sformatf("mseccfg mismatch: got rlb=%0b mmwp=%0b mml=%0b",
                     csr_pmp_mseccfg.rlb, csr_pmp_mseccfg.mmwp, csr_pmp_mseccfg.mml));
    end

    $display("RUNTIME_CHECK_PASSED");
    $finish;
  end
endmodule
SV

cat > "$TB_DIR/files.f" <<'EOF'
+incdir+/home/opentitan/hw/ip/prim/rtl
+incdir+/home/opentitan/hw/vendor/lowrisc_ibex/rtl
+incdir+/home/opentitan/hw/ip/rv_core_ibex/rtl
/home/opentitan/hw/vendor/lowrisc_ibex/rtl/ibex_pkg.sv
/home/opentitan/hw/vendor/lowrisc_ibex/rtl/ibex_csr.sv
/home/opentitan/hw/vendor/lowrisc_ibex/rtl/ibex_counter.sv
/home/opentitan/hw/vendor/lowrisc_ibex/rtl/ibex_cs_registers.sv
/home/opentitan/.tb_ibex_epmp_reset_values/epmp_reset_tb.sv
EOF

# Work around the VCS wrapper's host-kernel detection on this image.
export VCS_ARCH_OVERRIDE=linux
vcs -full64 -sverilog -timescale=1ns/1ps -assert svaext +define+IBEX_CUSTOM_PMP_RESET_VALUES \
  -Mdir="$TB_DIR/csrc" -f "$TB_DIR/files.f" -o "$TB_DIR/simv" -l "$COMPILE_LOG"
compile_rc=$?
if [ $compile_rc -ne 0 ]; then
  tail -n 200 "$COMPILE_LOG"
  report_result FAIL
  exit $compile_rc
fi

"$TB_DIR/simv" | tee "$RUN_LOG"
run_rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
# VCS can still exit 0 after $fatal in this flow, so require an explicit
# success marker from the testbench before reporting PASS.
if [ $run_rc -eq 0 ] && grep -q "RUNTIME_CHECK_PASSED" "$RUN_LOG"; then
  report_result PASS
  exit 0
fi

tail -n 200 "$RUN_LOG"
report_result FAIL
exit 1

problem_statement:
## Description
OpenTitan relies on the Ibex CPU's enhanced Physical Memory Protection (ePMP) reset state to provide a secure default access policy before the mask ROM writes any PMP Control and Status Registers (CSRs). In the affected implementation, when OpenTitan-specific custom PMP reset values are enabled, deasserting reset still leaves the PMP configuration in the architectural all-zero state: no ROM entry is present, no Memory-Mapped I/O (MMIO) window is defined, and the machine security configuration (`mseccfg`) policy bits remain cleared.

## Expected Behavior
Immediately after reset, before any boot code modifies the PMP CSRs, the hardware reset state must already expose the OpenTitan reset policy. PMP entry 2 must describe the ROM window `0x0000_8000-0x0000_FFFF` as a locked NAPOT (Naturally Aligned Power Of Two) read/execute region. PMP entries 10 and 11 must form a TOR (Top Of Range) MMIO window from `0x4000_0000` up to `0x4201_0000` with read/write permission. The `mseccfg` register must reset to `RLB=1`, `MMWP=1`, `MML=0`, where RLB is Rule Locking Bypass, MMWP is Machine Mode Whitelist Policy, and MML is Machine Mode Lockdown. With that reset state, machine-mode accesses outside the declared reset-time regions are blocked until software intentionally reconfigures PMP.

## Actual Behavior
After reset, the PMP reset state is effectively empty: the relevant PMP entries remain OFF, their reset addresses stay at zero, and `mseccfg` remains `RLB=0`, `MMWP=0`, `MML=0`. As a result, the ROM and MMIO regions are not predeclared in hardware, and unmatched machine-mode accesses are still allowed until later software writes the PMP CSRs.

## Affected Functionality
The affected functionality is the OpenTitan-specific ePMP reset-default path for the Ibex CPU, namely the hardware-provided PMP state that should be visible immediately after reset and before mask ROM initialization runs.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered immediately after reset deassertion in builds that enable PMP and OpenTitan's custom Ibex PMP reset values, before the mask ROM or test ROM programs any PMP/ePMP CSRs.

resolved_issues.title: [entropy_src] Timing issues in FW_OV "Insert Entropy" feature
resolved_issues.body:
__Summary:__
The FW_OV "insert_entropy" feature is currently unusable, due to three issues described below.
Some implicit assumptions have been made that inserted entropy is always ready at the same time as the Raw incoming RNG data.   FW cannot synchronize with the `main_sm` to insert processed entropy at the correct time.

__Background on this Feature:__
This feature is provided to allow firmware to override many key hardware features of the `entropy_src`.  In this mode:
1. Raw RNG data is to be fed to FW, which then performs it's own health checks.
2. FW examines the RNG data and returns known good data into the `FW_OV_WR_DATA` register
3. Ideally FW should have the option to push data through the SHA3 conditioner, _or_ pass already-conditioned data back directly to CSRNG (bypassing hardware conditioning).
4. Hardware Health tests _may_ still process the raw RNG data and record status, however failed hardware health checks should not cause the IP to discard data or trigger any alerts.

__Problem 1:__
The `main_sm` controls most aspects of the data pipeline, and the `main_sm` is in turn driven by the timing of the internal health tests.   The core around the hardware health tests issues pulses to advance the `main_sm` state.   The `main_sm` in turn issues pulses to SHA3 to process the final message (in non-bypass mode), and to the `esfinal` fifo to control the timing of data loads.   Meanwhile the loading of the SHA3 message is controlled by the general flow of data, either from the RNG or the `FW_OV_WR_DATA` register.

The timing of the SHA3 "process" command is outside of firmware's control.   The `main_sm` could even send a "process" command before FW inserts _any_ entropy.  Meanwhile, long bursts of FW writes could result in dropped data.

__Problem 2:__
Even in bypass mode, the `main_stage_push` signal which controls the `esfinal_fifo` is only asserted if there is a passing health check.  This violates requirement 4 above.

__Problem 3:__
There is no way for firmware to know when it is safe to write `FW_OV_WR_DATA` to prevent dropped data.

#!/bin/bash
set -e

cd /home/opentitan
git reset --hard
git clean -fdx
git checkout b3a4b12f1ca121ea996dad9b2f3683c10731b442

problem_statement:
## Description
The Entropy Source (`entropy_src`) IP has a synchronization bug in its firmware override (`FW_OV`) `insert_entropy` flow when firmware routes inserted entropy through the SHA3 conditioner instead of bypassing conditioning. In this feature, firmware receives raw random number generator (RNG) data, decides which data is acceptable, and writes the selected data back to the hardware for conditioning. The entropy source main state machine (`main_sm`), implemented in the `entropy_src_main_sm` submodule, does not stay aligned with firmware's timing for that transfer.

## Affected Function
The affected logic is the non-bypass firmware-override insert-entropy sequence in `entropy_src_main_sm`, including the transition from idle into firmware insertion, the start of the SHA3 conditioning flow, the handoff from message loading to SHA3 processing, and completion of the transfer back to the idle state.

## Expected Behavior
When firmware override `insert_entropy` is used in the non-bypass path, the Entropy Source must behave as a firmware-driven handshake. After the block enters firmware insertion mode, SHA3 must remain idle until firmware explicitly starts the transfer. The state machine must stay in the firmware insertion phase while firmware is still supplying the message, begin SHA3 processing only after the firmware-supplied message is complete, and, once the conditioned result is accepted by the final entropy stage, complete the operation and return to idle.

## Actual Behavior
The current `main_sm` still follows timing assumptions from the normal hardware-managed entropy pipeline. As a result, SHA3 start and later SHA3 processing can advance according to internal pipeline timing instead of firmware timing. In firmware override `insert_entropy` mode, the state machine can leave the firmware insertion phase, or begin or finalize the SHA3 sequence, before firmware has cleanly synchronized the transfer and finished supplying the message.

## Trigger Condition
This occurs when the Entropy Source is enabled in firmware override `insert_entropy` mode, the inserted entropy is routed through the SHA3 conditioner instead of bypass mode, and firmware initiates an insertion while the block is otherwise idle.

## Implementation Constraint
The firmware-override insert-entropy path should expose control inputs using the exact tokens `fw_ov_ent_insert_i` and `fw_ov_sha3_start_i`, so the main state machine can distinguish firmware-insert activity from the normal startup / SHA3 sequencing.
