#!/bin/bash
set -e

# Stage 1: checkout base_sha in a clean workspace (+submodules)
cd /home/opentitan
git reset --hard
git clean -fdx
git checkout 87c41e52d089527095e7df84931df5f2a550f3ce
git submodule update --init --recursive

# Stage 2: install repository apt dependencies (if present)
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
if [[ -f apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing apt dependencies from apt-requirements.txt"
  cp apt-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  sed -i -e '/^$/d' -e '/^#/d' -e 's/#.*//' /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  if [[ -s /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
    apt-get update
    xargs -r apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends < /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
  else
    echo "[INFO] apt-requirements.txt is empty after filtering comments"
  fi
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
else
  echo "[WARN] apt-requirements.txt not found at 87c41e52d089527095e7df84931df5f2a550f3ce; skipping repo-specific apt install"
fi

# Stage 3: install project-specific Python dependencies from the checked-out repo
if [[ -f python-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Python deps from python-requirements.txt"
  python -m pip install -U pip "setuptools<66.0.0"
  cp python-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
  python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re

path = Path("/tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt")
lines = []
for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
    stripped = line.strip()
    if stripped in {
        "types-dataclasses",
        "types-pkg_resources",
    }:
        continue
    line = re.sub(r'(#egg=[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)\s+[<>=!~].*', r'\1', line)
    lines.append(line)
path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
PY
  python -m pip install -r /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt --no-warn-script-location
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
else
  echo "[ERROR] python-requirements.txt not found at 87c41e52d089527095e7df84931df5f2a550f3ce"
  exit 1
fi

# Stage 4: install RISC-V toolchain, and keep Verible install best-effort
if [[ -f util/get-toolchain.py ]]; then
  toolchain_version=""
  if [[ -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
    toolchain_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
  fi

  echo "[INFO] Installing RISC-V toolchain via util/get-toolchain.py"
  if [[ -n "$toolchain_version" ]]; then
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update -r "$toolchain_version"
  else
    echo "[WARN] RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION not found; falling back to util/get-toolchain.py defaults"
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update
  fi
else
  echo "[WARN] util/get-toolchain.py not found at 87c41e52d089527095e7df84931df5f2a550f3ce; skipping RISC-V toolchain install"
fi

verible_version=""
if [[ -f hw/tool_requirements.py ]]; then
  verible_version="$(python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path

ns = {}
exec(Path("hw/tool_requirements.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8"), ns)
reqs = ns.get("__TOOL_REQUIREMENTS__", {})
entry = reqs.get("verible", "")
if isinstance(entry, dict):
    print(entry.get("min_version", ""))
elif isinstance(entry, str):
    print(entry)
PY
)"
fi
if [[ -z "$verible_version" && -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
  verible_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG VERIBLE_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
fi

if [[ -n "$verible_version" ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Verible ${verible_version} (best-effort)"
  rm -rf /tools/verible
  mkdir -p /tools/verible
  if curl -f -Ls -o /tmp/verible.tar.gz \
      "https://github.com/chipsalliance/verible/releases/download/${verible_version}/verible-${verible_version}-linux-static-x86_64.tar.gz"; then
    tar -C /tools/verible -xf /tmp/verible.tar.gz --strip-components=1
    rm -f /tmp/verible.tar.gz
  else
    echo "[WARN] Verible download failed for ${verible_version}; continuing without Verible"
    rm -f /tmp/verible.tar.gz
  fi
else
  echo "[WARN] Unable to determine Verible version from hw/tool_requirements.py or util/container/Dockerfile"
fi

cat > /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh <<'EOF'
for d in /tools/riscv/bin /tools/verible/bin; do
  [ -d "$d" ] && export PATH="$d:$PATH"
done
EOF

if [[ -f /etc/opentitan_bash_env ]]; then
  if ! grep -q "/etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh" /etc/opentitan_bash_env; then
    echo "source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh" >> /etc/opentitan_bash_env
  fi
else
  echo "source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh" > /etc/opentitan_bash_env
fi
source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh || true

if ! python -m pip show edalize fusesoc hjson >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[WARN] Python package sanity check failed; continuing with installed environment"
fi

if command -v riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  toolchain_banner="$(riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc --version 2>/dev/null || true)"
  toolchain_banner="${toolchain_banner%%$'\n'*}"
  if [[ -n "$toolchain_banner" ]]; then
    echo "[INFO] RISC-V toolchain ready: ${toolchain_banner}"
  else
    echo "[INFO] RISC-V toolchain ready"
  fi
else
  echo "[WARN] riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc not found after Stage 4"

problem_statement:
## Description
The bug affects the TL-UL (TileLink Uncached Lightweight) crossbar's `socket_1n` 1:N fanout path. A host-to-device request that is routed to one downstream device can still expose request payload information on the other, unselected device ports, which defeats the intended address-based blanking in the crossbar.

## Expected Behavior
When `socket_1n` routes a request to one downstream device, the selected port must see the original request unchanged. Every unselected port must keep `a_valid` low, replace the request data (`a_data`) with the all-ones blanking value, and must not reuse the original command/data integrity carried in the request user metadata (`a_user`). Unrelated `a_user` metadata may remain unchanged, but the integrity fields on an unselected port must be invalid so downstream logic cannot accept the blanked transfer as a legitimate command. Using an all-ones blanking value is important because zeroing the payload could create a usable multi-bit boolean (MUBI) disable value in security-sensitive registers.

## Actual Behavior
Unselected downstream ports suppress `a_valid`, but they still carry the original host request payload. In particular, an unselected device can observe the live `a_data` and the original, valid-looking integrity metadata in `a_user` from a request that is actually addressed to a different device.

## Trigger Condition
The problem appears on a host-to-device write routed through the TL-UL crossbar when one downstream device is selected and at least one other device port is unselected. In that case, the selected device should receive the original request, while the other ports should observe only the blanked payload.

problem_statement:
## Description
The KMAC (Keccak Message Authentication Code) IP exposes an entropy refresh threshold that controls after how many hash operations the block should request a new entropy seed from the EDN (Entropy Distribution Network). This threshold is configuration state and is intended to be protected by shadowed control and status register (CSR) semantics.

## Expected Behavior
The KMAC entropy refresh threshold CSR must behave as a shadowed register. After the first write of an update sequence, software should still read back the previously committed threshold value. The new threshold should become visible only after a second matching write completes the shadowed update.

## Actual Behavior
In the affected implementation, the entropy refresh threshold behaves like a normal writable CSR field instead of a shadowed one. After a single write, software can immediately read back the new threshold value even though the confirming second write has not occurred.

## Affected Function
This affects the KMAC CSR block's entropy refresh threshold configuration register, which controls the threshold used for requesting fresh entropy from the EDN.

## Trigger Condition
The bug appears when firmware updates the entropy refresh threshold while configuration writes are enabled but stops after the first write of the shadowed-register sequence. A read performed after that first write returns the new value instead of the previously committed threshold.

problem_statement:
## Description
The bug is in the OpenTitan Flash Controller IP's flash PHY erase-control path (`flash_phy_erase`), which mediates erase and erase-suspend requests between the controller and the underlying flash primitive. After an erase request has already been accepted and the erase is in progress, the erase-suspend request does not follow the documented suspend-handshake behavior.

## Expected Behavior
Once an erase operation is busy, an incoming erase-suspend request must be forwarded to the flash primitive so the primitive can acknowledge the suspend request. The suspend handshake and erase completion are separate, observable events: the suspend request is consumed when the flash side acknowledges it, while the controller-facing completion acknowledge must be generated only when the flash later reports that the erase operation is done.

## Actual Behavior
The current erase-control path does not preserve that separation. The suspend request is effectively tied to the later erase-complete indication instead of being handled as an acknowledge-based handshake while the erase is still active, so the suspend behavior is inconsistent with the documented flash interface.

## Trigger Condition
The problem is triggered when an erase request has already been accepted and is still busy, and an erase-suspend request arrives before the erase completes, especially when the flash side acknowledges the suspend request before it raises the erase-done indication.

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

cd /home/opentitan

TEST_NAME="rom_ctrl_kmac_valid_hold_chk"
SCRATCH_ROOT="/home/opentitan/.tb_${TEST_NAME}"

python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path

vseq = """// Copyright lowRISC contributors.
// Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0, see LICENSE for details.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

class rom_ctrl_kmac_valid_hold_chk_vseq extends rom_ctrl_base_vseq;
  `uvm_object_utils(rom_ctrl_kmac_valid_hold_chk_vseq)

  `uvm_object_new

  localparam string KmacReadyPath = "tb.kmac_app_if.req_data_if.ready_int";
  localparam string KmacValidPath = "tb.kmac_data_out.valid";
  localparam string FsmStatePath =
      "tb.dut.gen_fsm_scramble_enabled.u_checker_fsm.state_q";

  task body();
    bit valid;
    bit saw_valid;

    $assertoff(0, "tb.dut.KeymgrValidChk_A");
    $assertoff(0, "tb.kmac_app_if.req_data_if.H_DataStableWhenValidAndNotReady_A");

    if (!uvm_hdl_force(KmacReadyPath, 1'b0)) begin
      `uvm_fatal(`gfn, $sformatf("Failed to force %s", KmacReadyPath))
    end

    repeat (100) begin
      @(posedge cfg.clk_rst_vif.clk);
      if (!uvm_hdl_read(KmacValidPath, valid)) begin
        `uvm_fatal(`gfn, $sformatf("Failed to read %s", KmacValidPath))
      end
      if (valid) begin
        saw_valid = 1'b1;
        break;
      end
    end
    if (!saw_valid) begin
      `uvm_fatal(`gfn, "Timed out waiting for a pending KMAC beat")
    end

    @(negedge cfg.clk_rst_vif.clk);
    if (!uvm_hdl_force(FsmStatePath, rom_ctrl_pkg::Invalid)) begin
      `uvm_fatal(`gfn, $sformatf("Failed to force %s", FsmStatePath))
    end
    @(posedge cfg.clk_rst_vif.clk);
    if (!uvm_hdl_release(FsmStatePath)) begin
      `uvm_fatal(`gfn, $sformatf("Failed to release %s", FsmStatePath))
    end

    repeat (3) begin
      @(posedge cfg.clk_rst_vif.clk);
      if (!uvm_hdl_read(KmacValidPath, valid)) begin
        `uvm_fatal(`gfn, $sformatf("Failed to read %s", KmacValidPath))
      end
      if (!valid) begin
        `uvm_fatal(`gfn, "KMAC valid dropped before ready after injected fault")
      end
    end

    if (!uvm_hdl_release(KmacReadyPath)) begin
      `uvm_fatal(`gfn, $sformatf("Failed to release %s", KmacReadyPath))
    end

    repeat (10) @(posedge cfg.clk_rst_vif.clk);
    dut_init();

    $asserton(0, "tb.kmac_app_if.req_data_if.H_DataStableWhenValidAndNotReady_A");
    $asserton(0, "tb.dut.KeymgrValidChk_A");
  endtask : body

endclass : rom_ctrl_kmac_valid_hold_chk_vseq
"""

vseq_path = Path("hw/ip/rom_ctrl/dv/env/seq_lib/rom_ctrl_kmac_valid_hold_chk_vseq.sv")
vseq_path.write_text(vseq, encoding="utf-8")

core_path = Path("hw/ip/rom_ctrl/dv/env/rom_ctrl_env.core")
core_text = core_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
core_entry = "      - seq_lib/rom_ctrl_kmac_valid_hold_chk_vseq.sv: {is_include_file: true}\n"
if core_entry not in core_text:
    anchor = "      - seq_lib/rom_ctrl_kmac_err_chk_vseq.sv: {is_include_file: true}\n"
    if anchor not in core_text:
        raise SystemExit("Missing rom_ctrl_env.core anchor for custom vseq")
    core_text = core_text.replace(anchor, anchor + core_entry)
    core_path.write_text(core_text, encoding="utf-8")

list_path = Path("hw/ip/rom_ctrl/dv/env/seq_lib/rom_ctrl_vseq_list.sv")
list_text = list_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
list_entry = '`include "rom_ctrl_kmac_valid_hold_chk_vseq.sv"\n'
if list_entry not in list_text:
    anchor = '`include "rom_ctrl_kmac_err_chk_vseq.sv"\n'
    if anchor not in list_text:
        raise SystemExit("Missing rom_ctrl_vseq_list.sv anchor for custom vseq")
    list_text = list_text.replace(anchor, anchor + list_entry)
    list_path.write_text(list_text, encoding="utf-8")
PY

mkdir -p "${SCRATCH_ROOT}"

set +e
./util/dvsim/dvsim.py hw/ip/rom_ctrl/dv/rom_ctrl_sim_cfg.hjson \
  -i rom_ctrl_smoke \
  -t vcs \
  --fixed-seed 1 \
  --reseed 1 \
  --scratch-root "${SCRATCH_ROOT}" \
  --run-opts "+UVM_TEST_SEQ=rom_ctrl_kmac_valid_hold_chk_vseq +en_scb=0"
rc=$?
set -e

echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_START"
if [ "${rc}" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "TEST: ${TEST_NAME} ... PASS"
else
  echo "TEST: ${TEST_NAME} ... FAIL"
fi
echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"

exit "${rc}"

problem_statement:
## Description
OpenTitan's ROM controller (`rom_ctrl`) sends boot ROM data to KMAC (Keccak Message Authentication Code) while verifying the boot ROM digest. The `rom_ctrl`-to-KMAC data path uses a ready/valid handshake: once `valid` is asserted for a data beat, that beat remains pending until KMAC accepts it with `ready`.

## Affected Function
The affected logic is the `rom_ctrl` checker path that drives ROM data beats from `rom_ctrl` to KMAC during digest verification.

## Expected Behavior
If `rom_ctrl` has already asserted `valid` for a ROM data beat and KMAC is holding `ready` low, `rom_ctrl` must keep `valid` asserted for that same pending beat until KMAC accepts it. Detecting a fault may prevent new transfers, but it must not withdraw a beat that has already been presented on the interface.

## Actual Behavior
If `rom_ctrl` detects a fault while a beat is pending on the KMAC interface, it can drop `valid` before KMAC raises `ready` and accepts the beat. This violates the ready/valid protocol on the `rom_ctrl`-to-KMAC interface.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered during boot ROM digest verification when `rom_ctrl` has already presented a data beat to KMAC, KMAC is not yet accepting that beat because `ready` is low, and `rom_ctrl` detects a fault before the handshake completes.

title: [clkmgr, top] clkmgr and top updates to support ast external switch
body:
Review last commit only.

- ast provides a direct indication whether clock dividers should be stepped
  down during an external switch.

- clkmgr can make use of this mechanism directly without having to piece
  separate logic together.

- This PR may be incomplete at the moment because the relevant signals are
  in an async domain, this may be changed by an AST update.

fixes #10890

repo.name: opentitan
repo.description: OpenTitan: Open source silicon root of trust

commits.message:
[clkmgr, top] clkmgr and top updates to better support ast external clock

- ast provides a direct indication whether clock dividers should be stepped
  down during an external switch.

- clkmgr can make use of this mechanism directly without having to piece
  separate logic together.

- This PR may be incomplete at the moment because the relevant signals are
  in an async domain, this may be changed by an AST update.

Signed-off-by: Timothy Chen <timothytim@google.com>

#!/bin/bash
cd /home/opentitan
set +e

TB_NAME="chip_sw_uart_tx_rx_alt_clk_freq_low_speed"
SCRATCH_ROOT="/home/opentitan/.tb_chip_uart_extclk_low_speed"
RUN_LOG="/home/opentitan/.tb_chip_uart_extclk_low_speed/dvsim.log"

mkdir -p "$SCRATCH_ROOT"

./util/dvsim/dvsim.py hw/top_earlgrey/dv/chip_sim_cfg.hjson \
  -i chip_sw_uart_tx_rx_alt_clk_freq_low_speed \
  -t vcs \
  --fixed-seed 1 \
  --reseed 1 \
  --scratch-root "$SCRATCH_ROOT" \
  >"$RUN_LOG" 2>&1
rc=$?

if [ $rc -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_START"
  echo "TEST: ${TB_NAME} ... PASS"
  echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"
else
  echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_START"
  echo "TEST: ${TB_NAME} ... FAIL"
  echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"
fi

tail -n 200 "$RUN_LOG" 2>/dev/null
exit $rc
prepare_script:
#!/bin/bash
set -e

# Stage 1: checkout base_sha in a clean workspace (+submodules)
cd /home/opentitan
git reset --hard
git clean -fdx
git checkout 291d911f3bc8d4c2cc00628ca493eb6d32b7722c
git submodule update --init --recursive

# Stage 2: install repository apt dependencies (if present)
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
if [[ -f apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing apt dependencies from apt-requirements.txt"
  cp apt-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  sed -i -e '/^$/d' -e '/^#/d' -e 's/#.*//' /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  if [[ -s /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
    apt-get update
    xargs -r apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends < /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends dc time
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
  else
    echo "[INFO] apt-requirements.txt is empty after filtering comments"
  fi
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
else
  echo "[WARN] apt-requirements.txt not found at base_sha; skipping repo-specific apt install"
fi

# Stage 3: install project-specific Python dependencies from the checked-out repo
if [[ -f python-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Python deps from python-requirements.txt"
  python -m pip install -U pip "setuptools<66.0.0"
  cp python-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
  python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re

problem_statement:
OpenTitan's clock manager (`clkmgr`) can select the wrong divider setting for IO-derived clocks after a software-requested switch to an external clock. The affected logic is the external-clock bypass path for the IO clock, including the interface between `clkmgr` and the Analog Sensor Top (AST) clock source block that determines whether the external IO clock is running at nominal speed or in the low-speed 48 MHz mode.

When software enables the external clock in a life cycle state where this feature is allowed, such as the Return Merchandise Authorization (RMA) state, and requests the low-speed external IO clock, `clkmgr` must step down the internal IO dividers so that downstream clocks such as `clk_io_div2` and `clk_io_div4` stay at the same nominal frequencies they have in internal-clock mode. After the switch completes, IO-clocked peripherals must still observe the expected peripheral clock. In particular, UART communication after the switch must still be able to complete normal transmit and receive traffic at the configured baud rate.

Instead, the existing bypass logic can decide the divider step-down without reliably knowing whether the external IO clock is actually 48 MHz or nominal speed. This can leave the IO and peripheral clock tree in the wrong divide-by-2 versus divide-by-4 state after the external-clock switch. The bug is exposed in full-chip operation when software switches to the low-speed external clock and then continues to use an IO-clocked peripheral such as UART, which can fail because the peripheral clock no longer matches the expected frequency.

resolved_issues.body:
The debug spec requires the DMI CSR SBCS[SBACCESS] to be implemented as RW, but the design implements it as RO instead. 
See: https://github.com/riscv/riscv-debug-spec/raw/4e0bb0fc2d843473db2356623792c6b7603b94d4/riscv-debug-release.pdf
Page 43. 

The following logic 'overwrites' any changes made to `sbaccess`:
https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/60706c2b1f6b67da6dddbd2d6fb4e607f5ca0e2e/hw/vendor/pulp_riscv_dbg/src/dm_csrs.sv#L527

On line 431, it captures the data written to this field. 

The `dm_sba` appears to support sub-word accesses, as it sets the byte masks correctly. 

The end result is JTAG can only ever initiate 32-bit accesses over SBA.

problem_statement:
## Description
OpenTitan's RISC-V Debug Module (`rv_dm`) does not correctly support byte-sized System Bus Access (SBA) transactions issued through the Debug Module Interface (DMI). In the System Bus Access Control and Status (`SBCS`) register, the `SBACCESS` field is supposed to let a debugger select the access size for an SBA transaction, but in the current design that field is effectively forced back to the default 32-bit setting.

## Expected Behavior
After a debugger programs `SBCS.SBACCESS` for an 8-bit SBA transfer on a 32-bit system bus, the next SBA write must be issued as a byte transaction rather than a 32-bit word transaction. For example, an 8-bit write to address `0x1` must enable only byte lane 1, and the written byte must be aligned to that lane on the bus write data.

## Actual Behavior
The current `rv_dm` implementation behaves as if `SBCS.SBACCESS` were stuck at 32-bit access width. As a result, a debugger cannot trigger a true 8-bit SBA write: a write to address `0x1` behaves like a 32-bit access instead of a byte-lane-1 transaction.

## Affected Function
This bug is in the `rv_dm` IP, specifically the `SBCS` control path and the SBA request path that converts DMI-programmed debug transactions into system-bus writes.

## Trigger Condition
The bug appears when a debugger uses DMI to request an 8-bit SBA write on a 32-bit bus, especially when the target address is not word-aligned, such as address `0x1` within a 32-bit word.

problem_statement:
## Description
OpenTitan's Key Manager (keymgr) relies on the KMAC (Keccak Message Authentication Code) application interface to complete KMAC-backed key-derivation work. The bug is in the keymgr KMAC response handling: a `done` response from KMAC can arrive when keymgr has no outstanding KMAC-backed operation waiting for a response.

## Affected Function
The affected module is the keymgr KMAC response path and the keymgr fault-handling logic for asynchronous KMAC interface errors.

## Expected Behavior
A KMAC `done` indication is valid only while keymgr is actively waiting for the response to a previously issued KMAC-backed operation. If `done` is asserted while keymgr is idle or otherwise not expecting a response, keymgr must treat it as an asynchronous fatal fault. That fault must be reflected in keymgr's fault status, raise the fatal fault alert, and cause a subsequent keymgr advance operation to complete with a failure result rather than succeed; keymgr must enter its invalid state instead of continuing normal operation.

## Actual Behavior
A spurious KMAC `done` indication outside the valid response window can be ignored. As a result, keymgr may fail to report the asynchronous fault, and a later advance operation can proceed without being forced into the failed invalid-state outcome required after such a fault.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered when the KMAC response interface asserts `done` during an idle window, before keymgr has any outstanding KMAC-backed operation waiting for a response.

problem_statement:
## Description
The bug is in the OpenTitan key manager IP's controller logic for asynchronous fatal faults while the block is idle. After the key manager completes its advance into the initialized working state and no operation is active, an asynchronous fatal fault, such as a register-file integrity error, is recorded but does not immediately force the controller out of that state.

## Affected Function
The affected functionality is the key manager controller's idle-time fault handling path: how it reacts to an asynchronous fatal fault when no key manager operation is currently running.

## Expected Behavior
An asynchronous fatal fault must not wait for an operation boundary. If the key manager is idle in its initialized working state when such a fault arrives, the controller must latch the fault indication and immediately enter the `Invalid` working state, rather than remaining initialized until a later command, a later operation, or some other later event.

## Actual Behavior
When the controller is idle after initialization and a register-file integrity fault is asserted, the fault indication is recorded, but the controller can remain in the initialized working state instead of promptly transitioning to `Invalid`.

## Trigger Condition
Bring the key manager to its initialized idle state by letting its advance complete, then inject an asynchronous fatal fault on the register-file integrity path while no operation is active. This idle-fault case should immediately move the controller to `Invalid`, but the buggy behavior leaves it in the pre-fault state.

problem_statement:
## Description
The bug is in the OpenTitan Key Manager (`keymgr`) hardware block's alert interface. `keymgr` exposes two named alerts: the recoverable operation alert `recov_operation_err` and the fatal fault alert `fatal_fault_err`. These names are assigned to the wrong alert output indexes, so the named alert order does not match the physical alert outputs.

## Expected Behavior
`recov_operation_err` must be connected to the first `keymgr` alert output (alert index 0), and `fatal_fault_err` must be connected to the second `keymgr` alert output (alert index 1). When software writes the `recov_operation_err` bit in the `ALERT_TEST` register, only the recovery alert output should assert and the fatal alert output must remain deasserted.

## Actual Behavior
The two `keymgr` alert indexes are reversed. Forcing `recov_operation_err` through the `ALERT_TEST` register can assert alert index 1, which is the fatal alert output, while alert index 0 does not assert.

## Affected Function
The affected functionality is the `keymgr` alert definition and wiring, including the mapping between the named alerts in the register interface and the module's two alert outputs.

## Trigger Condition
The mismatch is observable when software forces the recovery alert by setting the `recov_operation_err` bit in the `ALERT_TEST` register.

title: [spi_device] Block the passthrough with BUSY status
body:
This commit addresses the issue #10785.

The BUSY @ SYS_CLK is set when SPI_DEVICE receives commands that satisfy:

- busy field in the CMD_INFO of the opcode is set
- CSb is de-asserted (SPI transaction completion)

When BUSY is set, SW may process the received command (assuming upload
field is set). After the command is processed by SW, SW may clear the
BUSY @SYS_CLK, which then will be propagated into SPI CLK (SCK) domain
at the next SPI transaction.

This commit is to turn off the passthrough interface if BUSY is set. So,
that the SW does not have to manually turn off the passthrough.

Keep in mind that this change cannot fully cover the corner cases:

- CSb is about to asserted (Beginning of the SPI transaction) at the
  same time BUSY is cleared by SW.

It is due to the CDC path of CSb to be used in SYS_CLK domain. It needs
to pass through 2FF synchronizer to be used in SYS_CLK safely. The delay
is 2 SYS_CLK. If BUSY falls in that window, the BUSY clearing may
unblock passthrough while SPI is active. The behavior of the IP is
undetermined.

diff --git a/hw/ip/spi_device/data/spi_device.hjson b/hw/ip/spi_device/data/spi_device.hjson
index c231f684b74b4..6b605b2908f8a 100644
--- a/hw/ip/spi_device/data/spi_device.hjson
+++ b/hw/ip/spi_device/data/spi_device.hjson
@@ -517,7 +517,8 @@
       fields: [
         { bits: "0"
           name: "busy"
-          desc: "BUSY"
+          desc: '''BUSY signal is cleared when CSb is high. SW should read
+            back the register to confirm the value is cleared.'''
           swaccess: "rw0c"
           hwaccess: "hrw"
           tags: [
diff --git a/hw/ip/spi_device/doc/_index.md b/hw/ip/spi_device/doc/_index.md
index 13b279c64f0cd..833a01a1fef85 100644
--- a/hw/ip/spi_device/doc/_index.md
+++ b/hw/ip/spi_device/doc/_index.md
@@ -410,6 +410,13 @@ Except BUSY bit, other bits are controlled by SW.
 BUSY bit is set by HW when it receives any commands that are uploaded to the FIFOs.
 SW may clear BUSY bit when it completes the received commands (e.g Erase/ Program).
 
+If BUSY is set, SPI_DEVICE IP blocks the passhthrough interface in Passthrough mode.
+The blocking of the interface occurs in SPI transaction idle state (CSb == 1).
+However, due to the instrinsic delay of the CDC, CSb transition is delayed by 2 SYS_CLK cycles.
+It may introduce a corner case when the host system starts sending a SPI transaction while SW may clear the BUSY signal.
+In that case, the blocking and unblocking of the passthrough may happen while SPI is active.
+The HW behavior in this scenario is not determined.
+
 If the host sends the Write Status commands, the commands are not processed in this module.
 SW must configure the remaining command information entries to upload the Write Status commands to the FIFOs.
 
diff --git a/hw/ip/spi_device/rtl/spi_device.sv b/hw/ip/spi_device/rtl/spi_device.sv
index 142b3fd5c31cb..79204f32753b7 100644
--- a/hw/ip/spi_device/rtl/spi_device.sv
+++ b/hw/ip/spi_device/rtl/spi_device.sv
@@ -1514,6 +1514,22 @@ module spi_device
   /////////////////////
   // SPI Passthrough //
   /////////////////////
+
+  // Passthrough block
+  // signal: sys_csb_syncd -> sysclock 2FF CSb
+  // signal: sys_busy  -> output of u_status readstatus_d[0]
+  //              set by CSb deassertion pulse & BUSY(SCK)
+  //              clr by CSb = 1 & SW writing 0
+  //
+  // NOTE: there will be a gap between the actual assertion of CSb and the CSb
+  //   syncd event visible in the u_status BUSY logic (2FF @ SYS_CLK). So,
+  //   there's chance that the SW may clear the BUSY right at the CSb
+  //   assertion event. If that happens, passthrough block may set during SPI
+  //   transaction. The behavior of the SPI_DEVICE in this scenario is
+  //   undeterminstic.
+  logic  sys_passthrough_block;
+  assign sys_passthrough_block = readstatus_d[0];
+
   spi_passthrough u_passthrough (
     .clk_i     (clk_spi_in_buf),
     .rst_ni    (rst_spi_n),
@@ -1534,6 +1550,9 @@ module spi_device
 
     .spi_mode_i       (spi_mode),
 
+    // Control: BUSY block
+    .passthrough_block_i (sys_passthrough_block),
+
     // Host SPI
     .host_sck_i  (cio_sck_i),
     .host_csb_i  (cio_csb_i),
diff --git a/hw/ip/spi_device/rtl/spi_passthrough.sv b/hw/ip/spi_device/rtl/spi_passthrough.sv
index 9d9df3e8b7427..25a078d3cccb9 100644
--- a/hw/ip/spi_device/rtl/spi_passthrough.sv
+++ b/hw/ip/spi_device/rtl/spi_passthrough.sv
@@ -100,6 +100,11 @@ module spi_passthrough
 
   input spi_mode_e spi_mode_i,
 
+  // Control: Passthrough block
+  //   If passthrough_block_i is 1, the passthrough is turned off.
+  //   The signal should be changed when CSb is high (SPI inactive).
+  input passthrough_block_i,
+
   // Command Info structure
   input cmd_info_t [NumTotalCmdInfo-1:0] cmd_info_i,
 
@@ -644,7 +649,7 @@ module spi_passthrough
   assign passthrough_o.csb    = host_csb_i | csb_deassert_outclk ;
 
   // passthrough_en
-  assign passthrough_o.passthrough_en = is_active ;
+  assign passthrough_o.passthrough_en = is_active && !passthrough_block_i;

problem_statement:
## Description
In the SPI Device IP, passthrough mode is not blocked when the IP raises its BUSY status after completing a command that is configured to be uploaded to software. A command-info (`CMD_INFO`) entry can mark an opcode as both `upload` and `busy`. After the external SPI host finishes that transaction and de-asserts chip select (`CSb`), the SPI Device sets BUSY to indicate that software must service the uploaded command. The passthrough path should then be disabled automatically, but it currently remains enabled.

## Expected Behavior
While the SPI Device is operating in passthrough mode, if a completed command with `CMD_INFO.upload = 1` and `CMD_INFO.busy = 1` causes BUSY to become set, the passthrough enable must be de-asserted during the idle period with `CSb` high. The passthrough interface must remain blocked while BUSY is set.

## Actual Behavior
BUSY is set after the matching command completes, but the passthrough enable signal remains asserted. As a result, the SPI Device still leaves the passthrough path enabled even though software is expected to handle the uploaded command.

## Affected Function
The bug affects the SPI Device IP's passthrough gating for BUSY handling, specifically the logic that should disable passthrough when a software-uploaded command leaves the IP busy.

## Trigger Condition
The failure occurs when the SPI Device is already in passthrough mode and the external SPI host sends a command whose `CMD_INFO` entry is valid and sets both `upload` and `busy`. When that SPI transaction completes and `CSb` returns high, BUSY becomes set, but passthrough is not blocked.

problem_statement:
## Description
The OpenTitan Key Manager (`keymgr`) issues one decoded command to its Keccak Message Authentication Code (`KMAC`) interface for each operation. For identity-generation and output-generation requests, that command is represented by a one-hot internal selection. Once a KMAC transaction has started, the in-flight command must remain identical to the command implied by the original software-programmed operation.

## Expected Behavior
After `keymgr` launches a KMAC transaction, the one-hot command delivered to the KMAC interface must stay unchanged until that transaction completes. In particular, if software starts an identity-generation operation (`OpGenId`), the in-flight request must remain an identity-generation request for the full transaction. If the command changes to a different legal one-hot value before completion, `keymgr` must treat this as a fatal command-consistency fault: the operation must end with `OP_STATUS` reporting failure, `FAULT_STATUS.CMD` set, and the key manager entering the terminal `Invalid` working state rather than accepting the altered command.

## Actual Behavior
In the buggy implementation, `keymgr` checks that the command is one-hot, but does not continuously verify that the active KMAC command still matches the command that started the transaction. A request can therefore begin as one legal command and later appear as a different legal one-hot command without triggering the fatal command-consistency fault. In that case, the operation is not forced onto the `OP_STATUS` failure, `FAULT_STATUS.CMD`, and `Invalid`-state path described above.

## Affected Function
This affects the `keymgr` KMAC command interface, specifically the in-flight command-consistency check for identity-generation and output-generation operations.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered when a valid generation request has already launched a KMAC transaction and, before KMAC signals completion, the internal one-hot command changes to a different legal command. A concrete failing case is an identity-generation request (`OpGenId`) whose in-flight KMAC command changes to a non-identity generate command while the transaction is still active.

problem_statement:
## Description
In OpenTitan Key Manager (`keymgr`), the control logic retains an internal working key in storage between commands. That retained working-key storage is not protected with error-correcting code (ECC). If a storage fault flips a bit in the retained working key while `keymgr` is idle, the corruption is not detected.

## Expected Behavior
The retained working-key storage in `keymgr` should be protected with ECC while the key is stored between operations. If the stored working key is corrupted, even when no new Key Manager command is running, `keymgr` must raise a fatal fault alert and transition its working state to `Invalid`.

## Actual Behavior
A bit flip in the retained working key while `keymgr` is idle can leave `keymgr` in a non-`Invalid` working state without raising a fatal fault alert.

diff --git a/hw/ip/lc_ctrl/rtl/lc_ctrl.sv b/hw/ip/lc_ctrl/rtl/lc_ctrl.sv

--- a/hw/ip/lc_ctrl/rtl/lc_ctrl.sv

@@ -711,6 +711,10 @@ module lc_ctrl

       u_lc_ctrl_fsm.u_fsm_state_regs, alert_tx_o[1])
+  `ASSERT_PRIM_FSM_ERROR_TRIGGER_ALERT(CtrlLcStateCheck_A,
+      u_lc_ctrl_fsm.u_state_regs, alert_tx_o[1])
+  `ASSERT_PRIM_FSM_ERROR_TRIGGER_ALERT(CtrlLcCntCheck_A,
+      u_lc_ctrl_fsm.u_cnt_regs, alert_tx_o[1])
   `ASSERT_PRIM_FSM_ERROR_TRIGGER_ALERT(CtrlKmacIfFsmCheck_A,
       u_lc_ctrl_kmac_if.u_state_regs, alert_tx_o[1])
 
diff --git a/hw/ip/lc_ctrl/rtl/lc_ctrl_fsm.sv b/hw/ip/lc_ctrl/rtl/lc_ctrl_fsm.sv
index cf74f6a56ed1c..dac04bd25c755 100644
--- a/hw/ip/lc_ctrl/rtl/lc_ctrl_fsm.sv
+++ b/hw/ip/lc_ctrl/rtl/lc_ctrl_fsm.sv
@@ -457,33 +457,35 @@ module lc_ctrl_fsm
 
   logic [LcStateWidth-1:0] lc_state_raw_q;
   assign lc_state_q = lc_state_e'(lc_state_raw_q);
-  prim_flop #(
+  prim_sparse_fsm_flop #(
+    .StateEnumT(lc_state_e),
     .Width(LcStateWidth),
     .ResetValue(LcStateWidth'(LcStScrap))

-    .d_i ( lc_state_d     ),
-    .q_o ( lc_state_raw_q )

+    .state_o ( lc_cnt_raw_q )

-      lc_state_valid_q     <= 1'b0;

-      lc_state_valid_q     <= lc_state_valid_d;

#!/bin/bash
cd /home/opentitan
set +e

TEST_NAME="lc_ctrl_state_cnt_sec_cm"
TB_ROOT="/home/opentitan/.tb_lc_ctrl_state_cnt_sec_cm"
LOG="$TB_ROOT/dvsim.log"

mkdir -p "$TB_ROOT"
rm -rf "$TB_ROOT/scratch"

cat > "$TB_ROOT/inject_runtime.py" <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path


def patch_env_cfg() -> None:
    path = Path("/home/opentitan/hw/ip/lc_ctrl/dv/env/lc_ctrl_env_cfg.sv")
    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    needle = '    tl_intg_alert_name = "fatal_bus_integ_error";\n'
    insert = needle + '    sec_cm_alert_name = "fatal_state_error";\n'
    if 'sec_cm_alert_name = "fatal_state_error";' not in text:
        text = text.replace(needle, insert, 1)
        path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")


def patch_sim_cfg() -> None:
    path = Path("/home/opentitan/hw/ip/lc_ctrl/dv/lc_ctrl_sim_cfg.hjson")
    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    alert_line = '                "{proj_root}/hw/dv/tools/dvsim/tests/alert_test.hjson",\n'
    sec_cm_line = '                "{proj_root}/hw/dv/tools/dvsim/tests/sec_cm_tests.hjson",\n'
    if sec_cm_line not in text:
        text = text.replace(alert_line, alert_line + sec_cm_line, 1)
    sim_tops_old = '  sim_tops: ["lc_ctrl_bind", "lc_ctrl_cov_bind"]\n'
    sim_tops_new = '  sim_tops: ["lc_ctrl_bind", "lc_ctrl_cov_bind", "sec_cm_prim_sparse_fsm_flop_bind"]\n'
    if "sec_cm_prim_sparse_fsm_flop_bind" not in text:
        text = text.replace(sim_tops_old, sim_tops_new, 1)
    path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")


def patch_base_vseq() -> None:
    path = Path("/home/opentitan/hw/ip/lc_ctrl/dv/env/seq_lib/lc_ctrl_base_vseq.sv")
    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    localparam_marker = "  lc_ctrl_state_pkg::lc_cnt_e lc_cnt;\n"
    localparam_block = (
        localparam_marker
        + '  localparam string SecCmLcStateRegPath = "tb.dut.u_lc_ctrl_fsm.u_state_regs";\n'
        + '  localparam string SecCmLcCntRegPath = "tb.dut.u_lc_ctrl_fsm.u_cnt_regs";\n'
        + "  localparam int NumExpectedSecCmTargets = 2;\n"
    )
    if "SecCmLcStateRegPath" not in text:
        text = text.replace(localparam_marker, localparam_block, 1)

    tail_old = """  virtual function void clear_kmac_user_digest_share();
    while (cfg.m_kmac_app_agent_cfg.has_user_digest_share()) begin
      void'(cfg.m_kmac_app_agent_cfg.get_user_digest_share());
    end
  endfunction

endclass : lc_ctrl_base_vseq
"""
    tail_new = """  virtual function void clear_kmac_user_digest_share();
    while (cfg.m_kmac_app_agent_cfg.has_user_digest_share()) begin
      void'(cfg.m_kmac_app_agent_cfg.get_user_digest_share());
    end
  endfunction

  virtual task test_sec_cm_fi();
    sec_cm_pkg::sec_cm_base_if_proxy target_if_proxy_q[$];
    string found_paths[$];

    foreach (sec_cm_pkg::sec_cm_if_proxy_q[i]) begin
      sec_cm_pkg::sec_cm_base_if_proxy if_proxy = sec_cm_pkg::sec_cm_if_proxy_q[i];
      if (if_proxy.path == SecCmLcStateRegPath || if_proxy.path == SecCmLcCntRegPath) begin
        target_if_proxy_q.push_back(if_proxy);
        found_paths.push_back(if_proxy.path);
      end
    end

    `uvm_info(`gfn, $sformatf("Found targeted sec_cm proxies: %p", found_paths), UVM_LOW)
    `DV_CHECK_EQ_FATAL(target_if_proxy_q.size(), NumExpectedSecCmTargets,
                       $sformatf("Expected %0d targeted sec_cm proxies (%s, %s), got %p",
                                 NumExpectedSecCmTargets, SecCmLcStateRegPath,
                                 SecCmLcCntRegPath, found_paths))

    dut_init("HARD");
    foreach (target_if_proxy_q[i]) begin
      sec_cm_pkg::sec_cm_base_if_proxy if_proxy = target_if_proxy_q[i];
      `uvm_info(`gfn, $sformatf("Injecting sec_cm fault into %s", if_proxy.path), UVM_LOW)
      sec_cm_fi_ctrl_svas(if_proxy, .enable(0));
      sec_cm_inject_fault(if_proxy);
      if ($urandom_range(0, 1)) sec_cm_restore_fault(if_proxy);
      check_sec_cm_fi_resp(if_proxy);
      sec_cm_fi_ctrl_svas(if_proxy, .enable(1));
      dut_init("HARD");
    end
  endtask : test_sec_cm_fi

endclass : lc_ctrl_base_vseq
"""
    if "virtual task test_sec_cm_fi();" not in text:
        text = text.replace(tail_old, tail_new, 1)

    path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")


patch_env_cfg()
patch_sim_cfg()
patch_base_vseq()
PY

python "$TB_ROOT/inject_runtime.py"

timeout 1800 python util/dvsim/dvsim.py \
  hw/ip/lc_ctrl/dv/lc_ctrl_sim_cfg.hjson \
  -i lc_ctrl_sec_cm \
  -t vcs \
  --fixed-seed 1 \

problem_statement:
## Description
In OpenTitan's life cycle controller (`lc_ctrl`), the controller finite state machine (FSM) keeps the current life cycle state and the life cycle transition count in the internal sparse-encoded registers `u_state_regs` and `u_cnt_regs`. These values are derived from the chip's One-Time Programmable (OTP) life cycle data.

## Expected Behavior
`u_state_regs` and `u_cnt_regs` should be protected in the same way as the main `lc_ctrl` FSM state register. If either register is corrupted to an invalid sparse encoding after reset, OpenTitan's predefined security-countermeasure fault-injection checks for sparse FSM state should be able to target that register, and `lc_ctrl` should treat the corruption as a life cycle state error: it must raise `fatal_state_error` instead of continuing to report a normal life cycle state.

## Actual Behavior
`u_state_regs` and `u_cnt_regs` are not handled as protected sparse FSM state elements in the same way as the main FSM state register. Because of that, the predefined security-countermeasure checks do not cover these two registers correctly, and fault injection or other corruption in either register can miss the expected fatal life cycle state error response.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered when a runtime fault, tamper event, or security-countermeasure fault injection corrupts `u_state_regs` or `u_cnt_regs` after reset so that the stored life cycle state or life cycle count is no longer a valid sparse encoding.

problem_statement:
## Description
In the OpenTitan AES IP, automatic operation can start an encryption too early after software clears the key, initialization vector (IV), and data input registers. The issue is observed in Cipher Feedback (CFB) mode: software writes `DATA_IN_3`, clears the key/IV/data input registers, and then writes the key, IV, and only `DATA_IN_0` through `DATA_IN_2` for the next transaction. Even though the last word of the new 128-bit input block has not been rewritten, the AES block can leave `IDLE` and later produce output.

## Expected Behavior
After software clears the AES key, IV, and data input registers, automatic mode must treat the next input block as incomplete until software rewrites all four `DATA_IN` registers (`DATA_IN_0` through `DATA_IN_3`) for that block. A `DATA_IN_3` write that happened before the clear must not satisfy the start condition for the post-clear transaction. In the sequence above, the AES block should remain idle and must not produce output until `DATA_IN_3` is written again after the clear. Once all four `DATA_IN` registers have been rewritten after the clear, the new encryption may start normally.

## Actual Behavior
If `DATA_IN_3` is written before the clear, the AES block can still start a new automatic encryption after the clear once the key, IV, and only `DATA_IN_0` through `DATA_IN_2` are rewritten. That causes encryption to run even though the post-clear input block is still missing `DATA_IN_3`.

## Affected Function
The affected functionality is the AES IP automatic-start logic that determines whether a complete 128-bit input block has been provided after the key, IV, and data input registers are cleared.

## Trigger Condition
This occurs when the AES IP is in automatic mode, configured for Cipher Feedback (CFB), `DATA_IN_3` is written, the key/IV/data input registers are cleared, and software then rewrites the key, IV, and only `DATA_IN_0` through `DATA_IN_2`. Under that sequence, the block may start before `DATA_IN_3` is rewritten after the clear.

resolved_issues.body:
This was brought up during the RV_DM testplan review. 

Currently, if the debugger-initiated access into the full chip over the SBA interface results in an error response, the error is silently dropped and the debugger has no way of knowing that that has happened. What the engineer intended to do using the debugger would actually not happen, and they wouldn't know about it. 

The SBCS register specification in the [RISCV debug spec 0.13.2](https://github.com/riscv/riscv-debug-spec/raw/4e0bb0fc2d843473db2356623792c6b7603b94d4/riscv-debug-release.pdf) (page 34) defines a 3-bit `sberror` field, with value of '7' representing "other" error. It does not explain well what constitutes as "other" error, but we could very well use that to indicate the returned error response. The `dm_sba.sv` module just needs to gain an input signal which will be wired up to the error response from the external device, and when asserted, it could be used to set `sberror = 7`. This seems like a fairly simple enhancement, which will improve the debug experience a bit.

If there is consensus on whether this is feasible and the right thing to do, we can open up a PR in the PULP repo and have it fixed.

problem_statement:
OpenTitan's RISC-V debug module (`rv_dm`) does not correctly report a System Bus Access (SBA) write failure when the downstream TL-UL (TileLink Uncached Lightweight) target returns an error response. SBA is the path that lets an external debugger access memory-mapped addresses through JTAG and the Debug Module Interface (DMI). In the failing case, the debugger issues a normal SBA write, the request is accepted, and the target later responds with a TL-UL error. That response is currently dropped, so the debugger can observe the transaction without any corresponding SBA error being recorded.

This affects the `rv_dm` SBA path, specifically the logic that turns TL-UL response errors into status in the System Bus Control and Status (`SBCS`) register.

Expected behavior: when an SBA write receives a TL-UL error response from the addressed target, `rv_dm` must update `SBCS.sberror` to the SBA bad-address / bus-access error classification so the debugger can tell that the access failed. The failure must not be reported as a busy error (`sbbusyerror`), and it must not be indistinguishable from a timeout or a successful completion.

Trigger condition: a debugger-initiated SBA write reaches the TL-UL system bus and the downstream target returns an error response for that write on the response path.

title: [spi_device] Change `addr_latched` to a pulse signal
body:
Problem:

    `addr_latched_i` in `spid_readsram` module is expected to be a pulse
    signal. The `spi_readcmd` module generates the signal as a level by
    comparing `addr_cnt_d` with all zero value.

    As a result, the `strb` register in `spid_readsram` follows the
    current address, which is increased by when a byte is sent to the
    host system. However, the `spid_readsram` logic pushes the data into
    the FIFO already. As the FIFO depth is 2, one more entry has been
    added to the FIFO, which results the host system sees the a byte has
    been shifted.

Resolution:

    Revised the `addr_latched` logic to be a pulse. Either `addr_cnt_d`
    or `addr_latched` can be revised. I chose the latter. Latching the
    latched signal and generated a pulse.

This PR contains #11829  Please review the last commit only. I will rebase once the PR is merged

problem_statement:
## Description
The bug affects the SPI_DEVICE IP's internally handled Read SFDP (Serial Flash Discoverable Parameters, opcode `0x5A`) path, specifically the flash-read datapath between `spi_readcmd` and `spid_readsram` that serves bytes from the SFDP region of the internal dual-port SRAM (DPSRAM).

## Observed Behavior
When an external SPI master performs a multi-byte SFDP read, the byte stream returned by SPI_DEVICE can be shifted relative to the contents stored in the SFDP SRAM region. The memory contents are correct, but the bytes driven on the SPI interface do not match the requested address sequence.

## Expected Behavior
After the 24-bit SFDP address has been accepted, SPI_DEVICE should return the bytes stored at that address and each following address in order, with no skipped, duplicated, or shifted bytes. For example, an 8-byte read starting at address `0x000080` should return the eight bytes stored at `0x000080` through `0x000087` in that same order.

## Trigger Condition
The failure appears when the Read SFDP command transitions from address capture into continuous multi-byte data output. It is observable on sequential SFDP reads, including an aligned 8-byte transfer starting at `0x000080`.

resolved_issues.title: [adc_ctrl/rtl] Fix Interrupt clock domain crossing
resolved_issues.body:
Currently the interrupt clock domain crossing uses a primitive with the unfortunate property that multiple triggers on the always on clock side while the gated clock is off can cause difficult to predict results.
The first trigger sets the interrupt, a second occurring during a gated period clears the interrupt again, a third sets it again and so on.
This leads to unexpected results.

Perhaps a scheme where all the interrupt logic is performed on the always on side, then copied via a request/acknowledge type CDC to the gated side, would be preferable.

I've re-enabled interrupts for test adc_ctrl_clock_gating in this PR https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/pull/11760

problem_statement:
## Description
The ADC Controller has an interrupt clock-domain crossing bug in the path that carries filter-match events from the always-on clock domain into the gated main clock domain.

## Expected Behavior
If an enabled filter-match event occurs while the main ADC interrupt/register clock is gated off, that event must remain pending until the main clock resumes. Repeated pulses from the same filter-match source during the gated interval must not cancel or clear the pending interrupt. Once the main clock is running again, the corresponding ADC interrupt-status bit and the top-level interrupt pending state must both be asserted.

## Actual Behavior
When the same filter-match source pulses multiple times while the main clock is gated, the current synchronization logic can toggle the pending state on each pulse. After an even number of pulses during one gated interval, the ADC Controller can resume with no pending interrupt, even though an enabled filter-match event occurred.

## Affected Function
ADC Controller interrupt handling for filter-match events that are generated in the always-on clock domain but must update interrupt status and interrupt pending state in the gated main clock domain.

## Trigger Condition
This is triggered when the ADC Controller enters a state where the main clock domain is gated but the always-on ADC logic continues running, and the same enabled filter-match interrupt source fires multiple times before the main clock domain is ungated.

problem_statement:
## Description
OpenTitan's KMAC (Keccak Message Authentication Code) IP has prefix control/status registers (CSRs) that hold the cSHAKE/KMAC function-name and customization prefix. The key manager (KeyMgr) also depends on this prefix when it uses KMAC internally. The bug is that software can still rewrite a KMAC prefix CSR after a KMAC operation has started and the engine is no longer idle.

## Expected Behavior
Once a KMAC operation has started, the prefix CSRs must remain unchanged until that operation finishes and the KMAC engine returns to the idle state. A write attempted while the engine is busy must not change the stored prefix value.

## Actual Behavior
A write to a prefix CSR during an active KMAC operation can change the stored prefix value before the engine returns to idle. As a result, the prefix setting is not guaranteed to stay stable for the full duration of the request, which is also unsafe for KeyMgr operations that rely on the same KMAC prefix setting.

## Trigger Condition
Program the KMAC prefix CSRs, start a KMAC operation, wait until the KMAC engine has left the idle state, and then write a new value to a prefix CSR before the operation completes.

resolved_issues.title: [spi_device] Write enable (WREN) and write disable (WRDI) should be handled in hardware
resolved_issues.body:
The write enable command (WREN, 0x06) sets the write enable latch (WEL) bit, while the write disable command (WRDI, 0x04) clears it. The host sends WREN every time before "writing" to the device, e.g. before chip/sector erase or page program. Since handling this in software would introduce additional latency; WREN & WRDI commands should be handled in hardware.

cc @cfrantz @a-will

problem_statement:
## Description
The OpenTitan SPI Device IP, when operating in flash mode, lacks dedicated command-info Control and Status Registers (CSRs) for the standard SPI flash Write Enable (WREN, opcode 0x06) and Write Disable (WRDI, opcode 0x04) commands. These commands control the write enable latch (WEL) and are issued by an external SPI flash master before program or erase operations, so they are part of the flash command path that hardware must recognize without depending on firmware latency.

## Expected Behavior
The SPI Device flash command interface should expose dedicated software-visible command-info CSRs for WREN and WRDI. Software should be able to program and read back the opcode definitions for these two commands through the register interface, so WREN and WRDI are represented in the flash-mode command-info CSR map in the same way as the other special flash commands.

## Actual Behavior
In the affected implementation, the SPI Device register model has no dedicated command-info CSRs for WREN or WRDI. Software cannot program or read back per-command entries for these opcodes, leaving the flash-mode command-info interface incomplete for these two standard commands.

## Trigger Condition
The problem appears when the SPI Device IP is used in flash mode and software or verification expects dedicated register entries for WREN and WRDI, especially in flows where an external SPI flash master issues WREN or WRDI before a write, page-program, or erase operation.

resolved_issues.body:
- d2s item

Unexpeted acks are checked in two places, the controller access
path and the host access path.

For the controller access path, the accesses are fsm controlled,
so whenever the fsm is idle it should not see an ack.

For the host access path, a small amount of logic is added to track
the number of outstanding host transactions. When there are no
outstanding transactions, a response is not expected and would constitute a
spurious ack.

problem_statement:
## Description
The Flash Controller (`flash_ctrl`) exposes flash memory through a host direct-access TL-UL (TileLink Uncached Lightweight) interface, separate from its control and status register interface. On that host direct-access path, command-integrity errors from the embedded-flash SRAM adapter are not connected to the controller's fatal fault reporting.

## Expected Behavior
If a TL-UL request on the flash host direct-access interface arrives with invalid command integrity bits, `flash_ctrl` must treat it as the same standard fatal integrity fault used for other Flash Controller TL-UL command-integrity failures. The error must be reported through the controller's normal standard fault and alert path rather than being ignored.

## Actual Behavior
When invalid command integrity is detected on the host direct-access path, the error is dropped before it reaches the Flash Controller's fatal fault handling. As a result, the integrity violation on that path is not reported as a fatal standard fault.

## Affected Function
The affected logic is the Flash Controller host direct-access memory interface, specifically the command-integrity reporting path from the embedded-flash TL-UL/SRAM adapter into `flash_ctrl`'s standard fatal fault reporting.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered when a bus master accesses the flash memory window through the host direct-access TL-UL interface, rather than through the control and status register interface, and the TL-UL command carries invalid integrity bits.

resolved_issues.body:
- [x] allow main_pd glitch to also cause an alert
- [x] clarify in the documentation / countermeasure naming the difference between local_esc and terminal
- [x] clarify in documentation (if not already) how local escalation resets are different from normal reset requests. 

The result of these changes is the following:
esc_rx timeout and main_pd glitch both will cause alerts and local escalation. Local escalation behavior is identical to global escalation which causes the pwrmgr to enter a reset sequence.

sparse fsm countermeasure does not cause a local escalation, but instead freezes the system in a terminal state until user or host intervention.

#!/bin/bash
set -uo pipefail

TEST_NAME="pwrmgr_main_pd_glitch_alert"
SCRATCH_ROOT="/home/opentitan/.tb_${TEST_NAME}"
DV_LOG="${SCRATCH_ROOT}/dvsim.log"
printed_result=0

print_result() {
  local rc="$1"
  echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_START"
  if [[ "$rc" -eq 0 ]]; then
    echo "TEST: ${TEST_NAME} ... PASS"
  else
    echo "TEST: ${TEST_NAME} ... FAIL"
  fi
  echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"
  printed_result=1
}

on_exit() {
  local rc=$?
  trap - EXIT
  if [[ "$printed_result" -eq 0 ]]; then
    print_result "$rc"
  fi
  exit "$rc"
}

trap on_exit EXIT

set -e
cd /home/opentitan

if [[ -f /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh ]]; then

  source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh
fi

problem_statement:
## Description
In the OpenTitan Power Manager (`pwrmgr`) IP, a transient glitch on the main power domain (`main_pd`) after the block has reached normal active operation already pushes the power manager into its reset-preparation flow, but the event is not fully reported as a fault.

## Expected Behavior
If `pwrmgr` detects an unexpected drop and recovery of the `main_pd` power-good signal while the system is active, it should enter the main-power reset-preparation sequence, assert the `pwrmgr` alert, and latch a software-readable `main_pd` glitch indication in the fault-status control/status register (CSR).

## Actual Behavior
The transient `main_pd` glitch still drives `pwrmgr` into reset preparation, but `pwrmgr` does not raise the alert for this case and does not latch a dedicated `main_pd` glitch fault indication for software.

## Affected Function
The affected logic is the OpenTitan Power Manager (`pwrmgr`) fault-reporting path for main power-domain glitches, specifically the logic that generates alerts and records fault causes when the main-power reset path is entered.

## Trigger Condition
This occurs when the `main_pd` power-good signal briefly drops and then returns after `pwrmgr` has reached its normal active state.

problem_statement:
## Description
In the OpenTitan flash controller IP (`flash_ctrl`), the host interface direct-read path for the flash data partition can decode memory-protection region attributes differently from controller-initiated flash accesses. The original issue reports that the host region decode does not incorporate the region enable (`EN`) bit, so a host direct read can use attributes from a region that is not actually enabled.

## Expected Behavior
For any flash data-partition address, the host interface direct-read path and the controller path must use the same effective access attributes. If an address falls inside the range of a memory-protection region whose `EN` bit is not active, that region must not affect the access; the host direct read must behave as if the disabled region were absent, matching the controller's view of the same address. In particular, in a configuration where scrambling is enabled for the effective access, a word programmed and then read back through the controller must match the data returned by a host direct read of that same word.

## Actual Behavior
A host direct read can apply attributes from a memory-protection region based only on the address range, even when that region is disabled. As a result, the data returned by a host direct read can differ from the data returned by a controller read of the same programmed flash word.

## Trigger Condition
This occurs when a host interface direct read targets a flash data-partition address that lies within the range of a configured memory-protection region whose `EN` bit is not active. The regression exposes the bug when that location is then compared between the controller read path and the host direct-read path in a scramble-enabled configuration.

title: [flash_ctrl] Separate invalid and disabled states.
body:
- fixes https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/issues/11825

Part of the D2S design fixes was to unify the disabled behavior across
more of the flash controller state machines. However this created a
problem for RMA entry.

When RMA entry is done, the RMA fsm also requests flash operationst to be
disabled. Previosuly, this caused the RMA fsm itself to transition into
an invalid state.  This caused 2 problems:

1. At the end of RMA, a fatal alert is generated. While this is
   not bad behavior in any meaningful way, it is very inconsistent with alert
   defintion because no fatal event has occurred. This leads to unnecessary
   DV work.

2. Since the RMA fsm transitions out of its ack state, it means the ack
   indication sent to life cycle controller will be held for only 1 cycle.
   This is most definitely not enough for CDC and means RMA cannot be completed.

This commit separates the idea of "disabled" and "invalid" for most of the fsms.
Disabled simply means functionally disabled from future operations, while
invalid is both disabled AND alert generation.

At the end of RMA transition, the device is simply "disabled" and not "invalid".
Invalid then can only be caused by an explicit error, or the FSMs going
completely to an undefined state.

This makes the overall definition more consistent.

repo.name: opentitan
repo.description: OpenTitan: Open source silicon root of trust

commits.message:
[flash_ctrl] Separate invalid and disabled states.

- fixes #11825

Part of the D2S design fixes was to unify the disabled behavior across
more of the flash controller state machines. However this created a
problem for RMA entry.

When RMA entry is done, the RMA fsm also requests flash operationst to be
disabled. Previosuly, this caused the RMA fsm itself to transition into
an invalid state.  This caused 2 problems:

1. At the end of RMA, a fatal alert is generated. While this is
   not bad behavior in any meaningful way, it is very inconsistent with alert
   defintion because no fatal event has occurred. This leads to unnecessary
   DV work.

2. Since the RMA fsm transitions out of its ack state, it means the ack
   indication sent to life cycle controller will be held for only 1 cycle.
   This is most definitely not enough for CDC and means RMA cannot be completed.

This commit separates the idea of "disabled" and "invalid" for most of the fsms.
Disabled simply means functionally disabled from future operations, while
invalid is both disabled AND alert generation.

At the end of RMA transition, the device is simply "disabled" and not "invalid".
Invalid then can only be caused by an explicit error, or the FSMs going
completely to an undefined state.

This makes the overall definition more consistent.

Signed-off-by: Timothy Chen <timothytim@google.com>

report_result_and_exit() {
  local status="$1"
  local rc="$2"

  echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_START"
  echo "TEST: ${TEST_NAME} ... ${status}"
  echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"
  exit "${rc}"
}

ST_RMA_RSP_VALUE="$(sed -n "s/^[[:space:]]*StRmaRsp[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*\\([^,]*\\),/\\1/p" \
  hw/ip/flash_ctrl/rtl/flash_ctrl_lcmgr.sv | head -n1)"

if [[ -z "${ST_RMA_RSP_VALUE}" ]]; then
  report_result_and_exit "FAIL" 1
fi

cat > "${VSEQ_FILE}" <<EOF
// Copyright lowRISC contributors.
// Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0, see LICENSE for details.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

class ${TEST_NAME}_vseq extends flash_ctrl_base_vseq;
  \`uvm_object_utils(${TEST_NAME}_vseq)
  \`uvm_object_new

  localparam logic [10:0] StRmaRspValue = ${ST_RMA_RSP_VALUE};

  virtual task body();
    string lcmgr_state_path = "tb.dut.u_flash_hw_if.state_q";
    string lcmgr_state_raw_path = "tb.dut.u_flash_hw_if.u_state_regs.state_o";
    int ack_high_cycles = 0;
    bit ack_seen = 0;

    \`uvm_info(\`gfn, "FLASH_CTRL_RMA_ACK_HOLD", UVM_LOW)

    cfg.clk_rst_vif.wait_clks(10);
    cfg.flash_ctrl_vif.rma_seed = 32'h1badc0de;
    cfg.flash_ctrl_vif.rma_req = lc_ctrl_pkg::On;

    if (!uvm_hdl_deposit(lcmgr_state_path, StRmaRspValue)) begin
      \`uvm_fatal(\`gfn, \$sformatf("Failed to deposit %s", lcmgr_state_path))
    end
    if (!uvm_hdl_deposit(lcmgr_state_raw_path, StRmaRspValue)) begin
      \`uvm_fatal(\`gfn, \$sformatf("Failed to deposit %s", lcmgr_state_raw_path))
    end

    repeat (20) begin
      cfg.clk_rst_vif.wait_clks(1);
      if (cfg.flash_ctrl_vif.rma_ack == lc_ctrl_pkg::On) begin
        ack_seen = 1;
        break;
      end
    end

    if (!ack_seen) begin
      \`uvm_fatal(\`gfn, "RMA ACK did not rise after depositing StRmaRsp")
    end

    repeat (10) begin
      if (cfg.flash_ctrl_vif.rma_ack == lc_ctrl_pkg::On) begin
        ack_high_cycles++;
      end
      cfg.clk_rst_vif.wait_clks(1);
    end

    \`uvm_info(\`gfn, \$sformatf("Observed RMA ACK high for %0d / 10 cycles", ack_high_cycles),
               UVM_LOW)
    if (ack_high_cycles < 10) begin
      \`uvm_error(\`gfn, \$sformatf("RMA ACK was not held high long enough: %0d / 10 cycles",
                                   ack_high_cycles))
    end
  endtask
endclass
EOF

if ! grep -q "${TEST_NAME}_vseq" "${VSEQ_LIST}"; then

  --fixed-seed 1 \
  --build-seed 1 \
  --run-opts +UVM_TEST_SEQ=${TEST_NAME}_vseq
rc=$?

if [[ ${rc} -eq 0 ]]; then
  report_result_and_exit "PASS" 0
else

fi

problem_statement:
## Description
In the OpenTitan flash controller, the life cycle manager logic that finishes an RMA (Return Material Authorization) entry mis-handles the final response phase. When the wipe flow completes and the controller simultaneously marks flash access as disabled for all future operations, the RMA completion path treats that normal post-RMA disabled condition as an invalid/error condition. The controller then leaves the final RMA response state immediately, so the RMA acknowledgement signal `rma_ack` is asserted for only one cycle instead of being held long enough for the life cycle controller to sample it.

## Expected Behavior
After a successful RMA entry, the flash controller should enter a disabled post-RMA state that blocks future flash operations without being treated as an invalid state. While RMA completion is being reported, `rma_ack` must remain asserted until the life cycle controller can observe the acknowledgement across the clock-domain crossing (CDC) handshake.

## Affected Functionality
This affects the flash controller's life cycle manager submodule responsible for RMA completion and the acknowledgement path from the flash controller back to the life cycle controller, especially the boundary between the final RMA response state and the post-RMA disabled state.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered at the end of a successful RMA wipe sequence, when the controller enters the final RMA response phase and the same transition also disables subsequent flash access.

problem_statement:
## Description
OpenTitan's Power Manager (pwrmgr) uses a slow finite state machine (FSM) in the slow clock domain and a fast FSM in the main clock domain. When the slow FSM enters an invalid sparse-encoded state and raises `slow_fsm_invalid`, that condition is supposed to be treated as a terminal security fault. The invalid indication must still cross from the slow clock domain into the fast clock domain so that the fast FSM can leave normal operation and enter its invalid fault-handling state.

## Expected Behavior
If the slow pwrmgr FSM enters an invalid sparse-encoded state, the `slow_fsm_invalid` indication must continue to propagate through the slow-to-fast clock-domain crossing (CDC) path even when pwrmgr is in, or entering, a low-power or clock-gating transition. After observing that indication, the fast FSM must not remain in its normal active flow; it must enter its invalid terminal state and assert the reset requests required by pwrmgr's terminal fault response.

## Actual Behavior
When `slow_fsm_invalid` is asserted while the slow FSM would otherwise allow clocks to be turned off, the clock feeding the slow-to-fast CDC path can stop before the invalid indication is sampled in the fast clock domain. As a result, the fast FSM can remain in its normal active state instead of entering invalid fault handling, so the terminal response to the slow-FSM sparse fault is not completed correctly.

## Affected Function
This bug affects the pwrmgr slow FSM clock-enable logic during invalid-state handling, specifically the clocks that keep the slow-to-fast invalid-signal CDC path alive, and therefore the fast FSM's response to a slow-FSM sparse-encoding fault.

## Trigger Condition
The failure is triggered when the slow pwrmgr FSM is forced into an invalid sparse-encoded state at a time when its normal sequencing would otherwise gate clocks off or allow them to turn off.

title: [spi_device] spi_p2s to run only when `data_valid`
body:
This commit addresses the issue #12342.

As dummy cycle may not be byte granularity, the output logic `spi_p2s`
now runs only when `data_valid_i` is high.

Now, `data_sent_o` is asserted when `data_valid_i` is high. The
data_sent_o is high based on the io_mode to compare `cnt` with the
correct value. The logic increases `cnt` only when `data_valid_i` is
high.

As `last_beat` is not asserted anymore, the `io_mode` does not latch
`io_mode_i` at `last_beat`. The logic uses `io_mode_i` directly. It is
OK as spi_device top latches comb logic io_mode at @ iSCK.

repo.name: opentitan
repo.description: OpenTitan: Open source silicon root of trust

commits.message:
[spi_device] spi_p2s to run only when `data_valid`

This commit addresses the issue #12342.

As dummy cycle may not be byte granularity, the output logic `spi_p2s`
now runs only when `data_valid_i` is high.

Now, `data_sent_o` is asserted when `data_valid_i` is high. The
data_sent_o is high based on the io_mode to compare `cnt` with the
correct value. The logic increases `cnt` only when `data_valid_i` is
high.

As `last_beat` is not asserted anymore, the `io_mode` does not latch
`io_mode_i` at `last_beat`. The logic uses `io_mode_i` directly. It is
OK as spi_device top latches comb logic io_mode at @iSCK.

Signed-off-by: Eunchan Kim <eunchan@opentitan.org>

resolved_issues.title: [spi_device] Dummy Cycle should be io_mode independent
resolved_issues.body:
dummy size should be independent of IoMode (Single, Dual, Quad).

In current design, the readcmd FSM assigns default IoSingle mode while in the dummy state. It results the parallel-to-serial logic to assert the `p2s_sent` signal in 8th cycle. If host system issues *Fast Read Dual* command, the dummy cycle is usually multiple of 4 cycles. As CMD_INFO slot for *Fast Read Dual* command is configured as to have 4 dummy cycles, the HW could not send correct values to the host system.

CC: @weicaiyang @kosta-kojdic

fix_patch:
diff --git a/hw/ip/spi_device/rtl/spi_p2s.sv b/hw/ip/spi_device/rtl/spi_p2s.sv
index 514993e84caad..0a1841cfbe20c 100644
--- a/hw/ip/spi_device/rtl/spi_p2s.sv
+++ b/hw/ip/spi_device/rtl/spi_p2s.sv
@@ -170,22 +170,13 @@ module spi_p2s
 
   // io_mode
   // io_mode reset value is SingleIO (as described in assumption)
-  // Then, every byte sent, the logic updates its value to `io_mode_i`
-  // This makes the logic safer than direct use of `io_mode_i`.
-  // If `io_mode_i` value is changed within a byte, it affects to `last_beat`
-  // then, the incorrect `last_beat` affects `cnt`, which could break
-  // the data operation.
+  // Previously, logic updated io_mode at every byte. It was to make io_mode
+  // safer. However, as `io_mode_i` is updated at @iSCK (from spi_device top),
+  // and also spi_p2s logic runs only when `data_valid_i` is high, the need of
+  // latching logic disapears.
   //
-  // Following logic has high chance to break the rule. As there's no
-  // indication of the end of a byte. `data_sent_o` is not a valid indicator
-  // as the signal asserted one cycle earlier than the last beat.
-  always_ff @(posedge clk_i or negedge rst_ni) begin
-    if (!rst_ni) begin
-      io_mode <= SingleIO;
-    end else if (last_beat) begin
-      io_mode <= io_mode_i;
-    end
-  end
+  // Now, the logic uses `io_mode_i` directly.
+  assign io_mode = io_mode_i;
 
   // cnt
   always_ff @(posedge clk_i or negedge rst_ni) begin
@@ -193,7 +184,7 @@ module spi_p2s
       cnt <= BitWidth'(0);
     end else if (last_beat) begin
       cnt <= BitWidth'(0);
-    end else if (tx_state != TxIdle || cpha_i == 1'b 0) begin
+    end else if (data_valid_i && (tx_state != TxIdle || cpha_i == 1'b 0)) begin
       cnt <= cnt + 1'b 1;
     end
   end

problem_statement:
## Description
The bug is in the OpenTitan SPI (Serial Peripheral Interface) Device IP, specifically the `spi_p2s` transmit logic used by the read-command data path after dummy clocks. The dummy-clock phase is currently not treated independently from the selected SPI I/O width, even though Single I/O, Dual I/O, and Quad I/O read commands can use different numbers of data lines while still defining dummy time in SPI clock cycles.

## Expected Behavior
Dummy clocks must be consumed as command-defined idle SPI clock cycles, not counted as payload-transfer progress. During the dummy phase of a read command, the SPI Device must not treat the transfer as having advanced by part of a byte, must not indicate that a payload byte has been sent, and must not drive payload output enables. When the data phase starts, transmission must resume in the configured I/O mode. For example, if a Fast Read Dual command is configured with 4 dummy clocks before data, the SPI Device should consume exactly those 4 clocks as dummy time, then start the payload phase in Dual I/O, and only indicate that a byte has been sent after two valid Dual-I/O beats.

## Actual Behavior
In the current design, entering the dummy state can make byte-progress tracking behave as if Single I/O rules still applied. As a result, dummy clocks can be counted toward byte completion, causing the byte-sent indication to assert too early and the payload phase to start on the wrong boundary.

## Trigger Condition
This occurs for SPI Device read commands that use Dual I/O or Quad I/O and include a dummy phase whose length is not an 8-clock Single-I/O byte. A concrete failing case is a Fast Read Dual transaction configured with 4 dummy clocks before the payload data phase.

resolved_issues.title: [spi_device] Write enable (WREN) and write disable (WRDI) should be handled in hardware
resolved_issues.body:
The write enable command (WREN, 0x06) sets the write enable latch (WEL) bit, while the write disable command (WRDI, 0x04) clears it. The host sends WREN every time before "writing" to the device, e.g. before chip/sector erase or page program. Since handling this in software would introduce additional latency; WREN & WRDI commands should be handled in hardware.

cc @cfrantz @a-will

problem_statement:
## Description
OpenTitan's SPI Device hardware block can act as an SPI flash target. In the `silicon_creator` boot firmware initialization path, `spi_device_init()` does not enable hardware handling of the standard SPI flash Write Enable (WREN, 0x06) and Write Disable (WRDI, 0x04) commands. That leaves this initialization path without the expected hardware-managed write-enable latch behavior.

## Expected Behavior
After `spi_device_init()` configures the SPI Device for flash-style operation, WREN must be recognized in hardware and set the write enable latch (WEL) bit in the status register, while WRDI must be recognized in hardware and clear the same WEL bit. An external SPI host that issues Read Status (0x05) after WREN should observe WEL asserted, and the same status read after WRDI should observe WEL deasserted, without requiring software handling of those commands.

## Actual Behavior
With the current `spi_device_init()` configuration, WREN and WRDI are not enabled as hardware-handled flash commands for this boot-firmware path. As a result, an external SPI host cannot rely on the normal WREN -> Read Status -> WRDI -> Read Status sequence to drive the WEL bit through the expected set and clear transitions.

## Affected Module
The affected area is the `silicon_creator` boot firmware's SPI Device initialization path, specifically the SPI Device flash-command configuration performed by `spi_device_init()`.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered when the SPI Device has been initialized by `spi_device_init()` for flash-style operation and an external SPI host sends WREN or WRDI, then reads status to check the WEL state.
