  CHECK_DIF_OK(dif_lc_ctrl_get_hw_rev(&lc_ctrl, &hw_rev));

  LOG_INFO("Observed LC HW revision chip_gen=%u chip_rev=%u", hw_rev.chip_gen,
           hw_rev.chip_rev);

  spi_device_init();

  mmio_region_t spi_device =
      mmio_region_from_addr(TOP_EARLGREY_SPI_DEVICE_BASE_ADDR);
  uint32_t jedec_id =
      mmio_region_read32(spi_device, SPI_DEVICE_JEDEC_ID_REG_OFFSET);
  uint32_t chip_rev =
      bitfield_field32_read(jedec_id, SPI_DEVICE_DEV_ID_CHIP_REV_FIELD);
  uint32_t chip_gen =
      bitfield_field32_read(jedec_id, SPI_DEVICE_DEV_ID_CHIP_GEN_FIELD);

  uint32_t exp_chip_rev =
      hw_rev.chip_rev & SPI_DEVICE_DEV_ID_CHIP_REV_FIELD.mask;
  uint32_t exp_chip_gen =
      hw_rev.chip_gen & SPI_DEVICE_DEV_ID_CHIP_GEN_FIELD.mask;

  LOG_INFO("Observed JEDEC register 0x%08x chip_gen=%u chip_rev=%u", jedec_id,
           chip_gen, chip_rev);

  CHECK(chip_rev == exp_chip_rev,
        "JEDEC chip_rev mismatch: expected %u observed %u", exp_chip_rev,
        chip_rev);
  CHECK(chip_gen == exp_chip_gen,
        "JEDEC chip_gen mismatch: expected %u observed %u", exp_chip_gen,
        chip_gen);

  return true;
}
""",
    encoding="utf-8",
)
PY
}

#!/bin/bash
set -e

# Stage 1: checkout base_sha in a clean workspace (+submodules)
cd /home/opentitan
git reset --hard
git clean -fdx
git checkout d14db57accb316648f9ca0ec7be5e511c804a419
git submodule update --init --recursive

# Stage 2: install repository apt dependencies (if present)
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
if [[ -f apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing apt dependencies from apt-requirements.txt"
  cp apt-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  sed -i -e '/^$/d' -e '/^#/d' -e 's/#.*//' /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  if [[ -s /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
    apt-get update
    xargs -r apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends < /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
  else
    echo "[INFO] apt-requirements.txt is empty after filtering comments"
  fi
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
else
  echo "[WARN] apt-requirements.txt not found at base_sha; skipping repo-specific apt install"
fi

# Stage 3: normalize and install Python dependencies from the checked-out repo.
# Bazel reads python-requirements.txt directly, so keep the normalized file in-tree.
if [[ -f python-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Python deps from python-requirements.txt"
  python -m pip install -U pip "setuptools<66.0.0"
  python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re

path = Path("python-requirements.txt")
lines = []
for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
    stripped = line.strip()
    if stripped in {
        "types-dataclasses",
        "types-pkg_resources",
    }:
        continue
    line = re.sub(r'(#egg=[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)\s+[<>=!~].*', r'\1', line)
    lines.append(line)
path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
PY
  python -m pip install -r python-requirements.txt --no-warn-script-location
else
  echo "[ERROR] python-requirements.txt not found at base_sha"
  exit 1
fi

# Stage 4: install RISC-V toolchain + Verible, then persist their PATH
if [[ -f util/get-toolchain.py ]]; then
  toolchain_version=""
  if [[ -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
    toolchain_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
  fi

  echo "[INFO] Installing RISC-V toolchain via util/get-toolchain.py"
  if [[ -n "$toolchain_version" ]]; then
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update -r "$toolchain_version"
  else
    echo "[WARN] RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION not found; falling back to util/get-toolchain.py defaults"
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update
  fi
else
  echo "[WARN] util/get-toolchain.py not found at base_sha; skipping RISC-V toolchain install"
fi

verible_version=""
if [[ -f hw/tool_requirements.py ]]; then
  verible_version="$(python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path

ns = {}
exec(Path("hw/tool_requirements.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8"), ns)
reqs = ns.get("__TOOL_REQUIREMENTS__", {})
entry = reqs.get("verible", "")
if isinstance(entry, dict):
    print(entry.get("min_version", ""))
elif isinstance(entry, str):
    print(entry)
PY
)"
fi
if [[ -z "$verible_version" && -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
  verible_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG VERIBLE_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
fi

if [[ -n "$verible_version" ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Verible ${verible_version}"
  rm -rf /tools/verible
  mkdir -p /tools/verible
  if curl -f -Ls -o /tmp/verible.tar.gz \
      "https://github.com/chipsalliance/verible/releases/download/${verible_version}/verible-${verible_version}-linux-static-x86_64.tar.gz"; then
    tar -C /tools/verible -xf /tmp/verible.tar.gz --strip-components=1
    rm -f /tmp/verible.tar.gz
  else
    echo "[WARN] Failed to download Verible ${verible_version}; continuing without Verible"
    rm -f /tmp/verible.tar.gz
  fi
else
  echo "[WARN] Unable to determine Verible version from hw/tool_requirements.py or util/container/Dockerfile"
fi

cat > /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh <<'EOF'
for d in /tools/riscv/bin /tools/verible/bin; do
  if [ -d "$d" ]; then
    export PATH="$d:$PATH"
  fi
done
true
EOF

if ! grep -q "/etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh" /etc/opentitan_bash_env; then
  echo "source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh" >> /etc/opentitan_bash_env
fi
source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh

python -m pip show edalize fusesoc hjson >/dev/null
if command -v riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[INFO] RISC-V toolchain ready: $(riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc --version | head -n1)"
else
  echo "[ERROR] riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc not found after Stage 4"
  exit 1
fi
if command -v verible-verilog-lint >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[INFO] Verible ready: $(verible-verilog-lint --version | head -n1)"
else
  echo "[WARN] verible-verilog-lint not found after Stage 4"
fi
problem_statement:
## Description
In OpenTitan, the silicon_creator boot firmware initializes the SPI Device peripheral's JEDEC device-identification register in `spi_device_init()`. The Life Cycle Controller (LC_CTRL) provides the hardware revision as separate chip-generation and chip-revision values, and that revision information is intended to populate the SPI Device JEDEC ID used for bootstrap and reporting.

## Expected Behavior
After `spi_device_init()` completes, the SPI Device JEDEC ID register must encode the current LC_CTRL hardware revision in its `CHIP_GEN` and `CHIP_REV` fields. Because those JEDEC fields are narrower than the LC_CTRL hardware-revision fields, each JEDEC field should contain the least-significant bits of the corresponding LC_CTRL value that fit in the field.

## Actual Behavior
`spi_device_init()` leaves the JEDEC `CHIP_GEN` and `CHIP_REV` fields at zero instead of deriving them from LC_CTRL. When LC_CTRL reports non-zero hardware-revision bits, software that reads the SPI Device JEDEC ID register sees revision fields that do not match the device's hardware revision.

## Affected Module
This bug affects the silicon_creator SPI Device initialization path, specifically the JEDEC ID setup for the SPI Device peripheral and its interaction with the Life Cycle Controller (LC_CTRL) hardware-revision register.

## Trigger Condition
The mismatch is observable whenever `spi_device_init()` runs on hardware or simulation where the LC_CTRL hardware revision contains non-zero bits within the width of the JEDEC `CHIP_GEN` or `CHIP_REV` fields. Reading the SPI Device JEDEC ID register after initialization then returns zero in one or both revision fields instead of the truncated LC_CTRL hardware revision.

title: [flash_ctrl] Select appropriate ready's based on request source
body:
- fixes https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/issues/12381
- the previous design used the read stage's ready for arbitration.
  Due to the way the design is currently done, the read stage ready
  is actually dependent on the the downstream flash macro actually
  ack-ing the transaction.  To fix this, we would need to de-couple
  the req/ack interface on the side facing the phy and the side facing
  the macro.  While this is doable, it would also require us to latch
  incoming bus attributes.  However, there is not a lot to gain by doing
  so, because as long as the flash has not responded, the next read
  cannot proceed anyways.
- This dependency can cause program/erase operations to lock-up if the
  the downstream macro does not always keep ack asserted when idle (in
  effect behaving more like ready).
- Even though the above fix would be cleaner long term, the quick fix is
  simply to pick the appropriate ready for host and controller operations
  separately.

repo.name: opentitan
repo.description: OpenTitan: Open source silicon root of trust

commits.message:
[flash_ctrl] Select appropriate ready's based on request source

- fixes #12381
- the previous design used the read stage's ready for arbitration.
  Due to the way the design is currently done, the read stage ready
  is actually dependent on the the downstream flash macro actually
  ack-ing the transaction.  To fix this, we would need to de-couple
  the req/ack interface on the side facing the phy and the side facing
  the macro.  While this is doable, it would also require us to latch
  incoming bus attributes.  However, there is not a lot to gain by doing
  so, because as long as the flash has not responded, the next read
  cannot proceed anyways.
- This dependency can cause program/erase operations to lock-up if the
  the downstream macro does not always keep ack asserted when idle (in
  effect behaving more like ready).
- Even though the above fix would be cleaner long term, the quick fix is
  simply to pick the appropriate ready for host and controller operations
  separately.

Signed-off-by: Timothy Chen <timothytim@google.com>

[flash_ctrl] Allow fixed priority arbiter

- allow prim_arbiter_tree_dup to instantiate either rr or fixed priority
  arbiters
- switch phy arbitration to fixed priority since host most of the time
  has priority over controller

Signed-off-by: Timothy Chen <timothytim@google.com>

resolved_issues.title: Smoke test failing in the closed-source due to changes in the OS design
resolved_issues.body:
Hi,

Before everything, is it possible you'll add me as CC to the flash_ctrl's design PRs? It will help me to expect issues or things I need to update in the closed-source DV.

First of all, it seems the flash_ctrl prog_fifo depth has been changed in the flash_ctrl_env_pkg from 16 to 4, even though in the flash_ctrl spec is stated to still be 16. Is that intentional?
https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/48e4bb6fca893b2065ac14299369b2aa4739f48e/hw/ip/flash_ctrl/dv/tb/tb.sv#L94-L98
https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/48e4bb6fca893b2065ac14299369b2aa4739f48e/hw/ip/flash_ctrl/dv/env/flash_ctrl_env_pkg.sv#L34-L35
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/78012616/165791068-5483a74b-f86e-49e4-a17b-49e96751deea.png)


Secondly and more important, it seems that some changes that were done in the flash_ctrl files are causing some issues.
Before the full description, in order to reproduce the issue run flash_ctrl_smoke test in the closed-source env (and in the OS as well, to understand the difference). Notice that this issue happens in program transactions, so there is a some small chance the random smoke test will not create a program scenario, so it's better to run a few to make sure.

**Description:**
All program transactions are failing in the closed-source environment due to that program requests are initiated in the flash_ctrl but are blocked from being sent to the inner closed-source hierarchy.
It seems that in order to send prog_i to the inner hierarchies, the signal state_d in file flash_phy_core should be set to StCtrlProg:
https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/48e4bb6fca893b2065ac14299369b2aa4739f48e/hw/ip/flash_ctrl/rtl/flash_phy_core.sv#L298-L306
For state_d to change from idle to prog:
https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/48e4bb6fca893b2065ac14299369b2aa4739f48e/hw/ip/flash_ctrl/rtl/flash_phy_core.sv#L283-L284
Now, while prog_i is 1 as expected, ctrl_gnt stays 0.
This comes from:
https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/48e4bb6fca893b2065ac14299369b2aa4739f48e/hw/ip/prim/rtl/prim_arbiter_tree_dup.sv#L98-L99
https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/48e4bb6fca893b2065ac14299369b2aa4739f48e/hw/ip/prim/rtl/prim_arbiter_tree.sv#L124-L126
While the 2 first signals are 1 as needed, the ready signal isn't and comes from:
https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/48e4bb6fca893b2065ac14299369b2aa4739f48e/hw/ip/flash_ctrl/rtl/flash_phy_rd.sv#L333-L335
All of those signals are as needed, except the ack. Notice that in order for the ready to be 1 the ack signal coming from the inner hierarchy should be 1, which isn't seems reasonable. Since no request was sent to the inner hierarchy by now, why would it send an acknowledge?
What comes from this is a loop - the request waits for an acknowledge which waits for a request.

In addition, it seems that the smoke test is passing in the OS env. The reason it's passing is because for some reason the acknowledge seems to always come before the request:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/78012616/165788041-8ba36cc3-b7f0-4f12-b579-9b03dae0cc73.png)

Thanks!

fix_patch:
diff --git a/hw/ip/flash_ctrl/rtl/flash_phy_core.sv b/hw/ip/flash_ctrl/rtl/flash_phy_core.sv
index 05ecbe32e14ba..f1982d6e50d0d 100644
--- a/hw/ip/flash_ctrl/rtl/flash_phy_core.sv
+++ b/hw/ip/flash_ctrl/rtl/flash_phy_core.sv
@@ -101,7 +101,7 @@ module flash_phy_core
   state_e state_q, state_d;
 
   // request signals to flash macro
-  logic [PhyOps-1:0] reqs;
+  logic [PhyLastOp-1:0] reqs;
 
   // host select for address
   logic host_sel;
@@ -236,7 +236,7 @@ module flash_phy_core
   // controller request can only win after the entire read pipeline
   // clears
   logic ctrl_req;
-  assign ctrl_req = req_i & rd_stage_idle & ~host_req &
+  assign ctrl_req = req_i & rd_stage_idle &
                     mubi4_test_false_strict(flash_disable[CtrlDisableIdx]);
 
   logic [1:0] data_tie_off [2];
@@ -244,24 +244,30 @@ module flash_phy_core
 
   // SEC_CM: PHY_ARBITER.CTRL.REDUN
   logic phy_req;
+  logic phy_rdy;
+
   prim_arbiter_tree_dup #(
     .N(2),
     .DW(2),
-    .EnDataPort('0)
+    .EnDataPort('0),
+    .FixedArb(1)
   ) u_host_arb (
     .clk_i,
     .rst_ni,
     .req_chk_i('0),
-    .req_i({host_req, ctrl_req}),
+    .req_i({ctrl_req, host_req}),
     .data_i(data_tie_off),
-    .gnt_o({host_req_rdy_o, ctrl_gnt}),
+    .gnt_o({ctrl_gnt, host_req_rdy_o}),
     .idx_o(),
     .valid_o(phy_req),
     .data_o(),
-    .ready_i(rd_stage_rdy),
+    .ready_i(phy_rdy),
     .err_o(arb_err_o)
   );
 
+  assign phy_rdy = phy_req & host_req ? rd_stage_rdy : rd_stage_idle;
+
+
   // if request happens at the same time as a host grant, increment count
   assign inc_arb_cnt = req_i & host_gnt;
 
diff --git a/hw/ip/flash_ctrl/rtl/flash_phy_pkg.sv b/hw/ip/flash_ctrl/rtl/flash_phy_pkg.sv
index eaffdfd7d2cc2..4603ec0e93a28 100644
--- a/hw/ip/flash_ctrl/rtl/flash_phy_pkg.sv
+++ b/hw/ip/flash_ctrl/rtl/flash_phy_pkg.sv
@@ -84,14 +84,12 @@ package flash_phy_pkg;
 
   // Flash Operations Supported
   typedef enum logic [1:0] {
-    PhyRead      = 2'h0,
-    PhyProg      = 2'h1,
-    PhyPgErase   = 2'h2,
-    PhyBkErase   = 2'h3
+    PhyProg,
+    PhyPgErase,
+    PhyBkErase,
+    PhyLastOp
   } flash_phy_op_e;
 
-  localparam int PhyOps = 4;
-
   // Flash Operations Selected
   typedef enum logic [1:0] {
     None         = 2'h0,
diff --git a/hw/ip/prim/rtl/prim_arbiter_tree_dup.sv b/hw/ip/prim/rtl/prim_arbiter_tree_dup.sv
index 58d7abb5b42d9..8ed2a7c20dc09 100644
--- a/hw/ip/prim/rtl/prim_arbiter_tree_dup.sv
+++ b/hw/ip/prim/rtl/prim_arbiter_tree_dup.sv
@@ -20,6 +20,9 @@ module prim_arbiter_tree_dup #(
   // EnDataPort: {0, 1}, if 0, input data will be ignored
   parameter bit EnDataPort = 1,
 
+  // if arbiter has fixed priority
+  parameter bit FixedArb = 0,
+
   // Derived parameters
   localparam int IdxW = $clog2(N)
 ) (
@@ -77,22 +80,43 @@ module prim_arbiter_tree_dup #(
       );
     end
 
-    prim_arbiter_tree #(
-      .N(N),
-      .DW(DW),
-      .EnDataPort(EnDataPort)
-    ) u_arb (
-      .clk_i,
-      .rst_ni,
-      .req_chk_i,
-      .req_i(req_buf),
-      .data_i(data_buf),
-      .gnt_o(arb_output_buf[i].gnt),
-      .idx_o(arb_output_buf[i].idx),
-      .valid_o(arb_output_buf[i].valid),
-      .data_o(arb_output_buf[i].data),
-      .ready_i
-    );
+    if (FixedArb) begin : gen_fixed_arbiter
+      prim_arbiter_fixed  #(
+        .N(N),
+        .DW(DW),
+        .EnDataPort(EnDataPort)
+      ) u_arb (
+        .clk_i,
+        .rst_ni,
+        .req_i(req_buf),
+        .data_i(data_buf),
+        .gnt_o(arb_output_buf[i].gnt),
+        .idx_o(arb_output_buf[i].idx),
+        .valid_o(arb_output_buf[i].valid),
+        .data_o(arb_output_buf[i].data),
+        .ready_i
+      );
+      logic unused_req_chk;
+      assign unused_req_chk = req_chk_i;
+
+    end else begin : gen_rr_arbiter
+      prim_arbiter_tree #(
+        .N(N),
+        .DW(DW),
+        .EnDataPort(EnDataPort)
+      ) u_arb (
+        .clk_i,
+        .rst_ni,
+        .req_chk_i,
+        .req_i(req_buf),
+        .data_i(data_buf),
+        .gnt_o(arb_output_buf[i].gnt),
+        .idx_o(arb_output_buf[i].idx),
+        .valid_o(arb_output_buf[i].valid),
+        .data_o(arb_output_buf[i].data),
+        .ready_i
+      );
+    end
   end
 
   // the last buffered position is sent out

problem_statement:
## Description
The bug is in OpenTitan's flash controller (`flash_ctrl`), specifically in `flash_phy_core`, the block that arbitrates between an external host-side flash access and an internal controller-initiated flash operation before forwarding a request to the downstream flash macro.

## Expected Behavior
When the controller side issues an erase request while the `flash_phy_core` read stage is idle and there is no competing host-side request, `flash_phy_core` must grant that controller request and forward the corresponding erase request to the flash macro. The flash macro's acknowledge (`ack`) signal may legally remain low while idle and only assert after a request is presented, so controller-side progress must not depend on `ack` already being asserted before the request is sent.

## Actual Behavior
A controller-originated erase request can deadlock inside `flash_phy_core`. The controller request waits for a grant/readiness condition that is itself derived from the downstream flash macro's `ack`, while the flash macro waits to see the erase request before asserting `ack`. As a result, the erase request never reaches the flash macro and the controller operation never completes.

## Affected Function
The affected functionality is the `flash_ctrl` `flash_phy_core` arbitration and request handoff for controller-side erase operations to the downstream flash macro.

## Trigger Conditions
The failure occurs when a controller-side erase operation, including page erase, is issued while the `flash_phy_core` read stage is idle, no host-side request is competing for arbitration, and the downstream flash macro uses a request/acknowledge handshake where `ack` is asserted only after a request is presented rather than being held high while idle.

problem_statement:
## Description
The affected module is the Serial Peripheral Interface (SPI) Device IP's passthrough clock-forwarding path, which drives `passthrough_req_t.sck` toward the downstream SPI flash while the SPI Device is operating in passthrough mode. In this mode, the passthrough command filter can block configured command bytes instead of forwarding them. The forwarded downstream clock is expected to honor the passthrough clock-gating condition (`passthrough_req_t.sck_gate_en` in the current design), but it does not.

## Expected Behavior
When passthrough mode is enabled and the command filter identifies the command byte as blocked, the downstream transaction should be cut off immediately. The downstream active-low chip select (`CSb`) should deassert, and the forwarded downstream serial clock (`SCK`) should remain low even if the upstream SPI host continues toggling `SCK` until it releases `CSb`.

## Actual Behavior
After a filtered passthrough command, the downstream `CSb` can deassert, but the forwarded `SCK` still mirrors the upstream SPI host's `SCK`. As a result, the downstream SPI flash continues to observe clock edges for a command that the SPI Device has already filtered out.

## Trigger Condition
This occurs in the SPI Device passthrough command-filter path when passthrough mode is enabled, the upstream SPI host sends a command whose opcode is configured to be filtered, and the upstream SPI host continues clocking after the command byte has been rejected.

problem_statement:
## Description
The OpenTitan SPI Host (Serial Peripheral Interface host) IP executes a transfer as a sequence of segments. When clock phase 1 (`CPHA=1`) is used, the end of the final segment can be mishandled: the last bit of that segment is not sampled correctly.

## Expected Behavior
For a `CPHA=1` transfer, the active segment must remain in progress until its final data bit has been sampled on the correct serial clock (`SCK`) edge. The data captured for the final segment must match the bits present on the SPI data lines, including the last bit.

## Actual Behavior
With `CPHA=1`, the final sampling point at the end of a segment can be mis-timed, so the last bit of the final segment is captured incorrectly.

## Affected Function
This affects the SPI Host IP's `CPHA=1` segment-completion timing and sampling logic.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered when the SPI Host runs a transfer with `CPHA=1` and reaches the boundary where the final bit of the final segment should be sampled.

which triggers the unaling error check in the reg adapter.
is this expected behavior for this test? it looks like the register should behave as any other register.

+  localparam int ByteMaskW = DW / 8;
 
-  logic rx_we, tx_re;

+    .tl_i(tx_win_i),
+    .tl_o(tx_win_o),
+    .en_ifetch_i(prim_mubi_pkg::MuBi4False),
+    .req_o(tx_valid_o),
+    .req_type_o(),
+    .gnt_i(1'b1),
+    .we_o(),
+    .addr_o(),
+    .wdata_o(tx_data_o),

+    .intg_error_o(),
+    .rdata_i('0),

problem_statement:
## Description
The bug affects the OpenTitan SPI Host IP's `TXDATA` transmit window on the TileLink Uncached Lightweight (TL-UL) bus and the `ERROR_STATUS` register bits that can change as a side effect of bad transmit-window accesses. `TXDATA` is a memory-like FIFO window with byte-write support, not a conventional word-aligned control and status register (CSR).

## Expected Behavior
Writes to `TXDATA` that enable one or more byte lanes must be accepted using window semantics, even when the TL-UL address uses nonzero low bits to select a specific byte lane. These accesses must not return an alignment or access error merely because they are not word-aligned like a normal CSR write. Separately, `ERROR_STATUS` bits that are raised by invalid transmit-window accesses or TX FIFO overflow are hardware-updated status, so CSR verification must not assume they remain equal to the last software-predicted value after such traffic.

## Actual Behavior
The SPI Host transmit window is handled like a normal CSR path. As a result, byte-enabled or sub-word writes to `TXDATA` can be rejected with a TL-UL access or alignment error when the address low bits are nonzero, even though the target is a byte-write FIFO window. In the same stress scenario, side effects from erroneous `TXDATA` writes can change `ERROR_STATUS`, which then causes false mismatches if those status bits are treated as ordinary software-controlled CSR contents.

## Trigger Condition
The failure appears during randomized concurrent CSR and memory traffic to the SPI Host, especially when partial writes reach the `TXDATA` window at nonzero byte-lane offsets and resets are injected while traffic is in flight.

title: fix(spi_device): Missed Command Upload
body:
This PR includes #12714 . Please review the last commit only.

This commit fixes one of the issue https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/issues/11871

Problem:

    SW read incorrect opcode for Page Program.

Analysis
--------

The Page Program (0x02) opcode is adjacent to other commands that
SPI_DEVICE processes. So, the Datapath is fixed when the exact last beat
of the command opcode arrives. It is the second half of the 7th SCK.

The command parser activates Upload module at that time. However, the
top module switches the SRAM mux to the Upload module when the datapath
is latched by inverted SCK, which is right after the 8th posedge of SCK.

The Upload module, however, pushes the CMDFIFO entry (0x02 Page Program)
prior to 8th posedge of SCK to safely update the FIFO content as SCK
may not have 9th posedge if the SPI command is opcode only commands.
Examples are CHIP ERASE (0xC7), SECTOR ERASE, etc.

Resolution
----------

This commit revises the Mux design. Rather than using
`cmd_dp_sel_outclk`, it uses `cmd_dp_sel` (SCK clock) directly for the
SRAM mux. Other signals must be in inverted SCK clock domain to match
the output data phase.

resolved_issues.title: [spi_device] When and how should SW read cmdfifo, addrfifo, and payload buffer for correct data?
resolved_issues.body:
* spi_device should have a bit that indicates the completion of a SPI transaction and the FIFOs & the payload buffer are ready to be read from.
  * It looks like `cmdfifo_notempty` and `addrfifo_notempty` are updated independently during a SPI transaction.
  * According to the spec, `upload_payload_not_empty` in `INTR_STATE` register is updated after the transaction ends but it's not useful for commands without payloads.
  * `csb` in the `STATUS` register can possibly be used to check if a SPI transaction is complete but it is not clear whether sw can read from the FIFOs and the payload buffer right away.


* spi_device should ensure that values read from cmdfifo, addrfifo and payload are consistent with each other, e.g. they should always reflect the last transaction.
  * The address read from the address FIFO could belong to any command in the command FIFO (some commands don't have address fields), and similarly for the payload.
  * Please see [this thread](https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/pull/11884#discussion_r842004669).

cc @cfrantz @a-will

problem_statement:
## Description
The bug is in the SPI Device IP's command-upload path in flash/passthrough mode. Software uses the uploaded command FIFO to identify flash transactions that are forwarded through the SPI device, so the uploaded opcode must correspond to the transaction that software is about to process.

## Expected Behavior
In flash/passthrough mode, when software observes that the upload command FIFO is non-empty and reads `UPLOAD_CMDFIFO`, the opcode returned by that register must match the newly completed uploaded flash transaction. In particular, after software has already consumed an uploaded opcode-only erase command such as Chip Erase, a later uploaded Page Program transaction must be reported as Page Program (`0x02`), not as an empty or stale previous opcode.

## Actual Behavior
After an uploaded opcode-only erase command has been handled, a subsequent uploaded Page Program transaction can be reported through `UPLOAD_CMDFIFO` with an incorrect opcode instead of `0x02`. The value seen by software may be stale from earlier traffic, causing software to misidentify the Page Program transaction.

## Trigger Condition
The failure occurs in the SPI Device IP flash/passthrough upload path when command upload is enabled, software handles an uploaded opcode-only erase command, the flash is then polled with Read Status until the BUSY bit clears, and a Page Program command is issued afterward.

title: fix(spi_device): Re-timing sck_cmdfifo_set clear time
body:
Related issue https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/issues/11871

In previous design, the `sck_cmdfifo_set` signal is set by the ACK of
CMDFIFO write port and cleared by the FIFO DEPTH == 0.

THe clearing of FIFO depth depends on the SW processing time. This
commit revises it to CSb assertion pulse signal.

It is still bounded by the clock ratio between the SYS_CLK and the SCK.
SYS_CLK should not be 3 times slower than the SCK to correctly generate
the pulse signal within the opcode timeline.

      clk, h2d, d2h,
      32'(spi_device_reg_pkg::SPI_DEVICE_UPLOAD_CMDFIFO_OFFSET),
      tl_rdata
    );

    opcode = tl_rdata[7:0];
    $display("SW: Received Command: %2Xh", opcode);
    if (opcode != spi_device_pkg::CmdChipErase) begin
      $fatal(1, "SW: Unexpected Command: %2Xh / EXP(%2Xh)",
        opcode, spi_device_pkg::CmdChipErase);
    end

    tlul_write(
      clk, h2d, d2h,
      32'(spi_device_reg_pkg::SPI_DEVICE_INTR_STATE_OFFSET),
      1 << BitCmdfifoNotEmpty,
      4'b 1111
    );

    tlul_read(
      clk, h2d, d2h,
      32'(spi_device_reg_pkg::SPI_DEVICE_UPLOAD_STATUS_OFFSET),
      tl_rdata
    );
    if (tl_rdata[4:0] != 0) begin
      $display("SW: CMDFIFO not empty after fetching: %2d", tl_rdata[4:0]);
    end

    #3us;
    @(negedge clk);

    tlul_rmw(
      clk, h2d, d2h,
      32'(spi_device_reg_pkg::SPI_DEVICE_FLASH_STATUS_OFFSET),
      32'h 0,
      32'h 1
    );

    wait(intr.upload_cmdfifo_not_empty);

    tlul_read(
      clk, h2d, d2h,
      32'(spi_device_reg_pkg::SPI_DEVICE_UPLOAD_CMDFIFO_OFFSET),
      tl_rdata
    );

    opcode = tl_rdata[7:0];
    $display("SW: Received Command: %2Xh", opcode);
    if (opcode != spi_device_pkg::CmdPageProgram) begin
      $fatal(1, "SW: Unexpected Command: %2Xh / EXP(%2Xh)",
        opcode, spi_device_pkg::CmdPageProgram);
    end

  endtask : test_upload
"""
sw_pattern = re.compile(
    r"  static task test_upload\(\);\n.*?  endtask : test_upload\n",
    re.DOTALL,
)
if sw_pattern.search(sw_text):
    sw_text = sw_pattern.sub(sw_new, sw_text, count=1)
elif sw_new not in sw_text:
    raise SystemExit("sw upload task patch point not found")
sw_path.write_text(sw_text, encoding="utf-8")
PY

set +e
timeout 1800 bash -lc "

#!/bin/bash
set -e

# Stage 1: checkout base_sha in a clean workspace (+submodules)
cd /home/opentitan
git reset --hard
git clean -fdx
git checkout 74db12b7552dcb0e938183bca15bfa1f54b99e70
git submodule update --init --recursive

# Stage 2: install repository apt dependencies (if present)
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
if [[ -f apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing apt dependencies from apt-requirements.txt"
  cp apt-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  sed -i -e '/^$/d' -e '/^#/d' -e 's/#.*//' /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  if [[ -s /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
    apt-get update
    xargs -r apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends < /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
  else
    echo "[INFO] apt-requirements.txt is empty after filtering comments"
  fi
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
else
  echo "[WARN] apt-requirements.txt not found at 74db12b7552dcb0e938183bca15bfa1f54b99e70; skipping repo-specific apt install"
fi

# Stage 3: install project-specific Python dependencies from the checked-out repo
if [[ -f python-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Python deps from python-requirements.txt"
  python -m pip install -U pip "setuptools<66.0.0"
  cp python-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
  python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re

path = Path("/tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt")
lines = []
for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
    stripped = line.strip()
    if stripped in {
        "types-dataclasses",
        "types-pkg_resources",
    }:
        continue
    line = re.sub(r'(#egg=[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)\s+[<>=!~].*', r'\1', line)
    lines.append(line)
path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
PY
  python -m pip install -r /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt --no-warn-script-location
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
else
  echo "[ERROR] python-requirements.txt not found at 74db12b7552dcb0e938183bca15bfa1f54b99e70"
  exit 1
fi

# Stage 4: install RISC-V toolchain + Verible, then persist their PATH
if [[ -f util/get-toolchain.py ]]; then
  toolchain_version=""
  if [[ -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
    toolchain_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
  fi

  echo "[INFO] Installing RISC-V toolchain via util/get-toolchain.py"
  if [[ -n "$toolchain_version" ]]; then
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update -r "$toolchain_version"
  else
    echo "[WARN] RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION not found; falling back to util/get-toolchain.py defaults"
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update
  fi
else
  echo "[WARN] util/get-toolchain.py not found at 74db12b7552dcb0e938183bca15bfa1f54b99e70; skipping RISC-V toolchain install"
fi

verible_version=""
if [[ -f hw/tool_requirements.py ]]; then
  verible_version="$(python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path

ns = {}
exec(Path("hw/tool_requirements.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8"), ns)
reqs = ns.get("__TOOL_REQUIREMENTS__", {})
entry = reqs.get("verible", "")
if isinstance(entry, dict):
    print(entry.get("min_version", ""))
elif isinstance(entry, str):
    print(entry)
PY
)"
fi
if [[ -z "$verible_version" && -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
  verible_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG VERIBLE_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
fi

if [[ -n "$verible_version" ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Verible ${verible_version}"
  rm -rf /tools/verible
  mkdir -p /tools/verible
  verible_url="https://github.com/chipsalliance/verible/releases/download/${verible_version}/verible-${verible_version}-linux-static-x86_64.tar.gz"
  if curl -f -Ls -o /tmp/verible.tar.gz "${verible_url}"; then
    tar -C /tools/verible -xf /tmp/verible.tar.gz --strip-components=1
    rm -f /tmp/verible.tar.gz
  else
    echo "[WARN] Failed to download Verible from ${verible_url}; continuing without local Verible install"
    rm -rf /tools/verible
    rm -f /tmp/verible.tar.gz
  fi
else
  echo "[WARN] Unable to determine Verible version from hw/tool_requirements.py or util/container/Dockerfile"
fi

cat > /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh <<'EOF'
for d in /tools/riscv/bin /tools/verible/bin; do
  if [ -d "$d" ]; then
    export PATH="$d:$PATH"
  fi
done
EOF

if ! grep -q "/etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh" /etc/opentitan_bash_env; then
  echo "source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh" >> /etc/opentitan_bash_env
fi
source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh

if ! python -m pip show edalize fusesoc hjson >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[WARN] One or more Python tool packages are not visible in the active environment"
fi
if command -v riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[INFO] RISC-V toolchain ready: $(riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc --version | head -n1)"
else
  echo "[WARN] riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc not found after Stage 4"
fi
if command -v verible-verilog-lint >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[INFO] Verible ready: $(verible-verilog-lint --version | head -n1)"
else
  echo "[WARN] verible-verilog-lint not found after Stage 4"
fi
problem_statement:
## Description
In the OpenTitan SPI Device IP's flash Passthrough mode, where selected SPI flash commands are forwarded to flash but also uploaded to software, the command upload path does not always preserve transaction boundaries. After software consumes one uploaded command, later bus activity can leave the upload notification associated with the old transaction instead of the next completed uploaded transaction.

## Expected Behavior
Each uploaded SPI flash transaction must be reported exactly once after chip-select (CSb) is deasserted for that transaction. Once software reads an opcode from `UPLOAD_CMDFIFO` and clears the corresponding `upload_cmdfifo_not_empty` interrupt, later non-uploaded transactions such as `READ_STATUS` must not re-assert that interrupt or expose a stale command entry. When the next uploaded transaction completes, software must receive a new `upload_cmdfifo_not_empty` event, and reading `UPLOAD_CMDFIFO` must return the opcode for that new transaction.

## Actual Behavior
If software first consumes an uploaded opcode-only command such as `CHIP_ERASE`, intervening hardware-handled `READ_STATUS` transactions can leave the upload indication tied to the earlier command. The next wait for `upload_cmdfifo_not_empty` may therefore wake on a stale event, and reading `UPLOAD_CMDFIFO` can return `0x00` or the previous opcode instead of the opcode for the next uploaded command. In a later uploaded `PAGE_PROGRAM` transaction, software can therefore miss the new upload or read the stale erase opcode rather than `PAGE_PROGRAM`.

## Affected Function
The affected logic is the SPI Device IP flash command upload path in Passthrough mode, specifically the software-visible command reporting mechanism through `UPLOAD_CMDFIFO` and `upload_cmdfifo_not_empty`.

## Trigger Condition
This occurs when an uploaded command that ends after the opcode phase, such as `CHIP_ERASE`, is followed by one or more non-uploaded `READ_STATUS` polling transactions, and then another uploaded command such as `PAGE_PROGRAM`. The failure depends on software having already read the earlier uploaded command and cleared its interrupt before the later uploaded command arrives.

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

# Stage 1: checkout base_sha in a clean workspace (+submodules)
cd /home/opentitan
git reset --hard
git clean -fdx
git checkout ac635cc09becb1d184b34541d712f3e38de129f8
git submodule update --init --recursive

export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
PREP_TMP="/home/opentitan/.prep_tmp"
rm -rf "${PREP_TMP}"
mkdir -p "${PREP_TMP}"

# Stage 2: install repository apt dependencies
if [[ -f apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing apt dependencies from apt-requirements.txt"
  sed -e '/^$/d' -e '/^#/d' -e 's/#.*//' apt-requirements.txt > "${PREP_TMP}/apt-requirements.txt"
  if [[ -s "${PREP_TMP}/apt-requirements.txt" ]]; then
    apt-get update
    xargs -r apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends < "${PREP_TMP}/apt-requirements.txt"
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
  else
    echo "[INFO] apt-requirements.txt is empty after filtering comments"
  fi
else
  echo "[WARN] apt-requirements.txt not found at base_sha; skipping repo-specific apt install"
fi

# Stage 3: install Python dependencies
if [[ -f python-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Python deps from python-requirements.txt"
  python -m pip install -U pip "setuptools<66.0.0"
  cp python-requirements.txt "${PREP_TMP}/python-requirements.txt"
  python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re

path = Path("/home/opentitan/.prep_tmp/python-requirements.txt")
lines = []
for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
    stripped = line.strip()
    if stripped in {"types-dataclasses", "types-pkg_resources"}:
        continue
    line = re.sub(r'(#egg=[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)\s+[<>=!~].*', r'\1', line)
    lines.append(line)
path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
PY
  python -m pip install -r "${PREP_TMP}/python-requirements.txt" --no-warn-script-location
else
  echo "[ERROR] python-requirements.txt not found at base_sha"
  exit 1
fi

# Stage 4: install the toolchain and Verible, then persist their PATH
if [[ -f util/get-toolchain.py ]]; then
  toolchain_version=""
  if [[ -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
    toolchain_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
  fi
  echo "[INFO] Installing RISC-V toolchain via util/get-toolchain.py"
  if [[ -n "${toolchain_version}" ]]; then
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update -r "${toolchain_version}"
  else
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update
  fi
else
  echo "[WARN] util/get-toolchain.py not found at base_sha; skipping RISC-V toolchain install"
fi

verible_version=""
if [[ -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
  verible_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG VERIBLE_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
fi

if [[ -n "${verible_version}" ]]; then
  verible_asset="verible-${verible_version}-linux-static-x86_64.tar.gz"
  if grep -q 'Ubuntu-18.04-bionic' util/container/Dockerfile; then
    verible_asset="verible-${verible_version}-Ubuntu-18.04-bionic-x86_64.tar.gz"
  fi
  echo "[INFO] Installing Verible ${verible_version}"
  rm -rf /tools/verible
  mkdir -p /tools/verible
  curl -f -Ls -o "${PREP_TMP}/verible.tar.gz" \
    "https://github.com/chipsalliance/verible/releases/download/${verible_version}/${verible_asset}"
  tar -C /tools/verible -xf "${PREP_TMP}/verible.tar.gz" --strip-components=1
else
  echo "[WARN] Unable to determine Verible version from util/container/Dockerfile"
fi

cat > /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh <<'EOF'
for d in /tools/riscv/bin /tools/verible/bin; do
  [ -d "$d" ] && export PATH="$d:$PATH"
done
EOF

if ! grep -q "/etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh" /etc/opentitan_bash_env; then
  echo "source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh" >> /etc/opentitan_bash_env
fi
source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh

python -m pip show edalize fusesoc hjson >/dev/null
if ! command -v riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[ERROR] riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc not found after toolchain install"
  exit 1
fi
if ! command -v verible-verilog-lint >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[ERROR] verible-verilog-lint not found after Verible install"
  exit 1
fi

echo "[INFO] RISC-V toolchain ready: $(riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc --version | head -n1)"
echo "[INFO] Verible ready: $(verible-verilog-lint --version | head -n1)"

rm -rf "${PREP_TMP}"
problem_statement:
## Description
OpenTitan's Reset Manager (rstmgr) includes a leaf-reset consistency mechanism that watches generated leaf resets for unexpected child reset assertions or releases. The Always-On (AON) leaf reset `por_io_div4` is special: instead of only driving downstream logic, it is routed back into rstmgr as the block's own reset input. A shadowed copy of this leaf output exists as well.

## Expected Behavior
Because `por_io_div4` and its shadowed copy are part of rstmgr's own incoming reset path, they must not be treated as ordinary independently checkable leaf resets. When leaf-reset consistency checking is exercised, those two outputs should be excluded from consistency-fault checking instead of being expected to raise a leaf-reset consistency fault.

## Actual Behavior
The current rstmgr implementation includes `por_io_div4` and its shadowed copy in the normal leaf-reset consistency flow. If unexpected child reset activity is applied on either path, the same event can reset or shut down the checker before it finishes, so the consistency check for that leaf cannot complete.

## Affected Function
Reset Manager (rstmgr) leaf-reset consistency checking for the AON `por_io_div4` leaf reset, which loops back into rstmgr, and for the shadowed copy of that leaf output.

## Trigger Condition
The bug appears when the leaf-reset consistency mechanism iterates across reset leaves and includes `por_io_div4` or its shadowed copy, then applies unexpected child reset activity to that path.

title: [flash_ctrl/prim] Flash interrupt usability and modeling updates
body:
- Address some usability issues identified in https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/pull/12834

- Read level interrupt is intended to trigger
  when the flash read deposits more than N number of
  entries into the FIFO. Therefore trigger only
  when there has been a deposit and not on withdrawals.

- Similarly, program level interrupt is intended to
  trigger when the flash withdraws more than N number
  of entries from the FIFO.  Therefore trigger only
  when there has been a withdrawwl, and not on
  deposits.

- Added a couple of parameters that could be employed by a user
  to change the model read/program/erase latency

- This is especially useful for interrupt tests, as the default
  access latencies for read are too small to make interrupts
  useable.

repo.name: opentitan
repo.description: OpenTitan: Open source silicon root of trust

commits.message:
[flash_ctrl/prim_flash] Add parameters to tweak module latency

- Added a couple of parameters that could be employed by a user
  to change the model read/program/erase latency

- This is especially useful for interrupt tests, as the default
  access latencies for read are too small to make interrupts
  useable.

Signed-off-by: Timothy Chen <timothytim@google.com>

[flash_ctrl] Change level interrupt triggering condition

- Address some usability issues identified in #12834

- Read level interrupt is intended to trigger
  when the flash read deposits more than N number of
  entries into the FIFO. Therefore trigger only
  when there has been a deposit and not on withdrawals.

- Similarly, program level interrupt is intended to
  trigger when the flash withdraws more than N number
  of entries from the FIFO.  Therefore trigger only
  when there has been a withdrawwl, and not on
  deposits.

Signed-off-by: Timothy Chen <timothytim@google.com>

problem_statement:
## Description
In the OpenTitan Flash Controller IP, the program FIFO level interrupt (`prog_lvl`) is generated from the current `prog_fifo` depth without distinguishing whether that depth changed because software deposited data or because an active flash program operation withdrew data. As a result, `prog_lvl` can assert immediately after software writes program words into `prog_fifo`, creating a false indication that the controller is ready for a refill.

## Expected Behavior
`prog_lvl` is a refill interrupt for the program FIFO. It should assert only after a flash program operation withdraws entries from `prog_fifo` and the remaining FIFO depth reaches the configured program FIFO interrupt threshold. Software writes that deposit data into `prog_fifo` must not assert `prog_lvl`.

## Actual Behavior
During an in-progress flash program transaction, `prog_lvl` can assert as soon as software writes data into `prog_fifo`, before the controller has consumed any queued program word.

## Trigger Conditions
This appears when a flash program operation is already running and the program FIFO interrupt threshold is configured to a low value such as 1 entry. In that state, writing program words into `prog_fifo` can incorrectly raise `prog_lvl` even though no withdrawal-based refill condition has occurred.

## Affected Function
The affected logic is the OpenTitan Flash Controller IP's program FIFO level interrupt generation for `prog_lvl`.

problem_statement:
## Description
The OpenTitan Power Manager (`pwrmgr`) has a clock-domain crossing (CDC) bug in its escalation-reset handling path. The affected function is the logic that takes an escalation-reset request on `esc_rst_tx_i`, transfers it into the slow clock domain, and turns it into the escalation-triggered reset request path that drives the life-cycle reset request output (`rst_lc_req`).

## Expected Behavior
If `pwrmgr` observes an escalation-reset request on `esc_rst_tx_i`, it must capture that request even when the input is only a brief, non-permanent pulse that begins and ends between consecutive slow-clock sampling edges. After the request has been captured, the slow-domain escalation reset request must assert, `rst_lc_req` must assert, and the captured escalation request must remain asserted until reset clears it.

## Actual Behavior
When `esc_rst_tx_i` is only asserted briefly, `pwrmgr` can lose the request while synchronizing it into the slow clock domain. The escalation receiver can observe the pulse, but the slow-domain escalation reset request never asserts, `rst_lc_req` does not assert, and the escalation reset is effectively dropped.

## Affected Function
This affects `pwrmgr`'s escalation-reset CDC and request-latching logic between the escalation input and the slow-domain reset-request path.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered when `esc_rst_tx_i` is a transient pulse asserted for fewer than two slow-clock cycles, so the pulse can occur entirely between slow-clock sampling edges instead of remaining continuously asserted.

title: [kmac] Wait for rand_valid
body:
Previously, I was possible that under some circumstances the SHA3 core would set `rand_consumed` without `rand_valid` being set. With this PR, `rand_valid` is also checked in StPhase2Cycle2 inside the masked SHA3 core. In addition, the entropy generator will not clear `rand_valid` when a reseed operation is ongoing and the SHA3 core is processing non-key material with `fast_process` enabled.

We should probably run an FPGA experiment to confirm this does indeed not introduce unwanted SCA leakage.

repo.name: opentitan
repo.description: OpenTitan: Open source silicon root of trust

commits.message:
[kmac] Only compute Phase2Cycle2 if fresh randomness is available

Previously, we were unconditionally computing Phase2Cycle2 relying on
fresh randomness always being available. This assumption is based on
an earlier implementation where we used intermediate results for
remasking the DOM multipliers in Phase2Cycle2.

This resolves lowRISC/OpenTitan#12996.

Signed-off-by: Pirmin Vogel <vogelpi@lowrisc.org>

[kmac] Don't clear rand_valid while reseeding via EDN with fast_process

This allows the SHA3 core to continue processing data with fast_process
enabled while an EDN reseed is taking place. The SHA3 core will only
wait for the EDN reseed when absorbing key material.

This is related to lowRISC/OpenTitan#12996.

Signed-off-by: Pirmin Vogel <vogelpi@lowrisc.org>

problem_statement:
## Description
The bug is in the KMAC (Keccak Message Authentication Code) IP's masked `keccak_round` logic, which uses a `rand_valid`/`rand_consumed` handshake to obtain fresh masking randomness during a round. In the failing case, the round can behave as if a new masking random value has been consumed even after `rand_valid` has gone low, so the round continues with no confirmed fresh randomness available.

## Expected Behavior
Whenever the masked `keccak_round` reaches a step that requires a new masking random value, it must not consume that value unless `rand_valid` is high. If `rand_valid` is low at that point, the round must stall in place, keep `rand_consumed` low, and keep `complete` low. After `rand_valid` returns high, the round may consume the randomness, resume, and eventually finish.

## Actual Behavior
Under the affected condition, the masked round can assert `rand_consumed` or continue progressing while `rand_valid` is low. This breaks the intended entropy handshake and lets the round move forward without verified fresh masking randomness.

## Trigger Condition
This occurs in the masked `keccak_round` path after the round has already consumed one batch of masking randomness and then reaches the next step that requires another batch while `rand_valid` is low.

#!/bin/bash
set -e

cd /home/opentitan
git reset --hard
git clean -fdx
git checkout bcb8ab186cd93d79c9b1c34b4a612545595b6f4f
git submodule update --init --recursive

export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
if [[ -f apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing apt dependencies from apt-requirements.txt"
  cp apt-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  sed -i -e '/^$/d' -e '/^#/d' -e 's/#.*//' /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  if [[ -s /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
    apt-get update
    xargs -r apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends < /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
  else
    echo "[INFO] apt-requirements.txt is empty after filtering comments"
  fi
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
else
  echo "[WARN] apt-requirements.txt not found at base_sha; skipping repo-specific apt install"
fi

if [[ -f python-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Python deps from python-requirements.txt"
  python -m pip install -U pip "setuptools<66.0.0"
  cp python-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
  python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re

path = Path("/tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt")
lines = []
for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
    stripped = line.strip()
    if stripped in {
        "types-dataclasses",
        "types-pkg_resources",
    }:
        continue
    line = re.sub(r'(#egg=[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)\s+[<>=!~].*', r'\1', line)
    lines.append(line)
path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
PY
  python -m pip install -r /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt --no-warn-script-location
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
else
  echo "[ERROR] python-requirements.txt not found at base_sha"
  exit 1
fi

if [[ -f util/get-toolchain.py ]]; then
  toolchain_version=""
  if [[ -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
    toolchain_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
  fi

  echo "[INFO] Installing RISC-V toolchain via util/get-toolchain.py"
  if [[ -n "$toolchain_version" ]]; then
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update -r "$toolchain_version"
  else
    echo "[WARN] RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION not found; falling back to util/get-toolchain.py defaults"
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update
  fi
else
  echo "[WARN] util/get-toolchain.py not found at base_sha; skipping RISC-V toolchain install"
fi

verible_version=""
if [[ -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
  verible_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG VERIBLE_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
fi

if [[ -n "$verible_version" ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Verible ${verible_version}"
  rm -rf /tools/verible
  mkdir -p /tools/verible
  curl -f -Ls -o /tmp/verible.tar.gz \
    "https://github.com/chipsalliance/verible/releases/download/${verible_version}/verible-${verible_version}-Ubuntu-18.04-bionic-x86_64.tar.gz"
  tar -C /tools/verible -xf /tmp/verible.tar.gz --strip-components=1
  rm -f /tmp/verible.tar.gz
else
  echo "[WARN] Unable to determine Verible version from util/container/Dockerfile"
fi

cat > /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh <<'EOF'
for d in /tools/riscv/bin /tools/verible/bin; do
  [ -d "$d" ] && export PATH="$d:$PATH"
done
EOF

fi
source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh

  echo "[WARN] riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc not found after Stage 4"

  echo "[INFO] Verible ready: $(verible-verilog-lint --version | head -n1)"
else
  echo "[WARN] verible-verilog-lint not found after Stage 4"
fi
problem_statement:
## Description
The Alert Handler IP block exposes a `crashdump` snapshot so software and hardware can inspect the alert causes and escalation state that were present when an alert class reached its configured crashdump trigger phase. OpenTitan groups alerts into four classes (A-D), and software clears a clearable class by writing the corresponding `class*_clr_shadowed` register.

## Expected Behavior
After the Alert Handler has latched a `crashdump` for one escalation event, clearing a different alert class that has not escalated must not re-arm crashdump capture. If another class escalates later, the exported `crashdump` must still report the original snapshot from the first escalation event instead of being overwritten by the later one.

## Actual Behavior
Writing `class*_clr_shadowed` for an unrelated class that is still idle can re-arm the crashdump latch. After that happens, a later escalation in another class can overwrite the stored `crashdump`, so the output no longer preserves the first captured escalation snapshot.

## Affected Function
This affects the Alert Handler IP's crashdump latching logic, specifically the logic that decides whether `crashdump` remains frozen after an escalation or starts tracking live state again.

## Trigger Condition
Configure crashdump capture for an early escalation phase such as `Phase0`, let one alert class escalate and latch the snapshot, then clear a different class that has not escalated, and finally trigger a later escalation in another class. In that sequence, the original crashdump should remain unchanged.

resolved_issues.body:
This issue is similar to #10134, in that it involves recoverable alerts that are firing continuously.  In this case it is the 11 different `*_FIELD_ALERTS` which are designed to check whether a bad MuBi has been received.   Once a bad MuBi has been written the alert fires continuously until the bad MuBi has been corrected.

This was not caught previously because the up to now the only sequence that performed such tests did not use scoreboarding.  However now that this class alert events is being added to the scoreboard however, this is causing troubles with verification.  The alerts are firing continuously and do not stop until the bad register has been corrected.  However, there is no time for the sequence to identify the problem before the alert refires.  (Image below)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/47870387/179873222-e335035a-bd55-48c4-aeda-fa7ac1254e80.png)

This should be resolved by making the input to the alert primitives an edge sensitive quantity.

problem_statement:
## Description
The affected module is the OpenTitan Entropy Source IP, specifically the shared recoverable alert output (`recov_alert`) associated with the Entropy Source `*_FIELD_ALERTS` checks. These checks detect invalid MuBi (multi-bit boolean) encodings written into MuBi-protected control fields.

## Expected Behavior
If software writes an invalid MuBi value to a protected Entropy Source control field, the corresponding `*_FIELD_ALERTS` status bit should latch and `recov_alert` should be emitted as a single alert pulse for that event. After the alert receiver completes the alert handshake, `recov_alert` should return low even if the invalid register value is still present, so one bad programmed state does not immediately retrigger additional recoverable alerts. This behavior must hold for firmware-controlled MuBi fields such as `FIPS_ENABLE`.

## Actual Behavior
`recov_alert` behaves as a level derived from the latched field-alert condition instead of as a pulse. After an invalid MuBi value is written, the alert keeps re-firing or staying asserted until software corrects the bad register value, so a single field-validation failure produces repeated recoverable alerts.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered by programming an invalid MuBi encoding into a MuBi-protected Entropy Source control field that raises a `*_FIELD_ALERTS` condition, including the `FIPS_ENABLE` case.

#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

cd /home/opentitan

TMP_DIR=/home/opentitan/.tb_prepare
rm -rf "$TMP_DIR"
mkdir -p "$TMP_DIR"

# Stage 1: checkout base SHA and submodules.
git reset --hard
git clean -fdx
git checkout 780788efc8dc7669dbc7314a6026f8bacbc46f7e
git submodule update --init --recursive
mkdir -p "$TMP_DIR"

# Stage 2: install repository apt dependencies.
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
if [[ -f apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
  cp apt-requirements.txt "$TMP_DIR/apt-requirements.txt"
  sed -i -e '/^$/d' -e '/^#/d' -e 's/#.*//' "$TMP_DIR/apt-requirements.txt"
  if [[ -s "$TMP_DIR/apt-requirements.txt" ]]; then
    apt-get update
    xargs -r apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends < "$TMP_DIR/apt-requirements.txt"
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
  fi
fi

# Stage 3: install Python dependencies from the checked-out tree.
python -m pip install -U pip "setuptools<66.0.0"
cp python-requirements.txt "$TMP_DIR/python-requirements.txt"
python - <<'EOF'
from pathlib import Path
import re

path = Path("/home/opentitan/.tb_prepare/python-requirements.txt")
lines = []
for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
    stripped = line.strip()
    if stripped in {"types-dataclasses", "types-pkg_resources"}:
        continue
    line = re.sub(r'(#egg=[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)\s+[<>=!~].*', r'\1', line)
    lines.append(line)
path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
EOF
python -m pip install -r "$TMP_DIR/python-requirements.txt" --no-warn-script-location

# Stage 4: install the toolchain and Verible, then persist PATH.
toolchain_version=""
if [[ -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
  toolchain_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
fi
if [[ -f util/get-toolchain.py ]]; then
  if [[ -n "$toolchain_version" ]]; then
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update -r "$toolchain_version"
  else
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update
  fi
fi

verible_version=""
if [[ -f hw/tool_requirements.py ]]; then
  verible_version="$(python - <<'EOF'
from pathlib import Path

ns = {}
exec(Path("hw/tool_requirements.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8"), ns)
reqs = ns.get("__TOOL_REQUIREMENTS__", {})
entry = reqs.get("verible", "")
if isinstance(entry, dict):
    print(entry.get("min_version", ""))
elif isinstance(entry, str):
    print(entry)
EOF
)"
fi
if [[ -z "$verible_version" && -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
  verible_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG VERIBLE_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
fi

if [[ -n "$verible_version" ]]; then
  rm -rf /tools/verible
  mkdir -p /tools/verible

  verible_downloaded=0
  for suffix in \
    "linux-static-x86_64.tar.gz" \
    "Ubuntu-18.04-bionic-x86_64.tar.gz"; do
    url="https://github.com/chipsalliance/verible/releases/download/${verible_version}/verible-${verible_version}-${suffix}"
    if curl -f -Ls -o "$TMP_DIR/verible.tar.gz" "$url"; then
      verible_downloaded=1
      break
    fi
  done

  if [[ $verible_downloaded -ne 1 ]]; then
    echo "[ERROR] Failed to download Verible ${verible_version}" >&2
    exit 1
  fi

  tar -C /tools/verible -xf "$TMP_DIR/verible.tar.gz" --strip-components=1
fi

cat > /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh <<'EOF'
for d in /tools/riscv/bin /tools/verible/bin; do
  [[ -d "$d" ]] && export PATH="$d:$PATH"
done
EOF

if ! grep -q "/etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh" /etc/opentitan_bash_env; then
  echo "source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh" >> /etc/opentitan_bash_env
fi
source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh

python -m pip show edalize fusesoc hjson >/dev/null
riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc --version | head -n1
verible-verilog-lint --version | head -n1
problem_statement:
## Description
The flash controller exposes flash contents to software through a memory-mapped TileLink Uncached Lightweight (TL-UL) read window. The TL-UL adapter on this software read path contains an internal response FIFO. That FIFO is expected to implement the `FIFO.CTR.REDUN` countermeasure, meaning its read and write pointers are protected by redundant counters and pointer corruption is treated as a standard fatal fault.

## Expected Behavior
The software read-window response FIFO must use redundant secure pointers. If either pointer is corrupted, the flash controller must detect the corruption on that path and escalate it through the controller's standard fatal fault mechanism instead of continuing silently.

## Actual Behavior
On the software read-window path, the TL-UL adapter response FIFO is not configured with secure redundant pointers. As a result, corruption of that FIFO's pointer state can go undetected on this path instead of being escalated as a standard fatal fault.

## Affected Function
The affected logic is the flash controller's software read window, specifically the TL-UL adapter response FIFO that returns flash read data to software.

## Trigger Conditions
The bug is triggered when the pointer state of the software read-window TL-UL adapter response FIFO is corrupted, including either the read pointer or the write pointer.

## Implementation Constraint
The flash-controller software read-path response FIFO should implement its `FIFO.CTR.REDUN` countermeasure through the secure-pointer hierarchy rooted at the exact token `gen_secure_ptrs` under the response FIFO count logic, so the secure write-pointer count path is present for fault injection.

However, this still does not track the last byte host read. It latches

fix(spid): Latch read command address only for Readbuffer

Related Issue: https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/issues/14538

This commit revises logic to latch read address only pointing to the
read buffer space.

(`main_st` is `MainOutput`). Previous design latches `addr_d` (pointing
the next byte).

The current `last_read_addr` CSR represents the address field the module lastly latched.

It would be beneficial if the module represents the last byte the host read out from the read buffer

CC: @tjaychen @weicaiyang

This part seems incorrect.
addr_in_mailbox is low before all 4 bytes address is collected. And it stores 3 bytes address into `readbuf_addr` before addr_in_mailbox is set.

```
  always_ff @(posedge clk_i or negedge sys_rst_ni) begin

    end else if (addr_latch_en && sel_dp_i == DpReadCmd
```

problem_statement:
## Description
In the OpenTitan `spi_device` IP, the flash-mode `LAST_READ_ADDR` control/status register (CSR) does not reliably report the address of the last byte that the SPI host read from the read buffer. Instead, the register can retain an address value that was latched earlier during read-command processing, before the transaction has finished returning data.

## Expected Behavior
After a flash-mode read-buffer transaction completes, `LAST_READ_ADDR` must equal the host-visible address of the final byte returned to the SPI host from the read buffer. If a read command starts at address `A` and returns `N` bytes from the read buffer, software should observe `LAST_READ_ADDR = A + N - 1` after the transaction.

## Actual Behavior
`LAST_READ_ADDR` reflects the earlier latched read-command address state rather than the final byte address that was actually returned. In multi-byte read-buffer transactions, software can therefore observe the starting command address instead of the address of the last byte delivered to the host.

## Affected Function
This affects the `spi_device` flash-mode read-command path, specifically the logic that updates the `LAST_READ_ADDR` CSR for read-buffer transactions. The linked issue history also ties this bug to the same address-latching path used when distinguishing read-buffer accesses from mailbox-region accesses.

## Trigger Condition
The bug appears when the SPI host performs a flash-mode read that returns data from the read buffer, especially when more than one data byte is returned and software inspects `LAST_READ_ADDR` after the transaction.

problem_statement:
## Description
The bug is in the OTP Controller (One-Time Programmable controller) device interface functions (DIFs) that manage runtime check locks and software-partition read locks. The DIF code confuses the configuration lock (`CHECK_REGWEN`) with the check-trigger lock (`CHECK_TRIGGER_REGWEN`), and it still handles several lock-enable bits as if writing `1` would clear them even though the current hardware contract requires write-0-to-clear behavior.

## Expected Behavior
`CHECK_REGWEN` and `CHECK_TRIGGER_REGWEN` protect different OTP Controller operations and must be checked independently. Locking `CHECK_REGWEN` should block only runtime check configuration; runtime integrity and consistency checks should remain available until `CHECK_TRIGGER_REGWEN` is locked. When software requests any of these locks, the DIF must clear the relevant enable bit by writing `0`, because those lock bits use write-0-to-clear semantics. The same rule applies to read-lock registers for software partitions. In addition, a software-partition read-lock request must respect `DIRECT_ACCESS_REGWEN`: if the direct access interface (DAI) is busy and that write-enable bit is cleared, the DIF must return `kDifUnavailable` instead of issuing the lock write.

## Actual Behavior
The DIF checks the wrong lock register before starting integrity or consistency checks, so it can treat the trigger path as locked when only configuration was locked. It also writes the wrong value when trying to clear lock-enable bits, so configuration locks or software-partition read locks may not actually take effect. For software-partition read locks, the DIF can also proceed while the DAI is busy even though the hardware interface is not writable.

## Affected Area
OTP Controller DIF lock handling for runtime check configuration, runtime integrity and consistency check triggering, and software-partition read locks.

## Trigger Conditions
This appears when software exercises the OTP lock APIs after the controller moved to write-0-to-clear register-write-enable behavior, especially when integrity or consistency checks depend on `CHECK_TRIGGER_REGWEN` while `CHECK_REGWEN` is in a different state, or when a software-partition read lock is requested while `DIRECT_ACCESS_REGWEN` is low because the DAI is busy.

title: [i2c] fix how sda_interference is detected.
body:
- fixes #15067
- instead of checking the input value immediately after changing sda, we instead wait through the rise time and sychronization delays.
- After waiting through that delay, if the input does not match the output, then assert sda interference.

In the process of making this fix, the fsm was simplified a tiny bit on the host side.  The SetupBit states were removed since they do not serve any function.  There is no need for the host to wait until the setup window before driving its output.

Additioanlly, minor fixes were made to the testbench to correct some of the ack and nak sampling behavior.

Signed-off-by: Timothy Chen <timothytim@google.com>

resolved_issues.body:
credit to @a-will for discovering this.

the i2c sda_interference detection is done in the same cycle.
Meaning, if the i2c fsm decides to drive sda high, it must observe the incoming `sda_i` is also high in the same cycle.
This is impossible, as `sda_i` is synchronized and can never be the same value on a transition. Even if there were no synchronization, it could still be difficult for `sda_i` to be the same value in the same cycle because `i2c` is inherently an interface with slow rise times. 

This bug was masked by #15066.

problem_statement:
## Description
The affected functionality is the OpenTitan I2C IP host-side finite state machine (FSM) that raises the `sda_interference` event/interrupt when the host controller believes SDA (Serial Data) is being held low by another device. In I2C, driving a logical 1 on SDA means releasing the open-drain line so an external pull-up can bring it high. Because the sampled SDA input (`sda_i`) passes through an input synchronizer and the bus has non-zero rise time, the sampled value is allowed to remain low for a short time after the host releases SDA.

## Expected Behavior
When the host releases SDA and expects it to be high, the controller must allow enough time for a legal SDA rise to propagate through the bus and input synchronizer before declaring interference. On an uncontended bus, a clean host transaction, including a host read transaction, must not raise `sda_interference` just because SDA is still low for a few cycles immediately after release; the transfer should continue and complete normally.

## Actual Behavior
The host-side FSM checks for SDA interference in the same cycle that it changes SDA from driven low to released high. As a result, the controller can compare its newly released output against a stale synchronized low sample on `sda_i` and falsely conclude that another device is holding SDA low. This raises `sda_interference` during an otherwise valid transaction.

## Trigger Condition
This occurs in host mode whenever the controller transitions SDA from driven low to released high and the synchronized SDA input still reflects the old low level for one or more cycles because of normal rise-time and synchronization delay. One observable case is a clean host read transaction on an uncontended bus: after the host releases SDA, the line is briefly sampled low, and the design incorrectly flags `sda_interference` instead of allowing the read transaction to complete.

title: fix(spid): To not push cmdaddr for invalidlocality
body:
_Related Issue: https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/issues/15251_

As described in the issue above, the TPM module uploaded a CMDADDR entry even for an invalid locality command. The read command pointing to invalid locality space, TPM HW returns itself with `0xFF`. There's no need for SW to consume the command and process.

If SW wants to receive the command in any case, SW may turn off invalid locality feature and process the command manually.

problem_statement:
## Description
The SPI Device IP's Trusted Platform Module (TPM) frontend mishandles TPM reads to an unsupported locality. For a TPM register that the SPI Device hardware is supposed to answer directly, the hardware correctly returns `0xFF` for the invalid-locality read, but it also forwards the same command/address header into the firmware-visible TPM command/address path and can report that a TPM header is pending.

## Expected Behavior
When a TPM read uses an unsupported locality and the access is one that the SPI Device hardware resolves by returning `0xFF`, the transaction should be completed entirely in hardware. The SPI host should receive only `0xFF` response bytes, and no firmware-visible TPM pending state should be created: no command/address entry should be queued, no TPM header-not-empty interrupt or non-empty status should assert, and software should not need to clear any leftover state for that transaction.

## Actual Behavior
The SPI host receives the `0xFF` response for the invalid-locality read, but firmware still sees a pending TPM command/address/header indication for the same transaction. This leaves stale TPM state that software must clear even though the read was already completed in hardware, and it can interfere with later TPM transactions if it is left uncleared.

## Affected Function
The bug is in the SPI Device IP's TPM frontend logic that decides whether a TPM transaction is completed internally by hardware or uploaded to the firmware-visible TPM command/address path.

## Trigger Condition
This occurs when the SPI host issues a TPM read to an unsupported locality for a TPM register that the SPI Device hardware normally serves directly.

title: fix(spid): Latch FIFOADDR at correct time
body:
_Related Issue: https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/issues/15266_

This PR fixes a bug for unaligned access in TPM read commands.

fifoaddr is latched with the counter being `'h1F`. The counter, however, runs on SPI_CLK, while the latching logic is running on inverted SPI_CLK domain.

As a result, the latching logic captures the fifo address at a cycle earlier with prematured address. So it always assume address[1] as address[0].

This commit fixes the issue by:

1. Convert `sck_fifoaddr_latch` into iSCK domain.
2. To not shift the address one bit more, use `sck_cmdaddr_wdata_q` rather than `sck_cmdaddr_wdata_d`.

resolved_issues.title: [spi_device] read TPM HW reg with an unaligned address
resolved_issues.body:
@eunchan 

In this case, the address is 'hf05. Since TPM_RID is only 1 bytes, design should return 'hff.
Looks like the address latch point is half cycle earlier, so that it got 'hf04.
![Screen Shot 2022-10-04 at 1 41 46 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/49293026/193923306-21b56d0f-c677-4aa8-b425-2d03aba28dd8.png)

Waves and saved session:
/mnt/disks/filestores/opentitan-shared/users/weicai/scratch/fix/spi_device-sim-vcs/0.spi_device_tpm_read_hw_reg/latest

fix_patch:
diff --git a/hw/ip/spi_device/rtl/spi_tpm.sv b/hw/ip/spi_device/rtl/spi_tpm.sv
index e7ed24dc68e81..3348242081390 100644
--- a/hw/ip/spi_device/rtl/spi_tpm.sv
+++ b/hw/ip/spi_device/rtl/spi_tpm.sv
@@ -353,6 +353,8 @@ module spi_tpm
 
   logic [FifoRegSize-1:0] isck_fifoaddr; // latched from sck_cmdaddr_wdata_d
   logic                   sck_fifoaddr_latch;
+  // isck_fifoaddr_latch converts sck_fifoaddr_latch by half SPI_CLK period.
+  logic                   isck_fifoaddr_latch;
 
   logic isck_fifoaddr_inc;
 
@@ -523,8 +525,39 @@ module spi_tpm
 
   assign check_hw_reg = (cmdaddr_bitcnt == 5'h 1D);
 
+  // sck_fifoaddr_latch & isck_fifoaddr_latch.
+  //
+  // isck_fifoaddr_latch is used to latch `isck_fifoaddr` as the name implies.
+  // The sck_fifoaddr_latch is high at the last beat of the address field as
+  // shown below.
+  //           _   _   _   _   _
+  // SPI_CLK _/ \_/ \_/ \_/ \_/ \_
+  //           ___ ___ ___ ___ ___
+  // bitcnt   X 0 X ..X 1EX 1FX
+  //
+  // But the data is valid second half of the 'h 1F phase. However, the
+  // latching logic latches @ clk_out_i (Inverted SPI_CLK). So it latches at
+  // a cycle earlier.
+  //
+  //                       | err here
+  //            _   _   _   _   _
+  // iSPI_CLK _/ \_/ \_/ \_/ \_/ \_
+  //         ___ ___ ___ ___ ___
+  // bitcnt  X 0 X ..X 1EX 1FX
+  //
+  //
+  // isck_fifoaddr_latch delays sck_fifoaddr_latch for the logic latches the
+  // address correctly.
   assign sck_fifoaddr_latch = (cmdaddr_bitcnt == 5'h 1F);
 
+  always_ff @(posedge clk_out_i or negedge rst_n) begin
+    if (!rst_n) begin
+      isck_fifoaddr_latch <= 1'b 0;
+    end else begin
+      isck_fifoaddr_latch <= sck_fifoaddr_latch;
+    end
+  end
+
   always_ff @(posedge clk_in_i or negedge rst_n) begin
     if (!rst_n) begin
       sck_cmdaddr_wdata_q <= '0;
@@ -543,10 +576,9 @@ module spi_tpm
   always_ff @(posedge clk_out_i or negedge rst_n) begin
     if (!rst_n) begin

problem_statement:
## Description
A bug exists in the SPI Device IP's Trusted Platform Module (TPM) read path for TPM hardware-returned registers. When the SPI Device is configured in TPM FIFO mode and the SPI host performs an unaligned TPM read, the device can use the previous byte address instead of the requested byte address.

## Affected Function
The affected functionality is the SPI Device IP's TPM hardware-register read handling in TPM FIFO mode, including reads of hardware-returned registers such as `TPM_RID`.

## Expected Behavior
The SPI Device must return data for the exact byte address requested by the SPI host. For the 1-byte `TPM_RID` register at offset `0xF04`, a 1-byte TPM read from address `0xD4_0F05` must return `0xFF`, because that byte is outside the implemented width of `TPM_RID`.

## Actual Behavior
A 1-byte TPM read from address `0xD4_0F05` can be interpreted as a read from `0xD4_0F04`, so the SPI Device returns the `TPM_RID` value instead of `0xFF`.

## Trigger Condition
This failure occurs when the SPI Device is operating in TPM FIFO mode, TPM hardware registers are returned directly by hardware, and the SPI host issues an unaligned TPM read to a hardware-returned register. The reported failing example is a 1-byte read of `TPM_RID` at address `0xD4_0F05`.

In this waveform, EX4B(E9) is received and cfg_addr_4b_en drops for a short period then asserts again without receiving a new command.

![Screen Shot 2022-09-14 at 10 50 47 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/49293026/190325000-92f70c4a-0e47-4c86-b43b-bc388588c7c3.png)

Looks like it's because the next command comes too quickly, `spi_csb_asserted_pulse_i` is asserted again but `spi_reg_cfg_addr_4b_en_sync` hasn't been updated.
```
  always_ff @(posedge spi_clk_i or negedge sys_rst_ni) begin
    if (!sys_rst_ni) begin
      spi_cfg_addr_4b_en_o <= 1'b 0;
    end else if (spi_addr_4b_set_i) begin

      spi_cfg_addr_4b_en_o <= 1'b 1;
    end else if (spi_addr_4b_clr_i) begin

      spi_cfg_addr_4b_en_o <= 1'b 0;
    end else if (spi_csb_asserted_pulse_i
      && (spi_cfg_addr_4b_en_o != spi_reg_cfg_addr_4b_en_sync)) begin
      // Update
      spi_cfg_addr_4b_en_o <= spi_reg_cfg_addr_4b_en_sync;
    end
  end
```

Maybe we need to define the timing between 2 transactions to avoid this or try to fix it in the design.
