problem_statement:
## Description
OpenTitan's CSRNG (Cryptographically Secure Random Number Generator) accepts application commands through per-interface command staging logic (`cmd_stage`). The affected functionality is the CSRNG software application interface (`SW_APP`) command path in this staging logic. An unsupported application-command opcode can be accepted far enough into that path to leave the interface stuck instead of being rejected cleanly.

## Expected Behavior
If `SW_APP` submits an unsupported application command, CSRNG should treat it as a recoverable error without leaving that interface unusable. After the recoverable alert for the invalid request is handled and cleared, a later valid `instantiate` command followed by a valid `uninstantiate` command on the same interface should still complete normally and report successful completion.

## Actual Behavior
An unsupported command can raise the recoverable alert but still leave the `SW_APP` command staging path wedged. After that happens, later legal commands on the same interface may no longer complete as expected. In particular, a normal `instantiate` followed by `uninstantiate` sequence can stop reaching its completion indication even though both commands are valid.

## Trigger Condition
This is triggered when the software application interface receives an unsupported generate-like application command that also carries extra command words, i.e. a nonzero command-length field (`clen`). The failure is especially visible with a multiword invalid request such as the reserved `GENU` opcode with `clen = 2`.

title: [keymgr] Modify PRNG reseeding
body:
This resolves https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/issues/22877.

For details, please see the individual commit messages.

repo.name: opentitan
repo.description: OpenTitan: Open source silicon root of trust

commits.message:
[keymgr] Don't block PRNG reseeding operations while processing commands

A code comment mentioned that this was due to DV limitations but there
are no signs that this limitation still exists. Removing this
qualification of the seed enable signal is more efficient from an
entropy consumption viewpoint as the entropy is anyway requested but
just dropped in case of commands being processed currently.

Signed-off-by: Pirmin Vogel <vogelpi@lowrisc.org>

[keymgr] Change reseed counter to count PRNG updates instead of cycles

Previously, the reseed counter was counting clock cycles which was
problematic for the following reasons:
- Once started, the counter couldn't be stopped anymore and keymgr would
  repeatedly request entropy even if being completely idle. This is bad
  for power.
- The number of clock cycles since the last reseed operation is no good
  indication for the seed lifetime.

Therefore, this commit changes the design to only advance the counter
when the PRNG is updated. Such updates only happen while keymgr is busy
and the number of PRNG updates is a more accurate measure for the seed
lifetime.

This resolves lowRISC/OpenTitan#22877.

Signed-off-by: Pirmin Vogel <vogelpi@lowrisc.org>

resolved_issues.title: [keymgr] Reseed interval timer modfications
resolved_issues.body:
### Description

While debugging a ROM_EXT issue #22819, we've noticed that the reseed interval timer inside keymgr is active all the time and doesn't take into account whether keymgr is actually busy.

This means, once software has started keymgr, it will continuously request fresh entropy from EDN0 (by default 64 bits every 256 clock cycles). What's worse, if software decides to lock the [reseed interval register](https://opentitan.org/book/hw/ip/keymgr/doc/registers.html#reseed_interval_shadowed), there is no way to stop this afterwards. The max interval is 65536, meaning every 0.65 ms, a reseed is happening anyway. Because the reseed frequency is then not tied to activity, there is no way to program this adequately.

I am proposing to change the design as follows: The counter should not count the clock cycles but instead the number of PRNG updates. The PRNG is currently updated using `ctrl_lfsr_en | data_lfsr_en | sideload_lfsr_en`. I am suggesting to just feed this signal also into the reseed interval timer.

Any objections @moidx @johannheyszl @andreaskurth ?

problem_statement:
## Description
The OpenTitan Key Manager IP uses an internal pseudo-random number generator (PRNG) implemented as a linear feedback shift register (LFSR). That PRNG is periodically reseeded from EDN0, the Entropy Distribution Network endpoint connected to Key Manager. In the affected design, the reseed interval counter advances on Key Manager clock cycles after the block has started instead of advancing only when the internal PRNG state is updated. Because of this, the module can request fresh entropy from EDN0 even while it is idle and no PRNG updates are occurring.

## Expected Behavior
`RESEED_INTERVAL_SHADOWED` must define the number of internal PRNG updates between reseed requests. After a reseed completes, the counter must advance only when Key Manager activity updates the internal PRNG state. If the programmed interval has not been reached by PRNG updates, an idle Key Manager must not issue another EDN0 request merely because more clock cycles elapsed.

## Actual Behavior
After Key Manager is enabled and at least one operation advances the internal PRNG, the reseed interval counter keeps progressing with clock cycles even when the block is idle. Once enough idle cycles pass, Key Manager issues another EDN0 reseed request even though no additional PRNG updates have happened.

## Affected Function
The bug is in the Key Manager IP's PRNG reseed control, specifically the logic that interprets `RESEED_INTERVAL_SHADOWED` and decides when to request a new seed from the Entropy Distribution Network.

## Trigger Conditions
Program a small value in `RESEED_INTERVAL_SHADOWED`, enable Key Manager, and run an operation that updates the internal PRNG state. After that operation and any in-flight reseed complete, leave Key Manager idle. In the buggy design, another EDN0 reseed request appears after enough clock cycles, even though the idle period contains no PRNG updates.

problem_statement:
## Description
OpenTitan ROM_EXT (ROM extension) revalidates previously stored DICE (Device Identifier Composition Engine) attestation certificates in info flash pages before deciding whether they need to be regenerated. The affected logic is the X.509 serial-number validation helper in the silicon_creator certificate library that ROM_EXT uses for the UDS (Unique Device Secret), CDI_0, and CDI_1 attestation certificates. When an existing certificate encodes its serial number as a shorter ASN.1 DER (Abstract Syntax Notation One Distinguished Encoding Rules) INTEGER because the value starts with a leading zero byte, the checker can reject a certificate whose serial-number value still matches the expected attestation key identifier.

## Expected Behavior
The certificate validity check should compare the serial number by value and accept a valid ASN.1 DER INTEGER encoding even when the stored serial number is shorter than 20 bytes because leading zero bytes were omitted. In particular, if the expected serial number is a 20-byte value whose most significant byte is `0x00`, a certificate that stores the same value as a 19-byte serial number must still be treated as valid. In that case, ROM_EXT should keep the existing certificate and continue boot instead of treating the certificate as outdated.

## Actual Behavior
ROM_EXT can report an existing attestation certificate as invalid even though it matches the current attestation key material. In the reported FPGA flow, this appears as warnings that the UDS or CDI_1 certificate is not valid, followed by entry into the certificate update path and a ROM_EXT fault during the CDI_1 sequence.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered when ROM_EXT re-checks an already programmed DICE attestation certificate whose serial number begins with one or more zero bytes, so the ASN.1 DER INTEGER stored in flash is shorter than the fixed 20-byte expected serial-number value. Under that condition, the serial-number validation logic misclassifies the stored certificate as invalid.

title: [keymgr] Don't update and reseed PRNG in Disabled/Invalid state forever
body:
Previously, keymgr would keep updating and reseeding the PRNG forever once entering the StCtrlDisabled or StCtrlInvalid state. This is not ideal from an entropy and power consumption viewpoint.

This commit changes the design to - once one of the two states is entered - to keep updating the PRNG (which also triggers the reseed operation) until two more PRNG reseed operation have happened.

This also includes the keymgr_DPE specific changes of lowRISC/OpenTitan#23071.
This is related to lowRISC/OpenTitan#22997.

resolved_issues.body:
Previously, keymgr would keep updating and reseeding the PRNG forever once entering the StCtrlDisabled or StCtrlInvalid state. This is not ideal from an entropy and power consumption viewpoint.

This commit changes the design to - once one of the two states is entered - to keep updating the PRNG (which also triggers the reseed operation) until two more PRNG reseed operation have happened.

This resolves lowRISC/OpenTitan#22997.

FYI, once in the Invalid or Disabled state and after having stopped PRNG update requests inside the main controller, it's still possible that the PRNG is advanced and that reseed operations are started. E.g. if there are still some handshakes on the KMAC app interface or on the sideload ports (see figure below). However, once in the Disabled state, those are not going to be constantly active as before this commit. I think this should be okay.

problem_statement:
## Description
The OpenTitan Key Manager (`keymgr`) controller's pseudo-random number generator (PRNG) reseed control path does not become quiescent after the block is disabled. Once software drives the block into the terminal `Disabled` working state, the controller can keep autonomously issuing Entropy Distribution Network (EDN) reseed requests, which keeps the PRNG active and continues consuming entropy and power even though the block is no longer doing useful work.

## Expected Behavior
After `keymgr` enters the terminal `Disabled` working state, any immediately pending reseed activity may complete, but the controller must then become quiet. While the block remains in `Disabled`, it must not continue generating periodic autonomous EDN reseed requests or other controller-driven background entropy traffic.

## Actual Behavior
In the broken implementation, entering `Disabled` does not stop the background reseed path. If the design keeps running after the disable operation completes, `keymgr` continues to request reseeds periodically instead of going quiet.

## Trigger Condition
This is triggered after `keymgr` has been initialized, software issues a disable operation, and the block reaches its `Disabled` working state. If execution continues in that terminal state, the controller keeps producing periodic reseed activity instead of eventually becoming idle.

title: [hmac,dv/rtl] Implement DV checks for new digest sizes/key lengths
body:
This PR implements scoreboard checks for the new HMAC digest sizes and key lengths for normal operation and whenever secure wiping is triggered.  For ease of DV checks and consistency across configuration changes where previous digests remain held in CSRs until HMAC starts a new operation, this PR also removes the clearing of redundant digest values for the smaller digest sizes in the RTL. It also updates the documentation to clarify that SW should only read the relevant digest CSRs for the digest size configured - @ballifatih (only read digests 0..7 for SHA-2 256 and digests 0..11 for SHA-2 384, i.e., do not assume the redundant digest values in these sizes will be all-zero.)

This should also fix the failing hmac_wipe_secret test (https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/issues/23053) and close other pending DV TODOS.

problem_statement:
## Description
The HMAC (Hash-based Message Authentication Code) IP exposes the current digest through `DIGEST_0`..`DIGEST_15` control/status registers (CSRs), and those registers can continue to hold the previous digest until a new hash operation starts. In secure-wipe flows and in digest reads performed after changing the HMAC configuration, readback for SHA-2 384 and SHA-2 512 is not handled consistently with this retained-digest behavior. Smaller-digest layouts are still treated as if the unused DIGEST words must always read back as zero, which leads to digest mismatches when a retained or wiped digest is read.

## Expected Behavior
Digest CSR readback must be interpreted according to the digest size that produced the digest currently visible in the registers: SHA-2 256 uses `DIGEST_0`..`DIGEST_7`, SHA-2 384 uses `DIGEST_0`..`DIGEST_11`, and SHA-2 512 uses `DIGEST_0`..`DIGEST_15`. For SHA-2 256 and SHA-2 384, the remaining DIGEST words are not part of the digest and must not be required to read as zero. If `wipe_secret` is triggered, any digest still visible in the DIGEST CSRs must be treated as corrupted regardless of digest size or HMAC key length.

## Affected Function
The affected functionality is the HMAC IP DIGEST CSR readback path, including retained-digest handling across configuration changes and secret-wipe behavior for SHA-2 256, SHA-2 384, and SHA-2 512 operation.

## Trigger Condition
This is triggered when software or verification reads the DIGEST CSRs after a SHA-2 384 or SHA-2 512 operation, after changing digest size or HMAC key length while the previous digest is still retained, or after asserting `wipe_secret` before that retained or current digest is replaced by a new operation.

title: [hmac,rtl/dv] Fix digest loading/error wiping and error handling
body:
This PR depends on PRs https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/pull/23108 and https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/pull/23220 to get merged. It implements fixes in HMAC RTL and DV scoreboard for digest loading (based on @ballifatih's PR https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/pull/23197) besides additional changes to fix issues with secret wiping and error handling (prioritizing `SwInvalidConfig` in case of simultaneous errors) across different digest sizes. 

This also implements a potential fix for https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/issues/23181 but needs to be tested - would you test this @ballifatih and let me know if this sorts this out?

There is currently an issue when we  switch between streams with different digest sizes, caused by the gating behavior. Creating this issue so that we can keep track of it. The previous issue #23014 is closed.

An ugly workaround would be to run a dummy operation in-between two streams to set the digest size to the correct value. 

cc: @gdessouky @martin-velay  @andreaskurth

problem_statement:
## Description
In the OpenTitan HMAC (Hash-based Message Authentication Code) IP, invalid software start requests are not reported to software consistently. If software programs an invalid hashing configuration and then issues `hash_start`, the block may fail to present the expected software-visible error condition, or it may report a different start-related error instead of the configuration error. Invalid configurations include a `CFG.digest_size` setting that does not select a valid Secure Hash Algorithm 2 (SHA-2) mode, HMAC mode with no valid key length selected, and HMAC-SHA-256 configured with a 1024-bit key, which is not supported.

## Expected Behavior
When software issues `hash_start` with one of these invalid configurations, the HMAC IP must reject the request immediately, set `INTR_STATE.hmac_err`, and latch `ERR_CODE` to `SwInvalidConfig`. If the HMAC error interrupt is enabled, the `hmac_err` interrupt output must assert as well. This behavior must remain deterministic even when another start-time error condition is present at the same time, such as SHA being disabled or a hash operation already being active; in those cases, `SwInvalidConfig` must still be the reported error.

## Actual Behavior
With certain invalid `hash_start` requests, the software-visible error indication is not reliable. Software can observe a missing HMAC error event or receive another start-related error code instead of `SwInvalidConfig`, which breaks error handling for invalid start requests.

## Affected Function
The bug affects the HMAC IP command-validation and error-reporting path for start requests, specifically the logic that drives `INTR_STATE.hmac_err`, the `hmac_err` interrupt, and `ERR_CODE`.

## Trigger Conditions
This is triggered when software writes an invalid HMAC/SHA-2 configuration and then issues `hash_start`, especially when that invalid configuration overlaps with another start-related error condition.

tb_script:
#!/bin/bash
set -uo pipefail

cd /home/opentitan || exit 1

export PATH="/tools/riscv/bin:${PATH}"

TEST_NAME="manifest_address_translation"
TB_DIR="/home/opentitan/.tb_manifest_address_translation"

set +e
(
  set -euo pipefail

  rm -rf "${TB_DIR}"
  mkdir -p "${TB_DIR}"

  cat > "${TB_DIR}/min_boot.S" <<'ASM'
.section .vectors,"ax"
.globl _start_vec
_start_vec:
  j _rom_ext_start_boot

.section .crt,"ax"
.globl _crt_init
_crt_init:
  nop

.section .text,"ax"
.globl _rom_ext_start_boot
_rom_ext_start_boot:
  nop
  ret

.section .shutdown,"ax"
.globl _shutdown_stub
_shutdown_stub:
  nop

.section .static_critical.version,"aw",@nobits
.globl _static_critical_pad
_static_critical_pad:
  .space 8136
ASM

  python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path

tb_dir = Path("/home/opentitan/.tb_manifest_address_translation")
src = Path("/home/opentitan/sw/device/silicon_creator/lib/manifest_def.c").read_text(
    encoding="utf-8"
).splitlines()

addr_idx = None
manifest_version_idx = None
for idx, line in enumerate(src):
    if ".address_translation" in line:
        addr_idx = idx
    if ".manifest_version" in line:
        manifest_version_idx = idx

# GCC 10 accepts the repo source as C, but this minimal build uses C++ mode to
# sidestep older `_Generic` issues in hardened.h. C++20 requires designated
# initializers to appear in declaration order, so reorder this one field if it
# is present.
if (
    addr_idx is not None
    and manifest_version_idx is not None
    and addr_idx > manifest_version_idx
):
    line = src.pop(addr_idx)
    src.insert(manifest_version_idx, line)

(tb_dir / "manifest_def_build.cc").write_text("\n".join(src) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
PY

  riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc \
    -c \
    -I/home/opentitan \
    -Os \

module tb;
  localparam int OFFSET = 816;
  localparam int WORD_BYTES = 4;
  localparam int MIN_BYTES = OFFSET + WORD_BYTES;
  localparam int unsigned HARDENED_FALSE = 32'h0000_01d4;
  localparam int unsigned HARDENED_TRUE  = 32'h0000_0739;

  byte unsigned slot_a_data [0:2047];
  byte unsigned slot_virtual_data [0:2047];

  function automatic int unsigned read_word(input byte unsigned data [0:2047]);
    return {data[OFFSET + 3], data[OFFSET + 2], data[OFFSET + 1], data[OFFSET]};
  endfunction

  task automatic check_image(
      input string path,
      inout byte unsigned data [0:2047],
      input int unsigned expected
  );
    integer fd;
    integer bytes_read;
    int unsigned actual;
    begin
      fd = $fopen(path, "rb");
      if (fd == 0) begin
        $fatal(1, "failed to open %0s", path);
      end

      bytes_read = $fread(data, fd);
      $fclose(fd);
      if (bytes_read < MIN_BYTES) begin
        $fatal(1, "%0s too short: %0d bytes", path, bytes_read);
      end

      actual = read_word(data);
      if (actual !== expected) begin
        $fatal(1, "%0s offset %0d expected 0x%08x got 0x%08x",
               path, OFFSET, expected, actual);
      end
    end
  endtask

  initial begin
    check_image("/home/opentitan/.tb_manifest_address_translation/slot_a.bin",
                slot_a_data, HARDENED_FALSE);
    check_image("/home/opentitan/.tb_manifest_address_translation/slot_virtual.bin",
                slot_virtual_data, HARDENED_TRUE);
    $display("manifest address translation values are correct");
    $finish;
  end
endmodule
SV

  vcs -full64 -sverilog "${TB_DIR}/tb.sv" -o "${TB_DIR}/simv" -l "${TB_DIR}/vcs_compile.log"
  "${TB_DIR}/simv" | tee "${TB_DIR}/vcs_run.log"

  # On this VCS image, `$fatal` is printed to the transcript but the process

  if grep -q '^Fatal:' "${TB_DIR}/vcs_run.log"; then
    exit 1
  fi
  grep -q 'manifest address translation values are correct' "${TB_DIR}/vcs_run.log"
)

git checkout 28787642672f5c080f5aad009288ef3819486862

else

# Stage 3: install project-specific Python dependencies from the checked-out repo

  cp python-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
  python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re

path = Path("/tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt")
lines = []
for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
    stripped = line.strip()
    if stripped in {
        "types-dataclasses",
        "types-pkg_resources",
    }:
        continue
    line = re.sub(r'(#egg=[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)\s+[<>=!~].*', r'\1', line)

path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

problem_statement:
## Description
OpenTitan ROM_EXT (ROM Extension) images include a manifest field named `address_translation`. That field is not being selected from the final link address of the ROM_EXT `.text` section.

## Expected Behavior
For every ROM_EXT image, the manifest `address_translation` field must be derived from the linked address of the `.text` section. If `.text` is linked inside embedded flash (eFlash), `address_translation` must be `false`. If `.text` is linked outside eFlash, `address_translation` must be `true`.

## Actual Behavior
ROM_EXT images can be produced with an `address_translation` value that does not match where the `.text` section was linked. In particular, an image linked outside eFlash can still carry the same `address_translation` setting as an image linked inside eFlash.

## Affected Function
The affected functionality is the OpenTitan silicon_creator ROM_EXT manifest generation path that populates the `address_translation` field.

## Trigger Condition
The problem appears when building ROM_EXT images whose `.text` section may be linked at different locations, including at least one image linked inside eFlash and another linked outside eFlash.

title: [hmac,rtl/dv] DV synchronization and error handling fixes
body: This synchronizes the scoreboard checks for digest sizes 384 and 512, and once merged would close https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/issues/22578. This also implements a minor RTL fix with the loading from the message FIFO for SHA-2 384/512; this has no impact on functionality and digests computation, but aligns reading the words from the FIFO (and thus depth and status throughout) with what would be expected. This also implements additional DV fixes for the error handling checks when simultaneous errors are triggered.

resolved_issues.title: [hmac/dv] CSR read check commented out in scoreboard
resolved_issues.body:
### Description

In the HMAC SB, there is condition on "do_read_check" to enable data comparison. But this is commented out since mid-February.

problem_statement:
OpenTitan's HMAC (Hash-based Message Authentication Code) IP has a synchronization problem in the SHA-384/SHA-512 status-reporting path. CSR (Control and Status Register) read checking in the HMAC DV (design verification) scoreboard had been disabled because, in these digest modes, reads of the software-visible `STATUS` register can stop matching the scoreboard's expected view while a message is being consumed from `MSG_FIFO`. The digest computation itself is not reported as incorrect; the mismatch is in the visible progress and status behavior during the operation.

Expected behavior: when the HMAC IP runs in the SHA-384/SHA-512 path, `STATUS` must continue to reflect the engine's real progress, including FIFO depth / empty state and idle-versus-busy state, so CSR read checking can remain enabled. In particular, during a SHA-512 operation on a full 1024-bit message block, repeated `STATUS` polls while the block is being loaded and processed should stay consistent with the actual message-consumption state until completion.

Affected module: the HMAC IP's SHA-384/SHA-512 message-loading and `STATUS` reporting path, together with the HMAC DV scoreboard logic that predicts `STATUS` reads for these digest sizes.

Trigger condition: start a SHA-512 hash, write a full 1024-bit message block into the HMAC message FIFO, and poll `STATUS` while the block is being consumed and processed. Under this condition, the expected and observed `STATUS` values can fall out of sync, which is why CSR read checking had been commented out for this path.

title: [hmac,rtl] HMAC FSM fixes for SAR
body:
This implements RTL changes to the HMAC FSM to handle context switching (transitions to `StDone` to wait on hash result, and then `StIdle` from where every context ought to start/continue) and aligns triggering of idle and done. With this change, the SAR smoke test passes on @martin-velay's SAR DV branch (https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/pull/23116) which tests out SAR across 2 contexts (HMAC + same digest size 256). 

This hasn't been tested out thoroughly, and I think other issues will come up as DV proceeds. I'm also running a block-level regression at my end. @ballifatih this should close this issue https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/issues/23352, but I wouldn't be surprised if something else comes up next.

resolved_issues.title: [hmac, rtl] Reset hmac_core FSM to Idle after stop
resolved_issues.body:
### Description

I am trying to interleave two HMAC streams. Namely:

- Stream A (HMAC-384) starts and feeds some of its messages.
- Stream A is stopped and the state is saved to SW context.
- Stream B (HMAC-256) starts and feeds some of its messages.
- After around ~1000 bytes or so, Stream B hangs forever, and the initial symptom is MSG_FIFO being full. The test eventually fails with a timeout.

I tried to track down the signals which fetch entries from MSG_FIFO, and I eventually stumbled upon the main FSM of `hmac_core`. When I issue `start` for Stream B, I was expecting `sha_hash_start_o` (of `hmac_core`) signal to be raised, which does not happen.

I am looking at waveforms from a high-level, so I am not sure if it helps much, but here is the clock cycle when `start` command is sent over TL-UL (note the vertical marker). `st_q` of `hmac_core` is at `StMsg` even though HMAC  should have a clear state.
![image](https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/assets/7850700/79d486f6-fd10-42d8-b6b7-624e96957d39)

Maybe we need a condition to go to `Idle` state from `StMsg` state, when `stop` is issued to HMAC HWIP. I do not understand the full interactions here to make a confident suggestion though.  


https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/0e5093d7098daf6b9b848e5c1ca6242336e731d3/hw/ip/hmac/rtl/hmac_core.sv#L352-L370

cc: @martin-velay @gdessouky @andreaskurth

problem_statement:
## Description
During save-and-restore or context-switching use of the OpenTitan HMAC IP, software may stop one HMAC stream, save its state, and then start a different stream. In the reported flow, Stream A is stopped, Stream B is started, and after roughly 1000 bytes Stream B stops making forward progress: the message input FIFO (`MSG_FIFO`) fills and the operation eventually times out. In this failure mode, the HMAC core still behaves as if the previous context is active when the second `start` command arrives.

## Affected Function
The bug is in the HMAC IP's `hmac_core` main state machine, specifically the logic that handles a `stop` request, returns the core to an idle state, and accepts a later `start` during save-and-restore or context-switch flows.

## Expected Behavior
After software issues `stop` for an active HMAC context, the core should finish the current message block, become idle once that block's hash operation completes, and then accept a later `start` for a different context. In that situation, the new `start` must raise the internal `sha_hash_start_o` start pulse and processing of the new stream must begin so that `MSG_FIFO` continues to drain.

## Actual Behavior
If `stop` is issued near the end of a later message block while the first context is still in the inner HMAC message-processing phase, the core may fail to return to its idle state after the current block completes. A subsequent `start` for another context then does not raise `sha_hash_start_o`, so the new stream never actually begins and its `MSG_FIFO` stops draining.

## Trigger Condition
This occurs in HMAC save-and-restore or context-switching flows that stop one stream and start another while the first stream is still processing the inner part of a non-first SHA-2 message block. Reported examples include interleaving HMAC-384 and HMAC-256 streams, and the failure is reproducible in a long SHA-256/HMAC message when `stop` is asserted close to the end of a later block.

title: [spi_device] Block flash write commands when busy
body:
Block uploads, WREN, WRDI, EN4B, and EX4B when the busy bit is set. The state of the device should not change until the busy bit is cleared.

This may be especially important to avoid the payload buffer changing its contents while software is processing a command.

Fixes #21700

resolved_issues.title: [spi_device] Disallow certain state changes when busy
resolved_issues.body:
### Description

On a real SPI flash device, many commands are ignored when the device is busy. We might want to consider adding this behavior to our IP as well.

Currently, command uploads, WREN, WRDI, EN4B, and EX4B all are allowed while the busy bit is set.

problem_statement:
## Description
The bug is in the OpenTitan SPI Device IP's flash-mode command parser. When the device's busy status bit is already set from an earlier flash operation, the parser can still accept a new Write Enable (WREN) command and a new command that is configured to be uploaded to software.

## Affected Function
The affected functionality is the SPI Device IP flash-mode command parser, specifically how it uses the device busy status while decoding incoming flash opcodes.

## Expected Behavior
If the SPI Device is already busy when the opcode byte of a new flash transaction is received, the parser must treat a Write Enable (WREN) command and any command configured for software upload as no-ops. They must not start a new write-side action, and they must not be forwarded to software until the busy status bit is cleared.

## Actual Behavior
These commands are still decoded and acted on even though the device is already busy. As a result, the SPI Device can accept a new WREN command or forward a new upload command to software while an earlier flash operation is still in progress.

## Trigger Condition
This occurs when the SPI Device IP is operating in flash mode and a new opcode arrives while the busy status bit is already asserted from a previous flash operation.

title: [csrng] Locally escalate upon FSM errors
body:
Previously, these errors would trigger a fatal alert but not cause a local escalation (i.e. lock up the main SM). Since these FSM errors are structural errors that can't occur e.g. due to how the module currently operates but instead due to FI attacks only, these errors should also cause a local escalation.

This change better aligns CSRNG with EDN and ENTROPY_SRC.

This is related to lowRISC/OpenTitan#19789.

resolved_issues.title: [edn] FIFO error does not cause local escalation
resolved_issues.body:
### Description

Currently FIFO errors do not cause local escalation as can be seen in this snippet from the edn_core.sv:

https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/e13ff43f1b951c00ea2e24cafa60f7ac11d04e01/hw/ip/edn/rtl/edn_core.sv?plain=1#L295-L307

Other errors like counter or state machine errors cause the SM to enter an error state, while after a FIFO error the SM continues its operation. 

According to secure hardware design guideline [5.2](https://opentitan.org/book/doc/security/implementation_guidelines/hardware/index.html#recommendation-5-alerts) we should "prefer to take a local action (clearing/randomizing state, cease processing) in addition to generating the alert".

There could very well be a reason for not escalating locally but I couldn't find any reason in the documentation or in the lines of code above.

Should this be changed in the design (local escalation on FIFO error) or documented why *no* local escalation is preferable in this case?

fix_patch:
diff --git a/hw/ip/csrng/rtl/csrng_core.sv b/hw/ip/csrng/rtl/csrng_core.sv
index 9a78fdcf0efc9..a390f7131ae89 100644
--- a/hw/ip/csrng/rtl/csrng_core.sv
+++ b/hw/ip/csrng/rtl/csrng_core.sv
@@ -490,6 +490,17 @@ module csrng_core import csrng_pkg::*; #(
     .intr_o                 (intr_cs_fatal_err_o)
   );
 
+  // Counter and FSM errors are structural errors and are always active regardless of the
+  // functional state. main_sm_err_sum is not included here to prevent some tools from
+  // inferring combo loops.
+  logic fatal_loc_events;
+  assign fatal_loc_events = cmd_gen_cnt_err_sum ||
+                            cmd_stage_sm_err_sum ||
+                            drbg_gen_sm_err_sum ||
+                            drbg_updbe_sm_err_sum ||
+                            drbg_updob_sm_err_sum ||
+                            aes_cipher_sm_err_sum;
+
   // set the interrupt sources
   assign event_cs_fatal_err = (cs_enable_fo[1]  && (
          (|cmd_stage_sfifo_cmd_err_sum) ||
@@ -512,13 +523,8 @@ module csrng_core import csrng_pkg::*; #(
          fifo_read_err_sum ||
          fifo_status_err_sum)) ||
          // errs not gated by cs_enable
-         cmd_stage_sm_err_sum ||
          main_sm_err_sum ||
-         drbg_gen_sm_err_sum ||
-         drbg_updbe_sm_err_sum ||
-         drbg_updob_sm_err_sum ||
-         aes_cipher_sm_err_sum ||
-         cmd_gen_cnt_err_sum;
+         fatal_loc_events;
 
   // set fifo errors that are single instances of source
   assign ctr_drbg_cmd_sfifo_cmdreq_err_sum = (|ctr_drbg_cmd_sfifo_cmdreq_err) ||
@@ -1160,7 +1166,7 @@ module csrng_core import csrng_pkg::*; #(
     .uninstant_req_o        (uninstant_req),
     .clr_adata_packer_o     (clr_adata_packer),
     .cmd_complete_i         (state_db_wr_req),
-    .local_escalate_i       (cmd_gen_cnt_err_sum),
+    .local_escalate_i       (fatal_loc_events),
     .main_sm_state_o        (cs_main_sm_state),

   );

python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path


def patch_once(path_str: str, old: str, new: str) -> None:
    path = Path(path_str)
    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    if new in text:
        return
    if old not in text:
        raise SystemExit(f"failed to patch {path_str}")
    path.write_text(text.replace(old, new, 1), encoding="utf-8")


def patch_all(path_str: str, old: str, new: str, count: int) -> None:
    path = Path(path_str)
    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    if old not in text:
        if text.count(new) == count:
            return
        raise SystemExit(f"failed to patch {path_str}")
    if text.count(old) != count:
        raise SystemExit(f"unexpected patch count in {path_str}: {text.count(old)}")
    path.write_text(text.replace(old, new), encoding="utf-8")


patch_once(
    "hw/ip/csrng/dv/tests/csrng_intr_test.sv",
    """    `DV_CHECK_RANDOMIZE_FATAL(cfg)

    `uvm_info("csrng_intr_dbg", $sformatf("%s", cfg.convert2string()), UVM_LOW)
""",
    """    `DV_CHECK_RANDOMIZE_FATAL(cfg)
    cfg.which_err_code = cmd_stage_sm_err;
    cfg.which_app_err_alert = cfg.NHwApps;

    `uvm_info("csrng_intr_dbg", $sformatf("%s", cfg.convert2string()), UVM_LOW)
""",
)

patch_all(
    "hw/ip/csrng/dv/env/csrng_scoreboard.sv",
    "`gmv(ral.fips_force)[app]",
    "((`gmv(ral.fips_force) >> app) & 1'b1)",
    3,
)

problem_statement:
## Description
The OpenTitan CSRNG (Cryptographically Secure Random Number Generator) does not locally escalate when the CSRNG command-stage state machine enters an illegal state while CSRNG is actively processing a command. The fault is reported as a fatal condition, but the CSRNG main state machine does not lock up.

## Expected Behavior
If the CSRNG command-stage state machine detects an illegal state encoding, CSRNG must treat that structural fault as a local-escalation event: it must force the CSRNG main state machine into its terminal error or lockup state and stop normal processing, in addition to reporting the fatal condition.

## Actual Behavior
When a command-stage state-machine fault is injected, CSRNG reports the fatal condition, but the CSRNG main state machine continues running instead of transitioning into its terminal error state.

## Affected Function
The affected logic is the CSRNG core's local-escalation path from command-stage state-machine fault detection to the CSRNG main state machine.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered when the CSRNG command-stage state machine enters an illegal state while CSRNG is enabled and handling a command.

title: [csrng] Flush command FIFO after signaling ACK errors
body:
The decision whether a command is invalid is taken based on the command header but EDN might continue and send the additional data as well (it might already be in the FIFO). Previously, CSRNG would just pop the invalid command header from the FIFO and leave any additional data in the FIFO which can then erroneously be interpreted as the next command header.

Instead, we have to absorb the full invalid command before we can continue. This commit modifies the design to keep emptying the FIFO until the command interface is idle.

This is related to lowRISC/OpenTitan#23526.

resolved_issues.title: [edn] valid/ready protocol violations in case of ack errors and disablement
resolved_issues.body:
### Description

I noticed a couple of issues between EDN / CSRNG related to the CSRNG CMD interface:
- In case of disablement and in case of ACK errors triggered inside CSRNG, EDN can de-asserted the valid without waiting for the ready. Similarly, it can send less additional data than announced in the first command word (CSRNG cannot handle that).
- In case of ACK errors, CSRNG pops the erroneous word from the command FIFO. But the command FIFO may already contain additional data belonging to that command which may be left in the FIFO. Instead of just popping the FIFO, the FIFO should probably be cleared.

Both things are non-ideal but not catastrophic as we can always get out of these situations by disabling / re-enabling both EDNs and CSRNG which is anyway recommended in the programmer's guide right now. However, it would be better if those protocol violations wouldn't happen and if we wouldn't have to shutdown all CSRNG contexts because of an issue triggered by a single EDN.

problem_statement:
## Description
In OpenTitan's entropy complex, the Entropy Distribution Network (EDN) sends command packets to the Cryptographically Secure Random Number Generator (CSRNG) over a hardware application command interface. Each packet begins with a 32-bit header word and may include additional 32-bit data words, as indicated by the header's `clen` field. The bug is in CSRNG's command-stage handling when the header of such a packet is rejected immediately as an invalid application command.

## Expected Behavior
When CSRNG rejects a command from its header and returns an acknowledgment (ACK) error for that packet, it must consume the entire packet before treating any later FIFO entry as the start of a new command. All additional data words that belong to the rejected packet, as indicated by `clen`, must be discarded as part of that same rejected packet. The rejected packet must produce only its single expected ACK/error response, and a following valid command must still be accepted at the next true packet boundary.

## Actual Behavior
If EDN sends an invalid command header with `clen > 0`, CSRNG removes only the rejected header word from the command FIFO. Any remaining data words from that rejected packet stay queued and can then be decoded as if they were a new command header. This can create an unexpected extra ACK response and can shift the command stream so that a later valid command is no longer interpreted at the correct packet boundary.

## Affected Function
The affected logic is the CSRNG command-stage and command FIFO handling for the EDN-to-CSRNG hardware application command interface, specifically the handling of header-rejected command packets that still have additional data words buffered or arriving immediately afterward.

## Trigger Condition
This is triggered when EDN issues a command that CSRNG rejects immediately based on the first 32-bit header word, while the same packet contains at least one additional data word (`clen > 0`) that is already buffered or arrives back-to-back after the header.

problem_statement:
## Description
The Entropy Distribution Network (EDN) hardware-controlled command path to the Cryptographically Secure Random Number Generator (CSRNG) can violate the CSRNG command valid/ready protocol when CSRNG reports an acknowledge/status error while an EDN hardware command is already pending. The affected logic is the EDN path that issues hardware-controlled CSRNG commands, including the boot request mode sequence.

## Expected Behavior
After EDN asserts the CSRNG command-valid signal for a hardware command, it must keep that request asserted until CSRNG raises the corresponding ready signal and the valid/ready handshake completes. If CSRNG reports an acknowledge/status error before that handshake completes, EDN must still finish the outstanding handshake first. Only after the handshake is complete should EDN record the CSRNG acknowledge error, raise its recovery status, and move into its reject/error state.

## Actual Behavior
If CSRNG signals an acknowledge/status error while the request is stalled and CSRNG is still not ready, EDN can drop the command-valid signal immediately. This cancels the in-flight hardware command before the handshake completes and violates the EDN-to-CSRNG valid/ready protocol.

## Trigger Conditions
This happens when EDN is issuing a hardware-controlled CSRNG command, CSRNG is backpressuring the interface so the request is waiting with valid high and ready low, and a CSRNG acknowledge/status error is reported during that stall. A representative case is boot request mode, where EDN has started a boot-time instantiate or generate command and CSRNG is not yet ready to accept it.

title: [entropy_src/rtl] Delay the main_sm_done signal
body:
Due to the relocation of the 1-4-bit packer FIFO, the main SM done signal arrived one cycle too early in the single lane mode. This caused the SHA3 process_i signal to go high one cycle too early. This in turn caused the issue that the last word from the precon FIFO is not absorbed properly by SHA3.
This commit fixes this by delaying the main_sm_done signal by 1 cycle in the single lane mode. The ht_error signal has to be delayed by 1 cycle as well to guarantee that the error signal arrives at the same time as the main_sm_done signal.

Resolves #23773

resolved_issues.title: [entropy_src] Delay ht_done_pulse_i for the main SM by 1 cycle
resolved_issues.body:
### Description

Moving the 1-4-bit packer back in the pipeline #21626 introduced an issue where the `ht_done_pulse_i` can go high 1 cycle too early. This in combination with some other recent changes caused some unwanted words to be absorbed by SHA3.

When `ht_done_pulse_i` goes high this causes `process_i` for SHA3 to go high, which in turn leads to SHA3 not accepting any new inputs. If these signals go high 1 cycle too early SHA3 doesn't absorb the last word. The result were some test sequences that were failing due to a mismatch in the produced seeds.

I only observed it happening for the single lane mode, where one of the 4 random bit lanes is selected. This might be because the `post_ht` FIFO still receives the entropy without delay in normal operation.

Unfortunately I can't post a failing seed here for the `entropy_src_rng` test, since I had to change a lot in the DV environment to discover this bug.

problem_statement:
## Description
The bug is in the OpenTitan ENTROPY_SRC (Entropy Source) IP's hardware-conditioned FIPS seed generation path, specifically the handoff from the health-test completion logic to the SHA3 conditioner when `RNG_BIT_ENABLE` selects a single RNG lane. In this mode, the completion of a health-test window can be signaled before the final word from that window has been accepted from the pre-conditioner FIFO.

## Affected Function
The affected logic is the ENTROPY_SRC main state machine and SHA3 conditioning interface that convert health-tested raw entropy into a conditioned seed output in single-lane FIPS operation.

## Expected Behavior
When ENTROPY_SRC is generating hardware-conditioned FIPS seeds from a single RNG lane, SHA3 must not start processing until every word belonging to the completed health-test window has been accepted from the pre-conditioner FIFO. The resulting conditioned seed must therefore be derived from the entire completed window, including its final word.

## Actual Behavior
In single-lane mode, the health-test completion pulse can arrive one cycle too early. This causes SHA3 `process_i` to assert before the last word from the pre-conditioner FIFO has been absorbed. Once `process_i` is asserted, SHA3 stops accepting new input words, so the final word of the completed window is omitted and the resulting conditioned seed no longer matches the expected seed for that window.

## Trigger Condition
The failure occurs when ENTROPY_SRC is configured for FIPS hardware conditioning with `RNG_BIT_ENABLE` selecting one of the four RNG lanes, and a health-test window completes while the final pre-conditioner FIFO word for that window is still being handed to SHA3. Under that boundary condition, the conditioned seed output is generated from incomplete input data and can mismatch.

resolved_issues.title: [usbdev] OUT side STALL response can leave device unable to capture next SETUP/OUT packet
resolved_issues.body:
### Description

An OUT packet that elicits a 'STALL' response is neither acknowledged nor rolled back; in `usb_fs_nb_out_pe` neither 'out_ep_acked_o' nor  'rollback_data' (= `out_ep_rollback_o`) is asserted.

This means that if the packet is 62 or more bytes in length, the byte counting logic in `usbdev_usbif` is not reset in preparation for the next OUT/SETUP packet to be received and the packet size recorded into the RX FIFO is incorrect; the true size of the packet is unknowable.

The STALLing mechanism is used within current test software to declare 'protocol stall' in response to the DEVICE_QUALIFIER requests, but this does not break anything because only the IN side receives a STALL response for that Control Transfer, I think.

To reproduce, fetch draft PR sequence #23805 and run with the following seed:
```
util/dvsim/dvsim.py hw/ip/usbdev/dv/usbdev_sim_cfg.hjson -i usbdev_setup_priority_over_stall_response --fi 71923730856705723741826963384972440023047469689158980899448095559948831305837 --wa shm --tool xcelium -v m
```
If that somehow passes, try specifying '.randomize_length(0), .num_of_bytes(64)' to the task enable 'send_prnd_out_packet(..)'

This issues needs further consideration and clarification of what else may be impacted.
To be clear, this is with ES and prod RTL; it does not relate to the draft proposed changes.

@a-will, @vogelpi, @andreaskurth

fix_patch:
diff --git a/hw/ip/usbdev/rtl/usb_fs_nb_out_pe.sv b/hw/ip/usbdev/rtl/usb_fs_nb_out_pe.sv
index 6e116820200de..56aaff79ffbd8 100644
--- a/hw/ip/usbdev/rtl/usb_fs_nb_out_pe.sv
+++ b/hw/ip/usbdev/rtl/usb_fs_nb_out_pe.sv
@@ -288,6 +288,7 @@ module usb_fs_nb_out_pe #(
           // Non-isochronous OUT transactions end here
           if (out_ep_stall_i[out_ep_index]) begin
             tx_pid_o = {UsbPidStall}; // STALL
+            rollback_data = 1'b1; // Packet not accepted
           end else if (nak_out_transaction | out_ep_full_i[out_ep_index]) begin
             tx_pid_o = {UsbPidNak}; // NAK -- the endpoint could not accept the data at the moment
             rollback_data = 1'b1;
problem_statement:
## Description
The bug is in the OpenTitan USB device IP, specifically the full-speed non-isochronous OUT packet engine (`usb_fs_nb_out_pe`) and the receive-side bookkeeping in `usbdev_usbif`. When the USB device responds to a host-to-device OUT transaction with `STALL`, the rejected packet is not rolled back internally. Receive-side state from that rejected OUT transaction can remain allocated even though the USB host was told that the transfer failed.

## Expected Behavior
A `STALL` response to an OUT transaction means the packet was rejected and must not consume receive state. After a stalled OUT transaction, the USB device must discard the rejected packet's bookkeeping, reset the receive-side byte count for that packet, and be ready to accept the next receive transaction. In particular, if control endpoint 0 (EP0) stalls a long OUT transaction, the following SETUP packet must still be acknowledged and its receive FIFO (RX FIFO) entry must match the actual SETUP packet length and payload.

## Actual Behavior
If a non-isochronous OUT transaction is stalled, the receive bookkeeping is not rolled back. For OUT packets 62 bytes or longer, the byte-counting logic in `usbdev_usbif` is left uncleared before the next receive transaction arrives. As a result, the next SETUP packet, or another OUT packet, can be recorded with the wrong length in the RX FIFO and may not be captured correctly; once this happens, the true size of the affected packet cannot be recovered from the RX FIFO entry.

## Trigger Conditions
This occurs when an endpoint is configured to return `STALL` for a non-isochronous OUT transaction, the device receives a long OUT packet (reported starting at 62 bytes, including a 64-byte OUT packet), and another receive transaction follows immediately. The benchmarked case is control endpoint 0 (EP0): a 64-byte OUT packet is stalled, and the very next SETUP packet should still be accepted correctly.

resolved_issues.body:
### Description

Reported by: @meisnere 

`sw_alert_handler_ping_ok` test fails post synthesis. 

The root cause seems to point to glitches on `err_o`. This is a CDC error as it takes time for the sum to converge here: 

https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/e439226b6c5314be12ccf5cc055f2d4b8149d0ab/hw/ip/prim/rtl/prim_count.sv#L140-L143

CC @andreaskurth @vogelpi

fix_patch:
diff --git a/hw/ip/prim/rtl/prim_count.sv b/hw/ip/prim/rtl/prim_count.sv
index c0e77647f48f9..f70999c546bcd 100644
--- a/hw/ip/prim/rtl/prim_count.sv
+++ b/hw/ip/prim/rtl/prim_count.sv
@@ -140,7 +140,18 @@ module prim_count
   // The sum of both counters must always equal the counter maximum.
   logic [Width:0] sum;
   assign sum = (cnt_q[0] + cnt_q[1]);
-  assign err_o = (sum != {1'b0, {Width{1'b1}}});
+
+  // Register the error signal to avoid potential CDC issues downstream.
+  logic err_d, err_q;
+  assign err_d = (sum != {1'b0, {Width{1'b1}}});
+  always_ff @(posedge clk_i or negedge rst_ni) begin
+    if (!rst_ni) begin
+      err_q <= 1'b0;
+    end else begin
+      err_q <= err_d;
+    end
+  end
+  assign err_o = err_q;
 
   // Output count values
   assign cnt_o              = cnt_q[0];
@@ -190,7 +201,7 @@ module prim_count
       rst_ni
       |=>
       $past(!commit_i) || (cnt_o == $past(cnt_after_commit_o)),
-      clk_i, err_o || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
+      clk_i, err_d || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
 
   // Clear
   if (PossibleActions & Clr) begin : g_check_clr_fwd_a
@@ -199,7 +210,7 @@ module prim_count
             |=>
             (cnt_o == ResetValue) &&
             (cnt_q[1] == ({Width{1'b1}} - ResetValue)),
-            clk_i, err_o || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
+            clk_i, err_d || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
   end
 
   // Set
@@ -209,7 +220,7 @@ module prim_count
         |=>
         (cnt_o == $past(set_cnt_i)) &&
         (cnt_q[1] == ({Width{1'b1}} - $past(set_cnt_i))),
-        clk_i, err_o || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
+        clk_i, err_d || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
   end
 
   // Do not count if both increment and decrement are asserted.
@@ -218,7 +229,7 @@ module prim_count
         rst_ni && incr_en_i && decr_en_i && !(clr_i || set_i)
         |=>
         $stable(cnt_o) && $stable(cnt_q[1]),
-        clk_i, err_o || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
+        clk_i, err_d || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
   end
 
   // Increment
@@ -227,24 +238,24 @@ module prim_count
         rst_ni && incr_en_i && !(clr_i || set_i || decr_en_i) && commit_i
         |=>
         cnt_o == min($past(cnt_o) + $past({2'b0, step_i}), {2'b0, {Width{1'b1}}}),
-        clk_i, err_o || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
+        clk_i, err_d || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
     `ASSERT(IncrDnCnt_A,
         rst_ni && incr_en_i && !(clr_i || set_i || decr_en_i) && commit_i
         |=>
         cnt_q[1] == max($past(signed'({2'b0, cnt_q[1]})) - $past({2'b0, step_i}), '0),
-        clk_i, err_o || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
+        clk_i, err_d || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
     `ASSERT(UpCntIncrStable_A,
         incr_en_i && !(clr_i || set_i || decr_en_i) &&
         cnt_o == {Width{1'b1}}
         |=>
         $stable(cnt_o),
-        clk_i, err_o || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
+        clk_i, err_d || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
     `ASSERT(DnCntIncrStable_A,
         rst_ni && incr_en_i && !(clr_i || set_i || decr_en_i) &&
         cnt_q[1] == '0
         |=>
         $stable(cnt_q[1]),
-        clk_i, err_o || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
+        clk_i, err_d || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
   end
 
   // Decrement
@@ -253,24 +264,24 @@ module prim_count
         rst_ni && decr_en_i && !(clr_i || set_i || incr_en_i) && commit_i
         |=>
         cnt_o == max($past(signed'({2'b0, cnt_o})) - $past({2'b0, step_i}), '0),
-        clk_i, err_o || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
+        clk_i, err_d || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
     `ASSERT(DecrDnCnt_A,
         rst_ni && decr_en_i && !(clr_i || set_i || incr_en_i) && commit_i
         |=>
         cnt_q[1] == min($past(cnt_q[1]) + $past({2'b0, step_i}), {2'b0, {Width{1'b1}}}),
-        clk_i, err_o || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
+        clk_i, err_d || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)

         cnt_q[1] == {Width{1'b1}}
         |=>
         $stable(cnt_q[1]),
-        clk_i, err_o || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
+        clk_i, err_d || fpv_err_present || !rst_ni)
   end

fi

# Stage 3: install project-specific Python dependencies from the checked-out repo
if [[ -f python-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Python deps from python-requirements.txt"
  python -m pip install -U pip "setuptools<66.0.0"
  cp python-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt
  python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re

path = Path("/tmp/opentitan-python-requirements.txt")
lines = []
for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
    stripped = line.strip()
    if stripped in {
        "types-dataclasses",
        "types-pkg_resources",
    }:

    line = re.sub(r'(#egg=[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)\s+[<>=!~].*', r'\1', line)

path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
PY

problem_statement:
## Description
`prim_count` is OpenTitan's hardened counter primitive. It stores the count in two redundant internal shares whose sum should remain all ones (`2**Width - 1`). The affected behavior is the primitive's integrity indicator, `err_o`, which is intended to report that the stored redundant state is invalid.

## Expected Behavior
When `prim_count` performs a legal count update from one valid redundant state to another, `err_o` must remain low. In particular, a normal increment that updates the counter must not create a transient `err_o` pulse. `err_o` should assert only if the stored redundant shares are actually inconsistent after the update has settled.

## Actual Behavior
`err_o` can glitch high during a normal count update even though the counter starts and ends in a valid redundant state. This false pulse can appear in post-synthesis timing and can be interpreted downstream as a false Clock Domain Crossing (CDC) or integrity error.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered when a legal increment updates both redundant shares in the same cycle and the two shares do not settle at exactly the same time. During that convergence window, the sum check can temporarily observe an invalid total and pulse `err_o` even though no real counter corruption occurred.

title: [top_earlgrey,pinmux] Enable pull-down for TAP strap 0 at reset
body:
TAP strap 0 is sampled after reset (and only once for life cycle states
that are not TEST_UNLOCKED* or RMA).  To ensure it gets sampled as 0
unless driven to 1 from an external source (and specifically that it
gets sampled as 0 when left floating / not connected), this enables the
pull-down of the pad at reset.

This resolves issue #24576 on `master`.

Earlgrey's IOC8 pad is used as TAP strap 0. [TAP strap 0 gets sampled at least once at boot in every LC state.](https://opentitan.org/book/hw/ip/pinmux/doc/theory_of_operation.html#strap-sampling-and-tap-isolation) Thus if the pad is not properly pulled down on a PCB and gets sampled as 1 at boot, the pads used for JTAG are not available as MIOs until the next reset (even if the LC state does not allow JTAG debug). To prevent this, we need to activate the pad-internal pull down of IOC8 at reset.

~~As the pad attributes of IOC8 are part of a multireg, we currently cannot set their reset value separately. We probably have to extend our multireg syntax and features to allow this.~~

This change needs to be applied on the `earlgrey_1.0.0` release branch (an ECO confirmed by a local RTL modification has already happened) as well as on `master`.

problem_statement:
## Description
In the top_earlgrey integration, IOC8 is the muxed I/O (MIO) pad used as TAP (Test Access Port) strap 0. TAP strap 0 is sampled during boot, and the sampled value determines whether the JTAG (Joint Test Action Group) pads remain reserved for TAP handling or stay available as general MIOs. The affected functionality is the pinmux IP reset state for the pad attributes of the MIO pad assigned to TAP strap 0.

## Expected Behavior
During reset and immediately after reset release, before software reprograms pad attributes, the pinmux pad-attribute state for the TAP strap 0 MIO pad must have its internal pull-down enabled. With that reset default, a floating or unconnected IOC8 pad is biased low and TAP strap 0 is sampled as 0 unless external hardware intentionally drives it high.

## Actual Behavior
The pinmux reset state leaves the TAP strap 0 MIO pad without its internal pull-down enabled. If IOC8 is floating or otherwise not driven low when the strap is sampled, it can be observed as 1 instead of 0. In that case, the JTAG-designated pads are not available as MIOs until the next reset, even in life cycle states that do not allow JTAG debug.

## Trigger Conditions
This occurs on Earlgrey systems when IOC8 serves as TAP strap 0, the device reaches the boot-time strap-sampling window after reset, and the pad is left floating, unconnected, or not actively driven low before software updates pad attributes.

resolved_issues.title: [hmac] `HMAC_CMD_HASH_STOP_BIT` and `HMAC_CMD_HASH_PROCESS` commands causing hang conditions

problem_statement:
## Description
The OpenTitan Hash-based Message Authentication Code (HMAC) IP can hang while finalizing a SHA-256 hash when software writes the last message word into the HMAC message FIFO, waits briefly, and only then issues `HMAC_CMD_HASH_STOP_BIT`, the command that tells the hardware that no more message data is coming. The affected functionality is the SHA-2 finalization path inside the HMAC IP.

## Expected Behavior
After the last message word has been accepted, issuing `HMAC_CMD_HASH_STOP_BIT` after a short delay must still finalize the pending message block, report that the hash operation is complete, and return the HMAC IP to idle. In software-visible terms, the idle bit in `HMAC.STATUS` (`hmac_idle`) must become set again instead of remaining cleared. This must also hold when the message length is exactly one full 512-bit SHA-256 block.

## Actual Behavior
With a short delay between the final FIFO write and `HMAC_CMD_HASH_STOP_BIT`, the hash operation can remain stuck in a non-idle state. Completion is never reported, `HMAC.STATUS.hmac_idle` stays cleared, and software waiting for the HMAC hardware to become idle can block indefinitely.

## Trigger Condition
This occurs when a block-aligned SHA-256 message is written to the HMAC message FIFO, the final 32-bit word completes the last 512-bit block, no further message words are written, and `HMAC_CMD_HASH_STOP_BIT` is issued only after a small delay such as interrupt latency.

title: [pwrmgr] Take external SoC reset into account in FSM
body:
1. Internally generated reset request passed to SoC.
2. Create a sticky assertion internally to log request. Sticky flag cleared only upon external reset deassertion.
3. SoC transfers this request to platform to assert external reset.
4. External SoC reset deasserts after some time.
5. Pwrmgr stays in FastPwrStateRstWait state until the external SoC reset deasserts.
6. Boot / reset sequence continues.
7. Also fixes the external reset signal glitch filter to use the por reset. This is required to make sure that the external reset state does not self-reset once asserted and faithfully forwards that state to pwrmgr.
8. Added some debug visibility signals for pwrmgr.
9. Added temporary reset loop back path in pwrmgr TB to translate internal reset req from OT --> ext reset from SoC to OT.  Needs a proper fix in testbench (issue #22710).

problem_statement:
## Description
OpenTitan's Power Manager (`pwrmgr`) controls reset sequencing and decides when the system can resume boot. When `pwrmgr` forwards an internally generated non-power-on reset request to an external SoC (system-on-chip) or platform reset controller, OpenTitan is expected to stay in reset until that external reset has been asserted and then deasserted.

## Expected Behavior
After an internal non-power-on reset request is handed off to the SoC/platform, the `pwrmgr` fast power finite-state machine (FSM) must remain in its reset-wait phase until the corresponding external reset cycle is fully complete. During that interval, `pwrmgr` must keep the system reset request asserted and keep processor instruction fetch disabled both before the external reset is asserted and while the external reset remains asserted. Normal boot may resume only after the external reset is deasserted.

## Actual Behavior
`pwrmgr` can treat the handoff as complete as soon as the original internal reset request clears. If the external reset is asserted later or remains asserted for longer, the FSM can leave the reset-wait phase too early, release the system reset request, and resume boot / processor fetch before the external reset cycle has finished.

## Affected Function
The bug is in the Power Manager (`pwrmgr`) fast power FSM logic that handles non-power-on reset handoff from an internally generated OpenTitan reset request to an externally driven SoC/platform reset.

## Trigger Condition
This occurs for an internally generated non-power-on reset, such as a software reset request, when the request is exported to the SoC/platform and the original internal request clears before the externally driven reset has completed its full assert/deassert cycle.

commits.message:
[keymgr_dpe, dv] Remove flash initialization

regular keymgr. This commit removes a spurious flash initialization in
the DV that resulted in a compilation failure.

Signed-off-by: Andrea Caforio <andrea.caforio@lowrisc.org>

[keymgr_dpe, rtl] Correct DPE policy bit order

The complete set of DV tests for keymgr_dpe was failing due to a

The keymgr_dpe KMAC maximum input width differs from the regular

It addresses issue #25994.

resolved_issues.title: [keymgr_dpe] Seed material going into creator root key
resolved_issues.body:
### Description

keymgr_dpe seems not to inlclude all the seed material into the creator root key it is meant to (see 
https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/master/hw/ip/keymgr_dpe/rtl/keymgr_dpe.sv#L460-L469). More precisely, we have
```sv
    adv_matrix[Creator] = AdvDataWidth'({sw_binding,     // 256b
                                        revision_seed,   // 256b
                                        otp_device_id_i, // 256b
                                        lc_keymgr_div_i, // 128b
                                        rom_digests,     // 512b
                                        creator_seed});  // 256b
```
This adds up to a total of 1664 bits whereas `AdvDataWidth` is just 1152 bits.

This means the `revision_seed` as well as the `sw_binding` are not actually included in the creator root key. All remaining values either come from OTP or ROM and as a result there is currently no way to modify the creator root key. I don't think this is intentional but an oversight and we need to decide how to fix this.

The most obvious option is to define a keymgre_dpe custom `AdvDataWidth` parameter that is set to 1664. (keymgr should remain untouched)
Any ideas anyone? @ballifatih , @sameo , @Razer6 

For comparison, the regular keymgr in Earlgrey constructs the adv_matrix as follows:
```sv
  assign adv_matrix[Creator] = AdvDataWidth'({sw_binding,        // 256b
                                              otp_device_id_i,   // 256b
                                              lc_keymgr_div_i,   // 128b
                                              rom_digest_i.data, // 256b - Note there is just one ROM digest for Earlgrey instead of 2.
                                              revision_seed});   // 256b
```
We changed this before the Earlgrey production tapeout (see #22878 for details).

problem_statement:
## Description
In OpenTitan's Key Manager DPE (`keymgr_dpe`) IP, an advance operation that derives the creator root key from a source slot at the Creator boot stage (`boot_stage = 0`) does not pass all intended seed material to the Keccak Message Authentication Code (KMAC) input. The Creator-stage advance message is supposed to concatenate the software binding value (`sw_binding`, 256 bits), the hardware revision seed (`revision_seed`, 256 bits), the One-Time Programmable (OTP) device identifier (256 bits), the life cycle key-manager diversification value (128 bits), two Read-Only Memory (ROM) digests (512 bits total), and the creator seed (256 bits), for 1664 bits in total. Instead, only 1152 bits are forwarded, so the leading 512 bits are truncated.

## Expected Behavior
When `keymgr_dpe` performs an advance operation from a source slot at the Creator boot stage, the KMAC message for creator root key derivation must include all 1664 bits of Creator-stage seed material in the defined order: software binding, hardware revision seed, OTP device identifier, life cycle diversification value, both ROM digests, and creator seed. The software binding and hardware revision seed must participate in the derivation and must not be dropped before the KMAC request is issued.

## Actual Behavior
The Creator-stage advance message is truncated to 1152 bits before it reaches KMAC. As a result, the software binding and hardware revision seed do not contribute to the creator root key derivation, and the KMAC request only includes the remaining OTP- and ROM-backed inputs plus the creator seed.

## Affected Function
This affects the `keymgr_dpe` Creator boot-stage advance path, specifically the logic that assembles and forwards the advance-operation message to the KMAC interface for creator root key derivation.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered when `keymgr_dpe` executes an advance operation whose source slot is at the Creator boot stage (`boot_stage = 0`), which is the path that constructs the creator root key input from software binding, hardware revision seed, OTP device ID, life cycle diversification data, ROM digests, and creator seed.

The issue is due to `deny_mask`, it is a common signal for read, write and execute, but I think it cannot be. I'll push a PR proposal to fix this soon.

problem_statement:
The Access Control Range Check (`ac_range_check`) IP filters TileLink Uncached Lightweight (TL-UL) requests against configured address ranges and permissions. If a request matches multiple enabled ranges, the lowest-index matching range has priority and is supposed to determine whether that specific access type is allowed.

The current RTL can violate that priority rule when overlapping enabled ranges disagree on permissions by access type. In particular, a higher-priority range that denies reads but allows writes can be overridden by a lower-priority overlapping range that allows reads but denies writes, causing a read request that hits both ranges to be forwarded even though the higher-priority range should block it.

Expected behavior is that `ac_range_check` resolves permissions per requested access type using the highest-priority matching range. In the overlapping-range scenario above, the read must be denied: the filtered TL-UL request must not be forwarded, the module must generate its deny response, and, when deny logging is enabled, `LOG_STATUS.deny_range_index` must report the index of the range that actually caused the deny. The same overlap must still allow the write request, because the highest-priority matching range permits writes.

Trigger condition: at least two enabled `ac_range_check` ranges overlap on the same address, the lower-index range has higher priority, and the overlapping ranges grant different access types for that address. The bug is visible when a request uses an access type that the highest-priority matching range denies but a lower-priority matching range allows.

title: [usbdev] Support conditional updates of the `rxenable_out` register
body:
This PR implements conditional changes to the enabled/disabled state of OUT transaction reception (`rxenable_out`) as described in #27434 in order to avoids a software/hardware race when the `set_nak_out` functionality is in use.

The register is implemented as `hwext` so that write enables may be supplied in the upper half-word, corresponding to new enable states (for those to be changed) in the lower half-word (USB supports a maximum of 16 OUT endpoints).

A follow-up PR implements a block-level DV sequence. The DV changes in this PR are necessary to keep the existing tests building and passing.

Fixes #27434

repo.name: opentitan
repo.description: OpenTitan: Open source silicon root of trust

commits.message:
[usbdev] Conditional update of rxenable_out register

Avoid a sw-hw race in which the USB device may disable OUT packet
reception on an endpoint - because of the set_nak_out functionality -
and software then re-enables OUT packet on that endpoint when it
was simply trying to re-enable OUT packet reception on another
active endpoint.

This is achieved by including 'preserve' bits in the upper half of
word writes to the rxenable_out register; software may then update
only the endpoint(s) it wants to affect.

The use of 'preserve' bits, along with the priority of software writes
over hardware clears achieves backwards compatibility whilst allowing
firmware to be simplified on future versions of the USB device.

Signed-off-by: Adrian Lees <a.lees@lowrisc.org>

[dif/usbdev] Update DIF to modify selected rxenable_out bit(s)

Implement conditional update of the rxenable_out.out bit(s) to
avoid race with any other endpoints that are active and are
configured to accept only a single OUT packet before NAKing.

Signed-off-by: Adrian Lees <a.lees@lowrisc.org>

resolved_issues.title: [USB] Interface for rxenable_out with set_nak_out is non-atomic
resolved_issues.body:
### Description

After much debugging, I am pretty sure I have tracked down a rare race condition that is currently impossible to avoid with the current register interface for `rxenable_out` when `set_nak_out` is enabled. The race condition occurs because both software and hardware are writing to `rxenable_out` at the same time, but the register is `rw` instead of an atomic safe interface.

This is the situation:
  * `set_nak_out` is enabled for all endpoints (i.e. `0xfff`)
  * An OUT packet comes in on endpoint 3
      *  Hardware immediately clears `(1 << 3)` in `rxenable_out`. Value of `rxenable_out` is `0xf7`.
   * Software processes endpoint 3 packet and can now receive another on that endpoint
   * Software must read-modify-write `rxenable_out`, however this can happen:
      * Software reads `rxenable_out` value as `0xf7`
      * USB HW peripheral receives a packet on endpoint 2 and clears bit `(1 << 2)` in `rxenable_out`. Value of `rxenable_out` is now `0xf3`.
      * Software sets bit `(1 << 3)` high again and write back `0xff` to `rxenable_out`
      * Now we have re-enabled endpoint 2 unintentionally even though software isn't ready for another packet on endpoint 2

I cannot figure out a way to prevent this race condition from occurring. It seems that the register interface for `rxenable_out` should be converted to two `rw1s` registers that either enable or disable `rxenable_out` so software has a option atomically enable/disable just a single endpoint.

problem_statement:
## Description
OpenTitan's USB device (`usbdev`) IP uses the `rxenable_out` control/status register (CSR) to decide which OUT endpoints are allowed to accept USB OUT transactions. When `set_nak_out` is enabled for an endpoint, hardware automatically clears that endpoint's `rxenable_out` bit after one OUT packet so later packets on that endpoint are answered with a negative acknowledgement (NAK) until firmware explicitly re-enables it.

The current `rxenable_out` behavior is not safe when software needs to change one endpoint while hardware may clear another endpoint at the same time. Because software must use a read-modify-write sequence, a concurrent hardware clear can be lost and an endpoint can be re-enabled unintentionally.

## Expected Behavior
The `rxenable_out` CSR must support conditional per-endpoint updates in a single write to the same register. Software must be able to change only the targeted OUT endpoint enables while leaving all untargeted endpoints at their current values, and a write that targets all endpoints must still replace the full OUT-enable bitmap as requested. Reads of `rxenable_out` must continue to report the current OUT-enable state.

## Actual Behavior
Any write to `rxenable_out` overwrites the entire OUT-enable bitmap. If firmware reads the register, changes one endpoint, and writes the result back while hardware clears a different endpoint in the meantime, the write can accidentally re-enable that other endpoint. More generally, a write that is intended to preserve one subset of endpoint states while updating another subset instead replaces every endpoint's enable state.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered in the USBDEV OUT reception path when multiple OUT endpoints are enabled, `set_nak_out` is in use, and firmware re-enables or disables one endpoint while another endpoint may be cleared by hardware. It is also exposed by software writes that are intended to preserve one subset of OUT endpoint enables while updating a different subset in a single `rxenable_out` access.

title: [prim/rtl] Synthesizable `countones` function
body:
Two commits:

1. Remove `countones` logic from DAI. The count value is released unconditionally.
2. Use `prim_sum_tree` for the calculation of `countones`.

Addresses #28017.

repo.name: opentitan
repo.description: OpenTitan: Open source silicon root of trust

commits.message:
[otp_ctrl/rtl] Unconditionally release countones after zeroization

In the absence of an error, the `ZEROIZE` command should always
release the `countones` value of the zeroized word to software.

Signed-off-by: Andrea Caforio <andrea.caforio@lowrisc.org>

[otp_ctrl/rtl] Use prim_sum_tree as $countones primitive

The SystemVerilog function `$countones` is not supported by all
tools. Emulate it using the `prim_sum_tree` primitive.

Signed-off-by: Andrea Caforio <andrea.caforio@lowrisc.org>

resolved_issues.title: [otp_ctrl] Move `countones` function from `otp_ctrl_top_specific_pkg.sv.tpl` to `prim_util_pkg`
