prepare_script:
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

cd /home/opentitan
git reset --hard
git clean -fdx
git checkout 073b849f6d62f7c2f04839dff3cac419d843217f
git submodule update --init --recursive

export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
if [[ -f apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
  cp apt-requirements.txt /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  sed -i -e '/^$/d' -e '/^#/d' -e 's/#.*//' /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
  if [[ -s /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
    apt-get update
    xargs -r apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends < /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
  fi
  rm -f /tmp/opentitan-apt-requirements.txt
fi

python -m pip install -U pip "setuptools<66.0.0"
python -m pip install -r python-requirements.txt --no-warn-script-location

toolchain_version=""
if [[ -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
  toolchain_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
fi
if [[ -n "${toolchain_version}" ]]; then
  python util/get-toolchain.py --update -r "${toolchain_version}"
else
  python util/get-toolchain.py --update
fi

verible_version=""
if [[ -f hw/tool_requirements.py ]]; then
  verible_version="$(python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
ns = {}
exec(Path('hw/tool_requirements.py').read_text(encoding='utf-8'), ns)
reqs = ns.get('__TOOL_REQUIREMENTS__', {})
entry = reqs.get('verible', '')
if isinstance(entry, dict):
    print(entry.get('min_version', ''))
elif isinstance(entry, str):
    print(entry)
PY
)"
fi
if [[ -z "${verible_version}" && -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
  verible_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG VERIBLE_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
fi
if [[ -n "${verible_version}" ]]; then
  rm -rf /tools/verible
  mkdir -p /tools/verible
  curl -f -Ls -o /tmp/verible.tar.gz \
    "https://github.com/chipsalliance/verible/releases/download/${verible_version}/verible-${verible_version}-linux-static-x86_64.tar.gz"
  tar -C /tools/verible -xf /tmp/verible.tar.gz --strip-components=1
  rm -f /tmp/verible.tar.gz
fi

cat > /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh <<'PATHEOF'
for d in /tools/riscv/bin /tools/verible/bin; do
  [ -d "$d" ] && export PATH="$d:$PATH"
done
PATHEOF

if ! grep -q '/etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh' /etc/opentitan_bash_env; then
  echo 'source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh' >> /etc/opentitan_bash_env
fi
source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh

python -m pip show edalize fusesoc hjson urllib3 >/dev/null
riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc --version | head -n1
verible-verilog-lint --version | head -n1
problem_statement:
## Description
OpenTitan's OTP (One-Time Programmable) Controller exposes a Direct Access Interface (DAI) `ZEROIZE` command that lets firmware erase words in zeroizable partitions. When the target word belongs to a secret partition, firmware cannot inspect the returned raw word directly because secret-partition contents are scrambled, so the controller is supposed to return the number of set bits observed in the zeroized word through the DAI read-data path. Firmware uses that count to decide whether the word was zeroized successfully enough or whether the operation must be retried.

## Affected Function
The affected functionality is the OTP controller's DAI `ZEROIZE` path for zeroizable secret partitions, specifically the logic that publishes the post-zeroization set-bit count back to software.

## Expected Behavior
If a `ZEROIZE` command on a zeroizable secret-partition word completes with no OTP macro error, the controller must always return the observed set-bit count for that word to software through the DAI read-data path. This must remain true even when the count is below the macro-specific threshold used to decide whether a partition should be considered sufficiently zeroized. That threshold is only for judging the zeroization result, not for deciding whether software can see the count.

## Actual Behavior
The DAI can suppress the returned set-bit count for a secret-partition `ZEROIZE` operation even when the OTP macro reports success. When the observed count is below the zeroization-valid threshold, software does not receive the count value that it needs to evaluate a partial zeroization result and decide whether to retry or escalate.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered when firmware issues `ZEROIZE` through the OTP controller DAI to a zeroizable secret partition, the OTP macro completes the command with `NoError`, and the returned zeroization word contains fewer set bits than the zeroization-valid threshold, for example one count below that bound.
